entries.name: MAPSENSE_TeleportCandidateLevelPolicyWitness
entries.notes: Unique 31-byte witness in the common canonical image: context at Game+0x106, CALL 0x554C7D -> 0x32C4A0, then Levels record byte +0x0E. Zero refuses; value two calls 0x350A20 with mask 0x804 before relocation through CALL 0x554CCE -> 0x491CA0. This is a coordinate trace with adjusted endpoints, not a destination-only collision mask. Entry 0x554C40 closely matches D2MOO SKILLS_SrvDo027_Teleport, but its initialized callback-table slot 27 is still unproven. No complete handler ABI, runtime cast or hook is qualified. D2MOO 19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 SkillSor.cpp:874-898 supplies semantic corroboration only.

entries.name: MAPSENSE_LocationCommandRange50Witness
entries.notes: Unique 28-byte argument/call/result witness passes 50 as fourth argument to coordinate validator 0x4FE1F0. The validator compares abs(targetX-unitX) and abs(targetY-unitY) independently and rejects only values greater than the bound, witnessed at 0x4FE255 and 0x4FE28E. Calls 0x4AD1A7 and 0x4AD297 also target this validator. This proves a per-axis inclusive command bound, not player viewport reach, mana, skill availability, packet opcode ownership or successful Teleport execution.

entries.name: MAPSENSE_GatedCoordinateTraceEndpointWitness
entries.notes: Unique 46-byte coordinate-adjustment witness in 0x351720. The wrapper 0x350A20 supplies source coordinates, target coordinates, cached source size, fixed target size two, room and mask; CALL 0x350B10 -> 0x351720. Sizes clamp to two, Manhattan distance below the size sum returns clear, otherwise endpoints move inward along the dominant axis or both equal axes before CALL 0x3517E6 -> 0x363F20. The chain is used by the Teleport candidate's Levels.Teleport=2 branch with 0x804. Exact raster traversal, ties, room-border behavior and initialized skill dispatch remain unqualified. D2MOO Units.cpp:2768-2860 corroborates the trace semantics only.

entries.name: MAPSENSE_RelocationPlayerSizeAndMaskWitness
entries.notes: Unique 37-byte relocation witness calls cached unit-size accessor 0x34B580, passes that size in R8D and collision mask 0x1C09 in R9D to 0x362F90. Earlier null destination-room handling calls 0x38DFB0 first with null then with the unit's current room. The free-position chain 0x362FBF -> 0x364E90, 0x364F69 -> 0x364D50, 0x364DE0 -> 0x366920 reaches the size-two cross check. It may adjust the requested landing; exact search order, complete ABI and dynamic occupancy remain gates.

entries.name: MAPSENSE_PlayerSizeTwoDispatchWitness
entries.notes: Unique 46-byte unit-type dispatch witness in 0x3481E0. Unit type zero indexes the first DWORD at 0x34829C, which resolves to 0x34822A and returns EAX=2. Cached accessor 0x34B580 calls 0x3481E0 at 0x34B5B9 and 0x34B5F8. The size is a pattern selector, not a two-subtile radius. This corroborates native player placement only; complete walking path footprint and transformed-player behavior are not qualified.

entries.name: MAPSENSE_CollisionSizeTwoPatternWitness
entries.notes: Unique 20-byte size-two branch witness calls 0x366920 from 0x364DE0. The dispatcher at 0x364D89 selects this branch for size two; sizes zero/one use a point and size three a different pattern. Unique slow-path witnesses 0x366C4C, 0x366C76 and 0x366CA3 test centre plus four cardinal neighbours and OR their masked collisions. This disproves a single-cell placement model for a player; it does not qualify every fast-path or border behavior for runtime use.

entries.name: MAPSENSE_RoomCoordinateListLookupWitness
entries.notes: Unique 33-byte loop witness in null-safe coordinate lookup 0x38DFB0. The caller first tests the supplied room, then obtains its room vector/count through CALL 0x38DFFA -> governed DUNGEON_GetRoomListAndCount at 0x2EFDE0 and tests entries using 0x2F0680. Bounds use ActiveRoom+0x80/+0x84 and +0x88/+0x8C, minimum inclusive, maximum exclusive. This adds a relocation consumer for the existing room-list accessor; list construction, exact membership and equivalence to generated near-room links remain unproven.

entries.name: DRLGOUTDESR_TemplateSelectorTablesWitness
entries.notes: Unique 22-byte witness 48980FB6840248C33F008B8C8228C33F004803CAFFE1 in the common canonical image. After the unsigned LevelId-41 <= 93 guard, CDQE indexes 94 bytes at RVA 0x3FC348, then eight DWORD RVA targets at 0x3FC328. IDs 41..46 select entries 0..5, ID 134 selects 6 and IDs 47..133 select default 7. Far Oasis 43 selects 2 -> 0x3FC095; default targets 0x3FC2EF. Widening only the outer bound for ID 147 indexes beyond the original selector table. Exact tables and instructions are checked by the audit script. This is a static selection witness, not a qualified hook or a claim about active D2RLoader modifications.

entries.name: DRLGOUTDESR_ExitPresetLevelIdentityWitness
entries.notes: Unique 37-byte witness 448B82F80100004183E82974304183E801742A4183E801741C4183E801740E4183F801753D. The Far Oasis branch passes its unchanged Level pointer through the unique call context at 0x3FC0AD, CALL 0x3FC0B4 -> 0x3FCA60. The callee rereads Level+0x1F8 and accepts only 41..45; 43 selects preset 0x186 at 0x3FCA99. ID 147 follows the invalid-ID path 0x3FCAC6 -> diagnostic call 0x3FCAD0 -> 0x3FBCE0, with conditional INT3 at 0x3FCAD9. Redirecting only the outer selector while preserving ID 147 therefore leaves a second identity dependency. No observed crash, complete helper ABI or hook safety is claimed. D2MOO 19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 source/D2Common/src/Drlg/DrlgOutDesr.cpp:224-260 corroborates exit-placement semantics only.

entries.name: DRLGOUTDESR_LevelIdDispatchRangeWitness
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness 8B87F801000083C0D783F85D0F87BD050000 in the common canonical image. The Act II outdoor branch calls entry 0x3FBD10 from 0x3EE4CD with context in CL and Level in RDX. After two generic setup calls this witness loads Level+0x1F8, subtracts 41, compares unsigned to 93 and branches to epilogue 0x3FC30F (return 0x3FC325). Level 147 therefore skips the desert-specific construction in unmodified D2R even with correct Act resolution. Generic setup still runs; no crash or empty-map claim is made. PDATA/Ghidra fragments are not reliable logical function bounds here. This is read-only evidence, not a qualified hook or a claim about an active loader's modifications. D2MOO 19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 source/D2Common/src/Drlg/DrlgOutDesr.cpp:46-120 is semantic corroboration only.

entries.name: INVENTORY_AutoSortPlanner
entries.notes: Native client AutoSort planner with observed Windows x64 ABI (targetPositions, currentPositions, itemGuids, itemCount, player, inventoryPage) -> bool. Both position arrays contain one uint32 per item with uint16 x at +0 and uint16 y at +2. It validates the complete source layout before returning a target layout. AutoSort owns this entry through one fail-closed inline hook, calls the original first, and overwrites only the complete target array after its pure planner succeeds. The entry and semantics are shared by the governed common corpus for D2R 3.2.92777 and 3.3.93847.

entries.name: INVENTORY_AutoSort
entries.notes: Native client AutoSort wrapper with observed ABI (playerUnitId, inventoryPage) -> void. It resolves the local player, enumerates at most 256 items from exactly the requested inventory page, calls INVENTORY_AutoSortPlanner at 0x15E790, compares current and target coordinates, executes the native client-side update path, then sends the authoritative packet through 0xECC70. AutoSort calls this unchanged wrapper for its Controls action so controller and keyboard input retain one native execution route.

entries.name: INVENTORY_AutoSort_PlannerCall
entries.notes: Unique direct CALL from INVENTORY_AutoSort to INVENTORY_AutoSortPlanner. The surrounding argument setup proves RCX target positions, RDX current positions, R8 item GUIDs, R9 item count, stack argument 5 player and stack argument 6 page. AutoSort fingerprints the full surrounding witness but does not patch this callsite.

entries.name: CLIENT_SendAutoSortPacket
entries.notes: Native AutoSort packet sender. It emits opcode 0x4E, page, player GUID, itemCount-1 and one five-byte record per item: packed nibble coordinate (y << 4) | x followed by uint32 item GUID. Packet length is 7 + 5*N and is queued through CLIENT_QueueOutgoingPacket. AutoSort fingerprints but never hooks or calls this function directly.

entries.name: SERVER_AutoSortCallback
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback for packet opcode 0x4E. It validates packet bounds, player identity, exact item count for the target inventory page, dimensions, coordinates, occupancy and every conflict before mutating the inventory and sending updates. This proves AutoSort is an all-or-nothing same-container transaction rather than a sequence of client coordinate writes. AutoSort fingerprints but never hooks this entry.

entries.name: CLIENT_IsOnlineState
entries.notes: Returns whether the current client state byte at context+0x5C equals 1. INVENTORY_AutoSortPlanner negates this result as the third argument to UNITS_GetInventoryGrid. AutoSort reproduces that exact grid selection call and fingerprints this entry before installing its planner hook.

entries.name: SKILLITEM_HandleItemEffectSkill
entries.notes: Authoritative server item-effect helper with observed ABI (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel, target, x, y, unitTypeOut, unitGuidOut, xOut, yOut, flag) -> int32. It resolves the context SkillsTxt record and refuses a zero ItemEffect word at record+0x20A before entering native target selection and the central skill handler. It saves the current target unit and first-point coordinates, temporarily installs the passed unit or position, applies SkillsTxt ItemTarget semantics, executes the central handler, then restores the saved descriptor. Its entry and semantics are byte-identical in the governed common corpus for 92777 and 93847. ArmageddonCtCFix owns this entry only for a thread-local item cast of configured skill IDs 249 and 250; Cast Triggers uses the control flow as proof but does not hook or call the helper directly.

entries.name: SKILLS_SrvDo124_Armageddon_Hurricane
entries.notes: Shared authoritative start callback for Armageddon and Hurricane with ABI (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel) -> int32. It requires UNITS_GetUsedSkill to identify the requested skill, creates or refreshes the aura state and active event, then stores a random periodic seed at D2Skill+0x24. A native chance-to-cast call has no matching used skill, which is the second proven failure gate after ItemEffect.

entries.name: SKILLS_SrvDo146_ArmageddonActive
entries.notes: Armageddon active-state callback with ABI (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel) -> int32. After validating the state it resolves the highest matching skill through 0x33DD40, consumes the seed at D2Skill+0x24, updates that seed and schedules the next active event. ArmageddonCtCFix temporarily links a stack-local surrogate only when its own synthetic CtC start retained a seed for the exact unit identity. Version 0.1.1 borrows the separately fingerprinted STATES_CheckState predicate at 0x3351B0 before this callback and after a zero return so natural expiration erases the retained seed without treating every native zero return as expiration.

entries.name: SKILLS_SrvDo145_HurricaneActive
entries.notes: Hurricane active-state callback with ABI (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel) -> int32. Unlike Armageddon's active callback it does not resolve or retain a D2Skill node after SrvDo124 has successfully established the state and event. ArmageddonCtCFix therefore does not hook this entry.

entries.name: SKILLS_GetHighestLevelSkillFromUnitAndId
entries.notes: Resolves the highest eligible D2Skill for a unit and skill ID with observed ABI (unit, skillId, selectionFlag) -> D2Skill*. The false-selection path scans SkillList+0x00, identifies each node through its SkillsTxt pointer at +0x00 and filters the node flag at +0x54. Armageddon's active callback calls it with selectionFlag false.

entries.name: TreasureClassEx_CompileTxtCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte CALL rel32 E8 C9 73 F5 FF to DATATBLS_CompileTxt 0x2FF970 inside the TreasureClassEx compiler loop for build 92777. The official eezstreet D2RL-Plugins feature items.playerConditionCalc extends the TXT descriptor at this site; it is separate from ISC12 G0-BBE's native stat() ordinal-width proof. Three isolated Loader 1.1.0-beta runs prove D2RCore changes the call before the first plugin loads, including with item_stat_ranges/maximum_sockets disabled and plugin-items ordered first; the exact v2 plugin therefore refuses fail-closed before applying any item operation. Treat this range as loader-owned under 1.1 and do not overwrite or dynamically chain it without an explicit compiler-extension contract.

entries.name: CLIENT_ItemUseTargetingDispatcher
entries.notes: Receives the used item in RCX, resolves its ItemsTxt record, reads pSpell at +0x94, collects item parameters and calls 0x1B9720 before returning 1. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777. MassID 0.1.7 hooks it before the targeted action is built; confidence remains medium until the gameplay witness confirms capture and cursor suppression.

entries.name: CLIENT_GetLocalDataContext
entries.notes: Returns the local client data-table context. SKILLTREE_CanAllocateSkill calls it first and passes the result to CLIENT_GetLocalPlayer. It was used by the superseded mono-rank BulkSkillPointAllocation queue and is not required by 1.2.1.

entries.name: CLIENT_GetLocalPlayer
entries.notes: Returns the local player for a client data context. The 92777 skill-tree eligibility path calls it at 0x14C3DB6. It was used by the superseded mono-rank BulkSkillPointAllocation queue and is not required by 1.2.1.

entries.name: PATH_GetRoom
entries.notes: Returns the ActiveRoom pointer stored at dynamic-path offset +0x20. UNITS_GetRoom tail-jumps here for player units; MapSense 0.9.3 validates this five-byte body as part of the current-level witness chain. The signature 48 8B 41 20 C3 is unique in the governed 92777 corpus reused for target 3.3.93847.

entries.name: UNITS_GetObjectInteractType
entries.notes: Null-safe object accessor with ABI (Unit*) -> uint8. Its strict unique 72-byte body requires Unit type 2, loads ObjectData* from Unit+0x10, then returns the byte at ObjectData+0x08. Its 28 direct readers include only three client paths: 0x9A39E tests the sign bit for object-lock behavior, 0x1CB118 feeds the shrine-record resolver, and 0xC1882 alone feeds DATATBLS_GetLevelsTxtRecord at client UI callsite 0xC188E. Native chest consumers split this byte into lock bit 0x80 and trap type bits 0..6; MapSense fingerprints both the entry and the complete valid layout path before consuming it. The body is byte-identical in the governed common corpus for targets 92777 and 93847.

entries.name: OBJECTS_IsShrine
entries.notes: Predicate with ABI (Unit*) -> int32. Its strict unique 30-byte body requires Unit type 2, follows Unit+0x10 to ObjectData and its active compiled ObjectsTxt record, then tests SubClass bit 0x01 at record+0x127. This is the generic runtime shrine classifier and does not depend on a vanilla or BKVince object-ID allowlist.

entries.name: UNITS_SetObjectInteractType
entries.notes: Setter with observed ABI (Unit*, uint8 interactType) -> void. Its unique strict normal body requires Unit type 2, follows Unit+0x10 to ObjectData, and writes the byte at ObjectData+0x08. OBJECTS_InitFunction01_Shrine passes its selected nonzero ShrinesTxt row index here; OBJECTS_InitFunction16_Well instead tail-calls it with twice the low byte of compiled ObjectsTxt Parm2.

entries.name: UNITS_SetShrineTxtRecordInObjectData
entries.notes: Setter with observed ABI (Unit*, ShrinesTxt*) -> void. Its unique strict normal body requires Unit type 2, follows Unit+0x10 to ObjectData, and stores the record pointer at ObjectData+0x10. The shrine initializer tail-jumps here only after resolving the same row index already written to ObjectData.InteractType.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetShrinesTxtRecordCount
entries.notes: Accessor with observed ABI (uint8 dataContext) -> int32. Its unique 32-byte entry witness selects the active data tables and reads the ShrinesTxt compiled-record count at DataTables+0x19B8, rejecting a value that cannot be represented by the returned 32-bit count. The shrine selection loop subtracts one before its bounded roll and adds one afterward, so row zero is not selected.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetShrinesTxtRecord
entries.notes: Bounds-checked accessor with observed ABI (uint8 dataContext, int32 shrineRow) -> ShrinesTxt*. Its unique 32-byte entry witness checks the row against DataTables+0x19B8, resolves the base at +0x19B0 and uses a compiled stride of 0x1C. OBJECTS_InitFunction01_Shrine resolves this exact row before storing the record pointer in ObjectData.

entries.name: OBJECTS_InitFunction01_Shrine
entries.notes: Object initializer with observed ABI (ObjectInitContext*) -> void. Its unique entry and interior witnesses read compiled ObjectsTxt Parm0 at +0x134, select a valid ShrinesTxt row, apply the native 4->2, 5->3 and 16->18 remaps, write that row to ObjectData.InteractType through 0x34E9D0, resolve the same row through 0x38FE40 and tail-jump to 0x34EE70 to store the record pointer. The true function entry is 0x50E450; 0x50E510 is only its random-selection loop.

entries.name: OBJECTS_InitFunction01_ShrineSelectionLoop
entries.notes: Unique interior witness inside OBJECTS_InitFunction01_Shrine, not a function entry. It reads the active ShrinesTxt count, rolls a row in the inclusive domain 1..count-1, resolves the row with stride 0x1C, compares current LevelId against ShrinesTxt+0x18 LevelMin, and retries at most eight times. This proves ObjectData.InteractType is the exact nonzero ShrinesTxt row index for objects initialized by InitFn 1.

entries.name: OBJECTS_InitFunction16_Well
entries.notes: Compact 22-byte object initializer with observed ABI (ObjectInitContext*) -> void. Its complete unique body loads compiled ObjectsTxt Parm2 at record+0x13C, doubles its low byte and tail-jumps to UNITS_SetObjectInteractType; it never resolves or stores a ShrinesTxt record. In the active BKVince TXT, ordinary Fountain/Well rows use InitFn 16 and do not carry SubClass bit 0, while shrine-semantic HealingWell and ManaWell rows intentionally use InitFn 1 plus SubClass bit 0.

entries.name: UNITS_GetSuperUniqueIndex
entries.notes: Null-safe accessor with ABI (Unit*) -> int32. Its complete strict unique 92-byte body validates Unit type 1 twice, loads MonsterData* from Unit+0x10, returns the uint16 SuperUniques row index at MonsterData+0x2A, and returns -1 on null, wrong type or missing data. MapSense fingerprints all 92 bytes so the second type gate and full success/failure paths are covered before resolving the index against the active mod SuperUniques table and localization.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetObjectsTxtRecordCount
entries.notes: Accessor with ABI (uint8 dataContext) -> int32. Its strict unique 20-byte body selects the active data tables and returns the ObjectsTxt compiled-record count at DataTables+0x1530. It is the runtime bound for fail-closed classification of active-mod object rows.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetObjectsTxtRecord
entries.notes: Bounds-checked accessor with ABI (uint8 dataContext, int32 classId) -> ObjectsTxt*. It checks classId against the count at DataTables+0x1530, uses the base pointer at +0x1528 and a compiled stride of 0x168, and returns null out of range. Runtime dispatchers prove InitFn at record+0x15C and OperateFn at +0x15E; binary-to-TXT correlation proves SubClass +0x127 and Lockable +0x12F.

entries.name: UNITS_GetObjectRuntimeFlagsC8
entries.notes: Null-safe raw-byte accessor with ABI (Unit*) -> uint8. Its strict unique 59-byte body returns Unit+0xC8. A native chest operation calls it and tests bit 0x01, while client snapshot replication copies the same byte into Unit+0xC8. Only after independent chest classification may MapSense interpret bit 0 as the sparkly/super-chest marker; all other object types and bits remain opaque and fail closed.

entries.name: ACTIVEROOM_GetDrlgRoom
entries.notes: Leaf accessor with ABI (ActiveRoom*) -> DrlgRoom*. Its complete body returns ActiveRoom+0x18 and is followed by an aligned trap padding run. MapSense calls it in Navigation and fingerprints the same strict 16-byte body-plus-padding witness in both the monster-marker and POI current-level chains before either path directly consumes ActiveRoom+0x18. The witness is unique in the governed common corpus for targets 92777 and 93847.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_GetLevelId
entries.notes: Returns the levelId through DrlgRoom+0x90 (Level*) and Level+0x1F8. MapSense 0.9.3 uses the same proven field chain after UNITS_GetRoom and ActiveRoom+0x18 to invalidate stale navigation immediately on a level transition. Its complete 14-byte body is unique in the governed 92777 corpus shared with target 3.3.93847.

entries.name: DRLGWARP_ResolveRoomTileLink
entries.notes: ABI (uint8 dataContext, DrlgRoom* sourceRoom, int32 sourcePresetId, int32* outReciprocalPresetId, LvlWarpTxt** outReciprocalLvlWarpTxt) -> ActiveRoom*. Initializes the source room, matches sourcePresetId against RoomTile+0x20 (LvlWarpTxt*) +0x2C in the source RoomTile chain at +0x78, follows RoomTile+0x00 to the destination DrlgRoom, validates the reciprocal RoomTile, writes the reciprocal LvlWarp identifier and record pointer, initializes the destination room when needed, and returns its ActiveRoom; unresolved reciprocal links return null. The wrapper at 0x361070 converts the returned ActiveRoom through +0x18, DrlgRoom+0x90 and Level+0x1F8 into the destination LevelId. MapSense 0.9.4 called this resolver on the UI thread. Live 0.9.9 diagnostics proved that its reciprocal requirement rejects valid lazy source-side links in Tamoe Highland, Barracks, and Jail Level 1. MapSense 0.10.0 therefore materializes each source room and reads the already-valid destination DrlgRoom directly from RoomTile+0x00; the independent 15-byte witness at 0x3DA9FB proves RoomTile+0x00, destination DrlgRoom+0x78, and reciprocal RoomTile+0x00. The 27-byte entry signature 48 89 5C 24 08 48 89 74 24 10 48 89 7C 24 18 41 56 48 83 EC 20 4D 8B F1 41 8B F8 is unique in the governed common corpus.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_FindWaypointRoomAndCoordinates
entries.notes: ABI (uint8 dataContext, Level* level, int32* outTileX, int32* outTileY) -> DrlgRoom*. Iterates Level+0x10 rooms, selects a room whose +0x50 flags intersect 0x30000, initializes it, then scans PresetUnit type 2 objects whose ObjectsTxt SubClass byte at +0x127 carries 0x40. On an exact waypoint match it writes room tile coordinates plus preset-relative coordinates divided by five; native callers initialize both outputs to -1 and fall back to the room center if either remains unset. MapSense 0.9.4 accepts only an exact non-null result with valid outputs, converts game tiles to world subtiles, and publishes no room-center or first-preset fallback. The 18-byte entry signature 48 89 6C 24 18 57 41 56 41 57 48 83 EC 20 48 8B 7A 10 is unique in the governed common corpus.

entries.name: DRLG_GetLevel
entries.notes: Resolves a Level with ABI (uint8 dataContext, Drlg*, int32 levelId) -> Level*. It traverses Drlg+0x868 through Level+0x1B8 and compares Level+0x1F8, but allocates and links a new Level when the target is absent. Native consumers pair it with DRLG_InitLevel when Level+0x10 is null. Since MapSense 0.9.9, Reveal owns the fingerprinted helper used by Navigation to resolve levels inside the captured client DRLG. MapSense 0.10.0 initializes only the explicit progression target and configured custom targets present in the current Level's eight Vis slots before source RoomTile enumeration; unavailable targets remain pending and never produce guessed lines.

entries.name: DRLG_InitLevel
entries.notes: Initializes the room chain of a Level with ABI (uint8 dataContext, Level*) -> void. A native consumer at 0x3DD5E3 first checks Level+0x10. Since MapSense 0.9.9, Reveal owns the strictly fingerprinted call and invokes it only when Level+0x10 is null. MapSense 0.10.0 reuses that governed helper for the explicit progression target and configured custom targets present in the current Level's eight Vis slots before reading source RoomTile links.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_GetPresetUnits
entries.notes: Returns DrlgRoom+0x98 after checking room flag bits 18 and 26, and may set bit 26. MapSense avoids this mutation and reads +0x98 directly after proving that the current active Level already owns the room chain. The complete strict signature through the trailing return is unique.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_RebuildNearRoomVector
entries.notes: ABI (DrlgRoom*) -> void. Clears the vector size at DrlgRoom+0x18, iterates the owning Level+0x10 room chain through DrlgRoom+0x48, compares rectangle fields +0x60/+0x64/+0x68/+0x6C, appends qualifying room pointers through the vector at +0x10/+0x18/+0x20 and sorts them. MapSense 0.9.5 does not invoke this mutating routine because later DRLG linkage can add cross-level neighbours; it uses three strict interior witnesses from this function to prove the existing near-room vector layout before passively enumerating outdoor inter-level boundaries.

entries.name: CLIENT_GetUnitByIdAndType
entries.notes: Resolves a client unit with ABI (unitId in ECX, unitType in EDX) -> Unit*. Packet handler 0x60 calls it with GUID packet+3 and unit type 2 before updating the portal object; the native caller at 0x198D66 independently loads a packet type byte and unit id. Its entry proves the client hash-table base at 0x2A23910, 128 buckets per unit type through mask 0x7F, and a 0x400-byte type stride. Its strict 33-byte entry signature is unique in the common corpus and differs from the adjacent server-unit lookup at 0x9A5A0 by its backing table and tail displacement. A client portal sidecar can use this resolver only for immediate class/GUID/low-byte revalidation and must never retain the returned Unit pointer. Floating Damage 1.2.8 and MapSense 0.12.0 already obey the same no-retained-pointer constraint.

entries.name: SERVER_GetUnitByIdAndType
entries.notes: Resolves a server unit with ABI (unitId in ECX, unitType in EDX) -> Unit*. Its unique strict 28-byte entry signature resolves the server Unit hash-table base at 0x2A25110, applies the same 128-bucket mask and 0x400-byte type stride as the adjacent client resolver, then tail-jumps to CLIENT_FindUnitInTypeBucket. The native missile consumer at 0x3B7D0E selects this resolver for unit type 3 when UNITS_IsServerUnit@0x34F8D0 is true and otherwise selects CLIENT_GetUnitByIdAndType. MapSense fingerprints this relationship before any bounded read-only server missile traversal.

entries.name: CLIENT_FindUnitInTypeBucket
entries.notes: Client hash-chain lookup witness. It loads one bucket head, compares Unit+0x08 to the requested id and Unit+0x00 to the requested type, and advances through Unit+0x158 until a match or null. MapSense 0.12.0 fingerprints the complete 41-byte helper and uses only the proven +0x158 next-link layout for bounded read-only traversal of the monster table.

entries.name: CLIENT_UnitHashTable
entries.notes: Base of the client Unit hash table. Each unit type owns 128 pointer buckets (0x400 bytes), so monster type 1 begins at +0x400 and missile type 3 begins at +0xC00. MapSense 0.12.0 reads the monster buckets while the local-player automap pass is active; its dual-source missile collector reads the client type-3 buckets first and gives those value copies priority over matching server identities. Both paths follow the separately witnessed Unit+0x158 link, enforce per-bucket and total traversal caps and retain no native Unit pointer.

entries.name: SERVER_UnitHashTable
entries.notes: Base of the server Unit hash table, exactly 0x1800 bytes after CLIENT_UnitHashTable: six client unit-type arrays of 128 pointers each precede it. SERVER_GetUnitByIdAndType proves the base, mask 0x7F and 0x400-byte type stride, placing server missiles at +0xC00 (D2R+0x2A25D10). A read-only runtime witness in Act IV observed zero client missiles and 11 then 15 valid server type-3 units with valid ids, classes and dynamic paths. MapSense scans this table only after its strict resolver fingerprint passes, deduplicates by unit id with class consistency, prefers client copies and retains no native pointer.

entries.name: UNITS_MissileTypeAndDataWitness
entries.notes: Unique strict 32-byte witness 40 53 83 39 03 4D 8B D0 48 8B D9 0F 85 59 01 00 00 4C 8B 49 18 48 8D 05 30 EC 91 01 48 89 7C 24. It requires Unit+0x00 to equal 3 before entering its missile-data path and reading the type-specific pointer at Unit+0x18. Combined with CLIENT_GetUnitByIdAndType and CLIENT_FindUnitInTypeBucket, it proves that client hash-table unit type 3 is the missile family used by MapSense's read-only collector; broader semantics of the function remain unnamed.

entries.name: DRLG_GetHoradricStaffTombLevelId
entries.notes: Returns Drlg+0x120 or zero for a null DRLG with observed ABI (Drlg*) -> int32. D2MOO supplies semantic provenance for nStaffTombLevel only; the x64 RVA, entry bytes and layout witness come from the governed common D2R corpus. MapSense 0.12.0 accepts only Tal Rasha tomb level ids 66 through 72 and resolves that exact RoomTile exit in the Canyon of the Magi.

entries.name: QUESTRECORD_GetQuestState
entries.notes: Reads one synchronized quest-record bit with observed x64 ABI (questRecord, questIndex, stateIndex) -> bool. D2MOO supplies the semantic bit formula and identifies QUESTSTATEFLAG_A2Q6 as 14 and QFLAG_REWARDGRANTED as 0; no 32-bit address or ABI is transplanted. MapSense 0.12.0 calls the strictly fingerprinted x64 function only for a non-null current-difficulty client record.

entries.name: CLIENT_CurrentDifficultyQuestRecord
entries.notes: Pointer to the synchronized client quest record for the current difficulty. The unique witness at 0x114C20 loads this pointer through RIP-relative addressing immediately before QUESTRECORD_GetQuestState. MapSense 0.12.0 fingerprints that full caller witness, rejects a null or unaligned record and reads only Act II quest 6 RewardGranted to choose red quest versus green farming navigation.

entries.name: CLIENT_UpdateCameraOffsets
entries.notes: Updates gameplay camera offsets from the local player. It resolves CLIENT_GetLocalDataContext and CLIENT_GetLocalPlayer, reads the player's client coordinates, subtracts half the native viewport dimensions and applies the optional camera displacement. Its only direct call is 0x93D79 in the main client-frame pass. The strict 33-byte build-92777 entry signature is unique. Floating Damage 1.2.8 invokes the original first, then uses this frame rendezvous to service every active target request with current camera state; gameplay confirmation remains required.

entries.name: RENDER_GetThreadContextRoot
entries.notes: Returns the renderer thread-context root, lazily initialized through TLS. Native unit-label projection callers read the active render context at +0x20 before calling RENDER_ProjectUnitToScreen. The strict 37-byte build-92777 entry signature is unique.

entries.name: RENDER_ProjectUnitToScreen
entries.notes: Projects a Unit into native UI float coordinates with observed ABI (renderContext, Unit*, floatXYOut, useUnitHeight bool) -> bool. Six direct callers establish the same first three arguments; 0x198F75 passes R9B=1, tests AL, converts the two output floats and bounds them with UI_GetNativeWidth/Height. The strict 61-byte build-92777 entry signature is unique. Runtime invalidated calling it from Floating Damage 1.2.5's overlay thread because its render context is TLS-bound. Gameplay then invalidated 1.2.6's passive observation and 1.2.7's conditional-entry rendezvous: moving the camera left only the principal target refreshed. Floating Damage 1.2.8 no longer hooks this entry; it calls the verified function from the native camera-frame rendezvous after CLIENT_UpdateCameraOffsets.

entries.name: CLIENT_SendFiveByteCommandPacket
entries.notes: Builds a five-byte client command from (opcode byte, value word, extra word) and submits it through the outgoing queue at 0xEE2A0. For opcode 0x3B, value is the skill id and extra encodes additional ranks: 0 means one total, 4 means five total, and 0xFFFF means every rank the runtime permits. The 0/0xFFFF client branches are proven at 0x14C6A11/0x14C6A01; extra=4 producing exactly five instant ranks was validated in game on 92777. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 hooks the strict 29-byte prologue and filters only opcode 0x3B.

entries.name: CLIENT_QueueOutgoingPacket
entries.notes: Generic outgoing client packet queue called by the five-byte builder at 0xEC700. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 preserves this native route and sends exactly one native 0x3B request per Ctrl or confirmed Shift action.

entries.name: CLIENT_DispatchItemAction9C
entries.notes: Common client dispatcher for the 8-byte 0x9C item-action envelope. It validates length-8 against the 0xF4 payload ceiling, copies the packet into a bounded local buffer, reads the action selector at +0x01 and dispatches through a 23-entry switch. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777. For historical provenance only, the RuffnecKk ExtendedItemStats prototype consumed EIT1 fragments here and was later exercised in an experimental RuffDood fork build; this hook was never part of upstream eezstreet and is not an ISC12 dependency.

entries.name: CLIENT_DispatchItemAction9D
entries.notes: Common client dispatcher for the 13-byte 0x9D item-action envelope. It rejects packets shorter than 13 bytes, copies the packet into a bounded local buffer, reads the action selector at +0x01 and dispatches through a 26-entry switch. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777. For historical provenance only, the RuffnecKk ExtendedItemStats prototype consumed EIT1 fragments here and was later exercised in an experimental RuffDood fork build; this hook was never part of upstream eezstreet and is not an ISC12 dependency.

entries.name: UI_RenderItemIcon
entries.notes: Central item-icon renderer with proven x64 ABI (item, packedScreenXY, scale, renderParams) -> void; packedScreenXY stores the screen-space top-left x in the low dword and y in the high dword. It has four direct callers, including the inventory loop call at 0x2A776C, and its 19-byte prologue is unique in build 92777. D2RLoader's inline trampoline prevents reliable _ReturnAddress filtering, so CharmZone leaves the native renderer unchanged and accepts only item pointers previously classified as inactive by its native charm-eligibility hook.

entries.name: SKILLS_GetRuntimeMaxLevel
entries.notes: Returns the effective runtime maximum for a compiled SkillsTxt row and data context. SKILLTREE_CanAllocateSkill calls it at 0x14C3E54. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 delegates the cap to the authoritative native bulk handler and no longer calls this helper.

entries.name: UI_VendorPanel_Configure
entries.notes: Configures VendorPanel mode, child enabled/visible states and mode-specific backgrounds with ABI (panel) -> void. It stores gamble mode 2 when CLIENT_GetVendorPanelGambleMode is nonzero and otherwise selects normal-vendor modes 0 or 1 by NPC class. Its strict 32-byte entry is hooked by VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 only after the original flow returns. The hook reuses button_refresh: it preserves the original state and layout position in gamble, then dynamically centers and shows that same native widget outside gamble.

entries.name: UI_TOOLTIP_ResolveHoveredUnit
entries.notes: Resolves the hovered unit from the tooltip panel state at +0x5C4/+0x5C8. The governed panel-update call at 0x2C89A5 returns to 0x2C89AA. ExtendedItemStats 0.3.0 substitutes the exact pinned unit only for the captured panel, allowing a huge tooltip to remain rendered while the pointer manipulates its scrollbar.

entries.name: UI_TOOLTIP_ResolveHoveredWidget
entries.notes: Resolves the active tooltip widget for the panel-update path. The governed call at 0x2C8B70 returns to 0x2C8B75. ExtendedItemStats 0.3.0 substitutes the exact pinned widget only for the captured panel so the native tooltip text persists outside the item hitbox.

entries.name: ITEMS_BuildItemTooltip
entries.notes: Builds the final item-tooltip string with the observed nine-argument x64 ABI used by AdvancedItemTooltips. The 92777 index proves exactly seven direct callers. AdvancedItemTooltips keeps this entry intact and redirects only those seven CALL rel32 sites through private near relays before applying its bounded tooltip transformation.

entries.name: BuildItemTooltipCall_2291DC
entries.notes: One of the seven direct 92777 calls to ITEMS_BuildItemTooltip. AdvancedItemTooltips validates the exact bytes E8 9F 42 09 00 and redirects only this callsite through its private near relay.

entries.name: BuildItemTooltipCall_2BCEE9
entries.notes: One of the seven direct 92777 calls to ITEMS_BuildItemTooltip. AdvancedItemTooltips validates the exact bytes E8 92 05 00 00 and redirects only this callsite through its private near relay.

entries.name: BuildItemTooltipCall_2C8C02
entries.notes: One of the seven direct 92777 calls to ITEMS_BuildItemTooltip. AdvancedItemTooltips validates the exact bytes E8 79 48 FF FF and redirects only this callsite through its private near relay.

entries.name: BuildItemTooltipCall_2CB32E
entries.notes: One of the seven direct 92777 calls to ITEMS_BuildItemTooltip. AdvancedItemTooltips validates the exact bytes E8 4D 21 FF FF and redirects only this callsite through its private near relay.

entries.name: BuildItemTooltipCall_2CE716
entries.notes: One of the seven direct 92777 calls to ITEMS_BuildItemTooltip. AdvancedItemTooltips validates the exact bytes E8 65 ED FE FF and redirects only this callsite through its private near relay.

entries.name: BuildItemTooltipCall_87E882
entries.notes: One of the seven direct 92777 calls to ITEMS_BuildItemTooltip. AdvancedItemTooltips validates the exact bytes E8 F9 EB A3 FF and redirects only this callsite through its private near relay.

entries.name: BuildItemTooltipCall_150C377
entries.notes: One of the seven direct 92777 calls to ITEMS_BuildItemTooltip. AdvancedItemTooltips validates the exact bytes E8 04 11 DB FE and redirects only this callsite through its private near relay.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetRunesTxtRecordFromItem
entries.notes: Validates UNIT_ITEM and resolves the active RunesTxt record for the concrete runeword item with observed ABI (item) -> record pointer. AdvancedItemTooltips validates its strict 32-byte 92777 signature and reads the localized name string id at record+0x46.

entries.name: STRING_EnsureCapacity
entries.notes: Ensures capacity for the native tooltip string object with observed ABI (string, requestedSize) -> void. AdvancedItemTooltips validates its strict 32-byte 92777 signature before using it for bounded final-tooltip growth.

entries.name: ITEMS_BuildQuantityDescription
entries.notes: Native localized quantity-tooltip appender with observed ABI void (item, wideCharacterAppendBuffer), bounded at 0x2C1E50..0x2C1F54. It reads stat 70, calls ITEMS_GetTotalMaxStack and appends ItemStats1i plus the line separator. Four direct callers are 0x2BD82B, 0x2BE124, 0x2BE822 and 0x2BEDF0. The first 32 bytes 48 89 5C 24 20 56 48 81 EC 40 01 00 00 48 8B 05 64 94 70 02 48 33 C4 48 89 84 24 30 01 00 00 45 are unique. This is not the icon-counter renderer. The September 5 Potion Stacking development source now owns an inline hook omitting this appender only for managed potions; the rebuilt DLL has not been deployed or runtime-qualified.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemInternal
entries.notes: Bounded continuous body 0x37FFD0..0x3801C5, called by public bitstream wrapper 0x375EE0 and recursively at 0x380159. Observed ABI int32(item, bitWriter, server, saveSockets, gamble, opaqueOptions); both stack arguments are forwarded by the wrapper and recursion. Entry 32 bytes 40 53 48 83 EC 50 48 89 6C 24 60 48 89 74 24 68 48 8B F2 48 89 7C 24 78 48 8B F9 4C 89 64 24 48 are unique. ItemData flags +0x18 are captured before serialization; compact bit 21 is set when GetCompactSave succeeds but is not cleared when it fails. The serialized flags precede the branch at 0x3800D0 into compact 0x37CA20 or complete 0x37D140. The unique 54-byte witness 0x3800BF covers the format dispatch and argument forwarding. Potion Stacking normalizes managed ordinary compact potions before calling the original, never by patching a partly written bitstream. Native save/reload and synchronization remain unqualified.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetAdvancedStashCounterByte
entries.notes: Complete leaf 0x46D9A0..0x46D9B4 with observed uint8(item) return ABI: null gives AL=0, otherwise Unit+0x10 yields ItemData and MOVZX reads its byte +0x9C. Thirteen direct callers; first non-null path has unique 12-byte witness 48 8B 41 10 0F B6 80 9C 00 00 00 C3 at 0x46D9A8. This vanilla byte getter is not the effective Loader counter or cap. The live Loader replaces selected callers (including 0x2CE509) with private D2RCore full-DWORD readers, without changing this leaf. The module-specific evidence is recorded separately in findings.md; do not truncate the Loader's counter through this getter.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetCompactSave
entries.notes: Observed ABI int32 (item). The complete body 0x377E30..0x377EA2 resolves the concrete compiled Items row and returns its compactsave byte at +0x153. The first 32 bytes 48 89 5C 24 08 57 48 83 EC 20 41 B8 54 15 00 00 48 8D 15 49 C5 98 01 48 8B F9 E8 11 1A FD FF 48 are unique. Outer serializer 0x37FFD0 calls it at 0x380061 and ORs compact bit 21 into the flags when true; false does not clear an existing compact flag. The later bit test at 0x3800D0 chooses compact 0x37CA20 versus complete 0x37D140. No compact-to-complete migration is qualified by this identification.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetStatsDescription
entries.notes: Builds the item-stat description buffer used by the tooltip. QtyDisplayIssue hooks its unique strict 32-byte prologue, calls vanilla first, then appends a bounded quantity line only for socketed stackable items. Four direct call sites and the item-type branch were verified in the persistent 92777 workbench.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetUnitBaseStat
entries.notes: Generic unit base-stat getter with ABI (unit, stat id, 16-bit layer). DurabilityResistance hooks its max-durability calls; SKILLTREE_CanAllocateSkill calls it with stat 5 and layer 0 for unspent skill points. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.0.7 used it for its superseded per-rank acknowledgement queue; 1.2.1 no longer reads it.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetUnitStat
entries.notes: Reads a unit stat with ABI (unit, statId, layer). ITEMS_AddSockets calls it with stat 0xC2 to preserve an existing socket count on set and unique items. ForceLarzukSockets uses the same getter only to refuse overwriting an already-socketed item. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints its unique 32-byte entry, reads burningmin 316, burningmax 317 and passive_fire_mastery 329 for generic production, and observes unit_dooverlay 178 before native last-write-wins visual arbitration.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetDifficultyRecord
entries.notes: Returns the native difficulty record with observed Windows x64 ABI (dataSet, difficulty) -> pointer. The unique 38-byte witness at 0x44DF40 proves the call order and the source bytes at Game+0x106 and Game+0x104. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints the resolver's unique 32-byte entry before constructing its synthetic Fire-resolution context.

entries.name: STATLIST_UnitGetStatValue
entries.notes: Unit-level (unit, statId, layer) wrapper with 91 direct callers. It packs the key as (statId << 16) | layer, resolves ItemStatCost, then calls the full-stat lookup at 0x2F9B10. EnhancedDamageMinMaxFix 1.0.0 hooked this wrapper unsuccessfully.

entries.name: STATLIST_SetUnitStat
entries.notes: Sets a unit stat with ABI (unit, statId, value, layer). The proven tail of ITEMS_AddSockets calls it with stat 0xC2 after setting IFLAG_SOCKETED. ForceLarzukSockets reuses this exact native setter only in the guarded Larzuk path after enforcing the physical and base/type/ilvl limits.

entries.name: STATLIST_EvaluateStatOperations
entries.notes: Recursive ItemStatCost operation evaluator. Its 14-entry switch maps operation 13 to 0x2F9709, where an item-owned stat is combined with the configured op-stat value as a percentage.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetBaseStatValue
entries.notes: Reads the packed stat from the base Stats array at stat-list offset 0x30 and applies the ItemStatCost minimum clamp.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetTotalStatValue
entries.notes: Reads the packed stat from FullStats at offset 0xA8 for an extended list, or from base Stats at offset 0x30 otherwise. It is a lookup, not the recursive ItemStatCost evaluator. EnhancedDamageMinMaxFix 1.1.0 hooked this function unsuccessfully and also decoded the packed stat in reverse.

entries.name: STATLIST_UpdateUnitStat
entries.notes: Updates a computed FullStats entry and runs the native unit/callback propagation path. ABI proven from calls at 0x2FA476, 0x2FA4B1 and 0x2FA7DD: (statList, packedStat, value, itemStatCost, callbackUnit).

entries.name: STATLIST_EvaluateAndUpdateStat
entries.notes: Evaluates a packed stat through 0x2F8AD0, recursively refreshes dependent op stats, and normally commits through 0x2F9DB0. Its operation switch at 0x2FA697 maps op=13 to 0x2FA8C7, which suppresses the commit when statList ownerType at +0x08 is UNIT_ITEM (4). EnhancedDamageMinMaxFix 1.2.0 hooks this routine and restores only the suppressed stats 17/18 update for effective nonweapon items; external in-game validation passed for melee and throwable weapon damage on 2026-07-20.

entries.name: STATLIST_MergeStatLists
entries.notes: Merges an item's extended stat list into a target unit with proven x64 ABI (target, item, mode) -> void. Clearing StatList[0] before calling this routine with mode 1 reproduces the 2.4 charm-aura re-registration path. Its extended 31-byte prologue is unique in build 92777. CharmZone deliberately does not hook this shared lifecycle entry; it filters ITEMS_IsCharmUsable instead.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetOwner
entries.notes: Returns the owner stored by an item's extended stat list and writes its merge mode. The canonical refresh loop at 0x46F220 calls it before expiring and re-merging each owned inventory item.

entries.name: STATLIST_ExpireUnitStatlist
entries.notes: Canonical stat-list invalidation step called with (player, item) at 0x46F2C4, immediately before STATLIST_MergeStatLists. It clears the stale extended ownership/effects that a direct owner-pointer reset does not cover after death.

entries.name: GetDataTablesForContext
entries.notes: Returns the active compiled data-table container with observed ABI DataTables* (uint8 dataContext). Its exact complete body asserts context<4 and then indexes the global table by context*16. Burn Damage Fix 2.2 uses the same contract for StatesTxt; ISC12 G4 now fingerprints it and rejects a preview D2S whose context byte at +0xF8 is outside 0..3 before any branch-B ItemStatCost lookup.

entries.name: DRLG_ResolveActFromLevelId
entries.notes: Central act resolver with observed Windows x64 ABI uint8 (uint8 dataContext, int32 levelId). It obtains the context ActInfo vector through 0x3006E0, reads its count at DataTables+0x108, walks records backward with stride 0x8C, compares levelId against the signed range start at record+0x04 and returns the selected zero-based act index; an empty or unmatched vector returns zero. The governed index contains 113 direct calls. Its strict 48-byte entry signature is unique in the common 92777/93847 corpus. A D2R 3.3.93847 runtime probe with the complete active stack observed dataContext 3 in BKVince and independently proved through PluginSDK DataTableServiceV1 that all three compiled Levels banks use row size 0x18C and the unique Act byte at row+0x0D. Extended Act Level IDs validates the service ABI, row size and anchor acts on every table revision, copies bank-owned rows into plugin-owned immutable caches and falls back to the original whenever a context, row or Act value is unavailable or invalid. Its final 0.1.0 runtime fixture compiled a temporary RotW Levels row Id 147 / Act 0 and the hooked entry resolved it to Act index 0 from Levels.txt before byte-exact restoration. Version 2.0.0 retains this hook and adds separately fingerprinted room-visibility producers and consumers. D2MOO supplies semantic provenance only and no legacy address, structure or ABI.

entries.name: DATATBLS_LevelsRecordCountGuard
entries.notes: Unique 36-byte witness in the governed common corpus. It compares the compiled Levels record count at DataTables+0x1468 with 0x400 and continues only through an unsigned JB, proving that D2R accepts at most 1023 compiled records. Extended Act Level IDs 2.0.0 fingerprints this native guard without patching it and limits canonical IDs to 0..1022.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x07_RoomInSight
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI void (D2Client*, int32 levelId, uint16 x, uint16 y). All four governed callers pass the complete level result in EDX, but this six-byte packet builder stores only DL at byte +5 after opcode 0x07 and WORD coordinates at +1/+3. Its strict 33-byte entry is unique in the common 92777/93847 corpus. Version 2.0.0 owns the entry and preserves the original path byte-for-byte for IDs 0..255.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x08_RoomOutOfSight
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI void (D2Client*, int32 levelId, uint16 x, uint16 y). Its governed caller passes the complete Level ID in EDX, but this six-byte packet builder stores only DL at byte +5 after opcode 0x08 and WORD coordinates at +1/+3. Its strict 33-byte entry is unique in the common 92777/93847 corpus. Version 2.0.0 owns the entry and preserves the original path byte-for-byte for IDs 0..255.

entries.name: CLIENT_HandlePacket0x07_RoomInSight
entries.notes: Consumes the stock six-byte 0x07 layout: WORD X at +1, WORD Y at +3 and BYTE Level ID at +5. It passes the zero-extended Level ID in R8D, X in R9D and Y on the stack to bridge 0x2EF320, which tail-jumps to DUNGEON_SetClientIsInSight 0x328680. Its strict 30-byte entry prefix is unique in the common 92777/93847 corpus.

entries.name: CLIENT_HandlePacket0x08_RoomOutOfSight
entries.notes: Consumes the stock six-byte 0x08 layout: WORD X at +1, WORD Y at +3 and BYTE Level ID at +5. It passes the zero-extended Level ID in R8D, X in R9D and Y on the stack to bridge 0x2EF700, which tail-jumps to DUNGEON_UnsetClientIsInSight 0x328780. Its strict 37-byte entry prefix is unique in the common 92777/93847 corpus.

entries.name: DUNGEON_SetClientIsInSight
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI void (uint8 dataContext, Act*, int32 levelId, int32 x, int32 y, Room*). The function preserves the complete R8D Level ID and forwards it to DRLG_GetLevel. Its strict 32-byte entry is unique in the common 92777/93847 corpus. Extended Act Level IDs 2.0.0 decodes marked 0x07 packets at this typed boundary before calling the original.

entries.name: DUNGEON_UnsetClientIsInSight
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI void (uint8 dataContext, Act*, int32 levelId, int32 x, int32 y, Room*). The function preserves the complete R8D Level ID and forwards it to DRLG_GetLevel. Its strict 29-byte entry is unique in the common 92777/93847 corpus. Extended Act Level IDs 2.0.0 decodes marked 0x08 packets at this typed boundary before calling the original.

entries.name: D2ClientPlayerIdentityLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Unique 52-byte interior witness proving D2Client flags at +0x4E0, cached player at +0x278, player GUID at +0x270, unit type at +0x26C and game at +0x2B0 before a call to SUNIT_GetServerUnit. Version 2.0.0 fingerprints the complete witness before using D2Client+0x270 to gate an extended room packet to the matching compatible peer or the local player.

entries.name: D2GAME_CreatePortalObject
entries.notes: Central portal-object constructor with a strict unique 32-byte entry in the governed common 92777/93847 corpus. It has fourteen direct callers spanning skill, object, missile and quest paths and calls D2GAME_CreateLinkPortal at 0x432F22. The Town Portal callsite at 0x46FD7C passes dynamic portal class 0x3B, keeps the full destination Level ID and records the created source portal GUID in PlayerData after success. A future Extended Act Level IDs hook must scope class 59 instead of altering all portal classes or patching fourteen callers.

entries.name: D2GAME_CreateLinkPortal
entries.notes: Authoritative linked-portal constructor reached by the Level 256 Town Portal runtime assertion. The observed D2R calling convention carries Game* in RCX, the owning unit in RDX, the source portal in R8, the destination Level ID in R9D and the source Level ID as the fifth stack argument; caller witness 0x432F12 is strict and unique. Its strict 32-byte entry is unique in the common 92777/93847 corpus. It uses the full R9D destination to resolve act, room and spawn, but the interior witness at 0x436052 proves that it obtains the source portal room Level ID as a full DWORD, asserts above 255, then stores only its low byte in the linked portal ObjectData.InteractType. Extended Act Level IDs 2.1.0 hooks this constructor only for validated dynamic class-59 pairs owned by LocalPlayerReady, refuses an incomplete extended contract before any unscoped native call, and scopes the room getter at the exact 0x43605F return address.

entries.name: D2GAME_CreateLinkPortal_LevelIdByteGuard
entries.notes: Strict unique 37-byte creation witness. After DUNGEON_GetLevelIdFromRoom returns the source portal room Level ID in EAX, the native code compares it with 0xFF, reaches the exact runtime assertion when greater, then executes MOVZX EDX,DIL and calls UNITS_SetObjectInteractType. Continuing or merely suppressing the assertion would therefore truncate Level 256 to zero; the gate cannot be fixed by removing the assertion alone.

entries.name: DUNGEON_GetLevelIdFromRoom
entries.notes: Null-safe active-room wrapper with observed ABI int32 (ActiveRoom*). It follows ActiveRoom+0x18 to DrlgRoom and tail-jumps to DRLGROOM_GetLevelId 0x360FC0; null returns zero. Its exact 17-byte body including the tail target is unique in the common 92777/93847 corpus. D2GAME_CreateLinkPortal calls it immediately before the Level-ID byte guard.

entries.name: SUNIT_GetPortalOwner
entries.notes: Portal-owner resolver with observed ABI Unit* (Game*, Portal*). Its strict 32-byte entry is unique in the common corpus. It reads ObjectData.InteractType through the uint8 getter 0x34AD40, zero-extends that byte into DRLG_ResolveActFromLevelId, reads destination-room coordinates at ObjectData+0x24/+0x28, finds or streams that room, then resolves the stored owner identity. A full Level ID sidecar must therefore cover this consumer; bypassing only the constructor assertion leaves the destination act truncated.

entries.name: OBJECTS_OperateFunction15_Portal
entries.notes: Authoritative portal operation with a strict unique 32-byte entry in the common corpus; PDATA fragments its logical body, so the entry and governed callsites define the witness. It validates player permissions, calls SUNIT_GetPortalOwner at 0x58F7CB, consumes the byte InteractType for level records at 0x58F803 and 0x58F8D8, gets full source and destination room Level IDs at 0x58F9DB and 0x58F9F2, requests the level transition at 0x58FA06, moves the player at 0x58FA2E and removes both owned portal halves at 0x58FB9B and 0x58FBF6. Extended use requires a validated full-ID sidecar scope; low-byte fallback is unsafe.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetLevelsTxtRecord
entries.notes: Returns a compiled Levels.txt record with observed D2R ABI (uint8 dataContext, int32 levelId) -> Levels*. Its strict 32-byte entry is unique in the common corpus and it has 44 direct callsites. OBJECTS_OperateFunction15_Portal calls it at 0x58F819 with the byte ObjectData.InteractType and immediately reads the Act field at record+0x0D. Extended Act Level IDs 2.1.0 leaves the shared entry untouched and redirects only that server-operation callsite. The failed 2.1.0 runtime additionally proves client UI callsite 0xC188E consumes the same portal byte and asserts when Level 256 is truncated to zero; the shared entry must remain untouched for MapSense and unrelated callers.

entries.name: CLIENT_PortalLabel_GetLevelsTxtRecordCall
entries.notes: Exact client call from the object label/text path to DATATBLS_GetLevelsTxtRecord. The helper entry at 0xC17E0 receives the output string in RCX and Unit* in RDX, preserves that Unit* in nonvolatile RSI, resolves ObjectsTxt, requires subclass bit 0x04, calls UNITS_GetObjectInteractType at 0xC1882, zero-extends the returned byte into EDX and uses the unit data context in ECX. Its 27-byte context witness at 0xC187F (48 8B CE E8 B9 94 28 00 0F B6 D0 40 0F B6 CF E8 0D AC 26 00 48 C7 C3 FF FF FF FF) has exactly one common-corpus match. On success it reads the Levels name key at record+0xFD and resolves it through LANG_GetStringByKey; a null record takes the existing string-ID 0x150D fallback. The 2.1.0 local runtime stack returned here at 0xC1893 and asserted because a Town Portal destination Level ID 256 had become byte value zero. The complete 28-reader InteractType census makes this the only client Levels lookup driven by that byte. A future relay may pass RSI as a third resolver argument, but must remain exact-callsite scoped and backed by a generation/GUID/class/low-byte validated client sidecar; globally replacing 0x32C4A0 is unsafe.

entries.name: OBJECTS_Portal_GetLevelsTxtRecordCall
entries.notes: Unique direct E8 call from OBJECTS_OperateFunction15_Portal to DATATBLS_GetLevelsTxtRecord after zero-extending ObjectData.InteractType. Version 2.1.0 redirects this five-byte call through a near absolute-jump relay so other consumers and MapSense continue to observe the untouched shared function entry.

entries.name: OBJECTS_Portal_GetLevelDefRecordCall
entries.notes: Unique direct E8 call from OBJECTS_OperateFunction15_Portal to DATATBLS_GetLevelDefRecord after zero-extending the same portal InteractType byte. Version 2.1.0 redirects only this five-byte callsite, preserving the shared 0x32C200 entry and its MapSense fingerprint.

entries.name: D2GAME_ObjectSpawnPortalUnitLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Strict unique 61-byte witness at the packet-0x51 callsite. It proves Unit+0x10 ObjectData, Unit+0x08 GUID, Unit+0x0C animation, Unit+0x04 class ID and ObjectData+0x08 InteractType before D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x51_ObjectSpawn. Version 2.1.0 fingerprints the full witness before reading the same minimal portal identity layout.

entries.name: D2GAME_PortalStateSenderCallerWitness
entries.notes: Strict unique 31-byte caller witness proving the D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x60_PortalState ABI: client in RCX, portal in RDX, owner-player current-room Level ID low byte in R8B, owner-player X in R9W and owner-player Y in the fifth stack slot. The caller obtains the owner unit through SUNIT_GetPortalOwner, then its live room and coordinates. The full current-room Level ID remains live in R12D at the exact call 0x5388E4 before R8B truncation. R8B is independent from the portal destination InteractType stored by the sender at packet +2; version 2.1.0 incorrectly required those values to match.

entries.name: D2GAME_PortalStatePrimaryFullLevelCall
entries.notes: Primary direct call to D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x60_PortalState. Its strict unique context begins at 0x5388CA and proves that the full owner-room Level ID remains in R12D while only R12B is passed in R8B. Extended Act Level IDs 2.1.2 redirects only this call through a relay that supplies R12D as a private sixth helper argument and preserves all five stock builder arguments, packet bytes and coordinates.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x51_ObjectSpawn
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry and unique direct call at 0x53885E. It sends the exact 14-byte object-spawn packet: opcode +0, unit type +1, GUID DWORD +2, object ID WORD +6, X WORD +8, Y WORD +0x0A, animation +0x0C and ObjectData.InteractType byte +0x0D. Extended Act Level IDs 2.1.2 calls this stock builder with every field and coordinate unchanged after publishing the full destination through a process-local GUID/session sidecar.

entries.name: CLIENT_HandlePacket0x51_ObjectSpawn
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry for the stock 0x51 object-spawn consumer. It reads GUID DWORD +2, object class WORD +6, X WORD +8, Y WORD +0x0A and InteractType byte +0x0D, then calls CLIENT_CreateObjectFromPacket 0x99510 at 0x129DD8. That helper performs the native creation before writing packet byte +0x0D through UNITS_SetObjectInteractType at 0x99582; its entry is not promoted because the 32-byte prefix has two corpus matches. Extended Act Level IDs 2.1.2 evicts a reused class-59 GUID, delegates the unchanged stock packet first, then validates the live object against the process-local destination sidecar; no client Unit pointer is retained.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x60_PortalState
entries.notes: Unique strict 32-byte entry for the complete 12-byte portal-state sender. Its packet layout is opcode +0, portal flags +1, destination InteractType byte +2, portal GUID DWORD +3, owner-player X WORD +7, owner-player Y WORD +9 and owner-player current-room Level ID byte +0x0B. The sync caller obtains the owner room ID as a full DWORD at 0x5388A8 but passes only its low byte at 0x5388E4. Packet +2 and +0x0B have distinct semantics and are not required to be equal.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETS_BuildPortalState0x60
entries.notes: Strict unique interior witness within the now-promoted sender entry at 0x47F620. It reads the portal flags and ObjectData.InteractType byte into packet offset +2; the complete 12-byte layout also carries GUID at +3, owner-player coordinates at +7/+9 and the owner-player current-room Level ID byte at +0x0B. This proves the stock 0x60 representation cannot transport either full Level ID above 255 and that +2 and +0x0B are semantically independent.

entries.name: CLIENT_HandlePacket0x60_PortalState
entries.notes: Stock client consumer for portal-state packet 0x60. Its strict 29-byte entry witness is unique in the common corpus. It resolves the client object by packet GUID at +3 through CLIENT_GetUnitByIdAndType(unitType=2), reads destination byte +2 and calls UNITS_SetObjectInteractType, then stores owner-player coordinates +7/+9 at Unit+0x1B6/+0x1B8 and owner-player current-room Level ID byte +0x0B at Unit+0x1BA. The client Town Portal usability predicate at 0xFE1F0 later consumes Unit+0x1BA at calls 0xFE307 and 0xFE333. Packet +0x0B is never part of destination validation, but it requires a separate full owner-room Level ID sidecar when the value exceeds 255.

entries.name: CLIENT_PortalStateOwnerLevelUnitLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Strict unique 15-byte packet-0x60 witness. It loads packet byte +0x0B and stores it at Unit+0x1BA after the same handler stored owner-player coordinates at Unit+0x1B6/+0x1B8. The value is the owner player's current-room Level ID low byte, not the portal destination InteractType.

entries.name: CLIENT_CanUseTownPortal
entries.notes: Observed client Town Portal usability predicate with ABI bool (localPlayer Unit*, portal Unit*). Its strict unique 32-byte entry requires a player, then a type-2 class-59 portal, validates owner or party eligibility, derives the data context from the player and consumes the owner-room Level ID byte at portal Unit+0x1BA. It preserves all native online-Act and quest restrictions after the two record lookups. The failed 2.1.1 runtime returned from the first lookup at 0xFE30C.

entries.name: CLIENT_TownPortalUsability_GetLevelsTxtRecordCall
entries.notes: Unique direct call from CLIENT_CanUseTownPortal to DATATBLS_GetLevelsTxtRecord after loading EDX from portal Unit+0x1BA and ECX from the local player's data context. The runtime assertion return 0xFE30C identifies this exact call. Extended Act Level IDs 2.1.2 redirects only this call through a relay that passes RBX as the live portal argument and substitutes a validated full owner-room Level ID without touching the shared getter.

entries.name: CLIENT_TownPortalUsability_GetLevelDefRecordCall
entries.notes: Unique direct call from CLIENT_CanUseTownPortal to DATATBLS_GetLevelDefRecord after loading the same portal Unit+0x1BA owner-room byte and data context. It is reached for non-owner party eligibility and feeds the unchanged native quest checks. Extended Act Level IDs 2.1.2 redirects only this call through the same validated full owner-room sidecar contract as 0xFE307, preserving the surrounding checks.

entries.name: D2Client_PlayerUnitGuidLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Strict unique 15-byte witness that reads D2Client+0x270 as a DWORD player-unit GUID and passes it beside a live Unit pointer to a native predicate. Independent server paths use D2Client+0x26C as unit type and +0x270 as unit GUID for SUNIT_GetServerUnit. This validates the existing local-client identity field; it does not explain the 2.1.1 0x60 refusal.

entries.name: D2GAME_PortalStateSecondaryFullLevelCall
entries.notes: Secondary direct call to D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x60_PortalState. The caller obtains the portal owner, reads its full room Level ID, retains that DWORD in EDI and passes only DIL in R8B. Its strict context at 0x592FFA is unique. Extended Act Level IDs 2.1.2 redirects only this call through a relay that supplies EDI as a private sixth helper argument and preserves all five stock builder arguments, packet bytes and coordinates.

entries.name: D2GAME_RemovePlayerPortal
entries.notes: Unique strict 32-byte entry for the authoritative player-portal cleanup. It reads and clears the portal GUID at PlayerData+0xA4, resolves the dynamic class 0x3B object through SUNIT_GetServerUnit, gets the linked owner portal, updates room portal flags and removes both halves through SUNIT_RemoveUnit at 0x4C8718 and 0x4C8726. Sidecar cleanup may use this proven boundary but must not depend on the generic unit remover because inactive compression can physically remove and later recreate a portal with the same GUID.

entries.name: SUNITINACTIVE_RestoreInactiveUnits
entries.notes: Unique strict 32-byte entry for inactive-unit restoration. For an object node it recreates or resolves the unit from the class at node+0x0C and retained GUID at node+0x20, then restores the single InteractType byte from node+0x28 through UNITS_SetObjectInteractType at 0x5039A6 or 0x503AA2. Portal Unit* identity is therefore unstable across room streaming while GUID/session identity survives.

entries.name: SUNITINACTIVE_CompressUnitIfNeeded
entries.notes: Unique strict 32-byte entry. Its exact object-class range check at 0x5042ED maps classes 59 and 60 to the special inactive compression path, marks the portal and calls the compressor before returning. This proves that generic physical unit removal is not equivalent to logical portal destruction and that a full-ID sidecar must survive room unloading.

entries.name: SUNITINACTIVE_CompressInactiveUnit
entries.notes: Unique strict 32-byte entry for inactive-unit compression. The object path allocates a 0x38-byte node; classes 59/60 retain the Unit GUID at node+0x20, while ObjectData.InteractType is read through the byte getter and stored at node+0x28. A sidecar keyed by session generation, Game* and GUID preserves the missing high Level-ID bits without widening this shared native node.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetMonStatsTxtRecordForContext
entries.notes: Returns a compiled MonStatsTxt record with observed ABI (uint8 dataContext, int32 classId) -> MonStatsTxt*. It resolves DataTables through 0x300A90, asserts before returning null when classId is negative or classId>=the uint64 count at DataTables+0xF60, then indexes the record base at DataTables+0xF58 with stride 0x1FC. MapSense 0.13.17 fingerprints through the first count comparison and preflights context, count and class id before calling it.

entries.name: DATATBLS_CompileStatesTxt_OverlayFieldWitness
entries.notes: Unique 33-byte read-only field-descriptor witness inside the StatesTxt compiler. It assigns TXT field type 0x16 to record offset +0x02, then begins the same descriptor for +0x04. Together with the subsequent +0x06/+0x08 descriptors, this proves that the first compiled state overlay is the 16-bit word at record+0x02.

entries.name: DATATBLS_CompileStatesTxt_RecordStrideWitness
entries.notes: Unique 22-byte instruction-aligned read-only prefix in the StatesTxt loader. It passes record size 0x44 to the governed table compiler before installing the resulting vector. The immediately following CALL is deliberately excluded because D2RLoader may redirect that compiler integration surface before plugins load; its target is irrelevant to the stride proof. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints only this stable prefix before calculating state 115 as base + 115*0x44.

entries.name: DATATBLS_CompileStatesTxt_VectorLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Unique 26-byte read-only witness in the StatesTxt loader. It takes the destination vector at DataTables+0x290 and transfers the newly compiled state records into it. The associated state count is independently witnessed at DataTables+0x298 by STATES_ToggleState.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetItemRecordFromItemCode
entries.notes: Resolves a four-byte item code in the active data context, writes the class ID and returns the corresponding 0x1C0-byte ItemsTxt record. Transmogrify 1.0.3 validates its strict 16-byte entry signature and uses the returned record to obtain the configured output's localized name-string ID.

entries.name: GetItemsTxtRecord
entries.notes: Returns a 0x1C0-byte compiled items record for a data context and class ID. DurabilityResistance 1.1.0 conditionally clears nodurability at +0x122 for bow/xbow families before the caller reads the record.

entries.name: DATATBLS_CompileItemsTxt
entries.notes: Called once per data context by the governed table-load orchestrator at 0x301773. It compiles the three 0x1C0-byte armor, weapons and misc record sets, merges them into the Items vector at DataTables +0x15A0, builds the associated lookup structures and returns after the active Items records are complete. ItemTypes is compiled earlier in the same orchestrator. Community Pack Item Durability 1.2.1 hooks this entry, calls the original first and then mutates the active compiled ranged records, leaving GetItemsTxtRecord 0x314110 unowned for CubeOutputQuantity and other consumers.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetClassSkillCount
entries.notes: Returns the compiled runtime skill count for class ids 0 through 7 from the active data context. The unique 32-byte entry signature is 48 89 5C 24 08 57 48 83 EC 30 48 63 DA 0F B6 F9 83 FB 07 76 19 48 8D 4C 24 48 C6 44 24 48 00. The D2S header writer calls it at 0x534519 and stores AL as NumSkills; the skills-section writer calls it at 0x52F58A/0x52F5D7 and emits one base-level byte per returned class skill.

entries.name: SKILLS_GetBaseLevel
entries.notes: Returns the requested native skill-level view. The skill-tree eligibility path passes flags 0,0 for the base invested level. BulkSkillPointAllocation used it in its superseded mono-rank queue; 1.2.1 no longer polls skill levels.

entries.name: SKILLS_GetSkillById
entries.notes: Resolves a player's skill by skill id and owner GUID. The eligibility path passes owner GUID -1 for the base class skill. BulkSkillPointAllocation used it in its superseded mono-rank queue; 1.2.1 no longer calls it.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetClassSkillIdByIndex
entries.notes: Returns the compiled SkillsTxt id for a zero-based class-skill index in the active data context. Its observed ABI is (uint8 context, int32 classId, int32 index) -> int32 skillId, and its unique 32-byte entry signature is 48 89 5C 24 08 48 89 74 24 18 57 48 83 EC 20 48 63 DA 41 8B F8 0F B6 F1 83 FB 07 76 19 48 8D 4C. The D2S load and save loops pair it with DATATBLS_GetClassSkillCount; the writer resolves each returned id through SKILLS_GetSkillById before serializing its base level.

entries.name: SKILLS_SetLeftActiveSkill
entries.notes: Canonical left-slot restore routine. It resolves a recreated skill by (skillId, ownerGUID) and stores it at skillList+0x08; CharmInventoryAuras uses it after re-merging aura charms.

entries.name: SKILLS_SetRightActiveSkill
entries.notes: Canonical right-slot pointer setter. It resolves an existing skill by (skillId, ownerGUID) and stores it at skillList+0x10. CharmInventoryAuras uses it after re-merging aura charms. Revive Overhaul 2.0 used it after native SrvDoFunc 58 cleared the right slot, but runtime evidence showed that this pointer-only restore does not reactivate Aura Enchanted; Revive Overhaul 2.1 instead uses D2GAME_AssignSkill 0x438A70.

entries.name: D2GAME_AssignSkill
entries.notes: Assigns an existing skill through the complete native active-skill path with observed Windows x64 ABI void (unit, side, skillId, ownerGuid). Side 0 obtains and sets the right active skill through UNITS_GetRightSkill and SKILLS_SetRightActiveSkill, then continues through the native activation and synchronization logic. MONSTERUNIQUE_UMod30_AuraEnchanted calls it at 0x495F64 as (monster,0,selectedSkillId,-1) after creating the aura skill. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in the governed common corpus. Revive Overhaul 2.1 replays this same path with the exact captured Aura Enchanted tuple after successful native Revive.

entries.name: GetItemDataContext
entries.notes: Returns the data-table context byte at Unit+0x1BD with observed ABI uint8 (Unit*). Despite its historical name, STATES_ToggleState calls it for arbitrary units before resolving the matching data tables. Burn Damage Fix 2.2 borrows its strict 47-byte body to select the active compiled StatesTxt context without persisting a Unit pointer.

entries.name: UNITS_SetOverlay
entries.notes: Applies a direct overlay to a unit with observed Windows x64 ABI void (unit, overlayId, unusedLayer). The entry validates the overlay index, obtains or allocates a stat list with internal flag 0x80, writes the overlay ID to unit_dooverlay stat 178 and refreshes the unit. Its strict unique 24-byte entry signature is 48 89 5C 24 18 55 57 41 56 48 83 EC 30 45 8B F0 8B FA 48 8B D9 48 85 C9. BKVCombat borrows it for Crushing Blow. Burn Damage Fix 2.1 also borrows it without hooking and applies fire_hit overlay 81 on layer 0 immediately after a positive state-confirmed Burn application, then periodically while state burning 115 remains active and the unit is alive. The direct-overlay channel is last-write-wins; Burn Damage Fix counts a foreign prior value before replacing it. Direct unit targeting does not guarantee that each emitted particle remains attached after spawning.

entries.name: UNITS_SetOverlay_UnitDoOverlayStatWitness
entries.notes: Unique read-only 30-byte witness 0F B6 8B BD 01 00 00 44 0F B7 CF 41 B8 B2 00 00 00 48 8B D6 44 89 74 24 20 E8 96 9E FA FF inside UNITS_SetOverlay. The MOV R8D,0xB2 proves that the overlay ID is written as unit_dooverlay stat 178; the separate 0x80 constant is a stat-list flag, not a stat ID. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints this witness before reading stat 178 for diagnostic arbitration.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetBeltType
entries.notes: Validates UNIT_ITEM, resolves its ItemsTxt record and returns the unsigned belt-type byte at record+0x140 with observed ABI (beltItem) -> int32. INVENTORY_GetFreeBeltSlot calls it for the item equipped in body slot 8. Its strict 32-byte prologue is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UNITS_GetUnitId
entries.notes: Returns the 32-bit unit id stored at unit+0x08, or 0xFFFFFFFF for a null unit. The 92777 merc-equipment callback calls it on the resolved hireling and compares the result with packet+0x05; the runtime 0x51 witness carried merc id 1 and item id 43. This corrects the former misleading UNITS_GetItemCell label.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_MercEquipment
entries.notes: Authoritative callback with ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32 for the 17-byte client opcode 0x51. Packet layout proven by paired equip/unequip traces is {opcode:u8, cursorItemId:u32, mercId:u32, equippedItemId:u32, bodyLoc:u32}. It requires size 17, resolves relation 7, validates the merc id through UNITS_GetUnitId, maps bodyLoc only below 11, and performs the native transactional placement and item updates. A successful torso equip reached SUNIT_AttachSound at 0x4C1364 with sound 0x5E. Its exact 29-byte entry signature beginning 40 55 53 57 48 8D 6C 24 B9 is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UNITS_GetInventory
entries.notes: Resolves a unit's inventory pointer through the same +A0/+98/+90 reference path as the legacy 0x208330 routine.

entries.name: UNITS_GetInventoryGrid
entries.notes: Maps a player, storage page and expansion flag to the active Inventory.txt grid. Page 0 resolves the main inventory, page 3 the Horadric Cube and page 4 the personal/shared stash grid.

entries.name: UNITS_GetItemData
entries.notes: Returns the item-data pointer stored at unit+0x10. CharmInventoryAuras reads flags at +0x18 and the inventory-grid node position at +0xB8.

entries.name: UNITS_GetSkillList
entries.notes: Returns the skill list stored through the unit path at +0x100. The list head is at +0x00, active left and right skill pointers are at +0x08 and +0x10, and the used skill is at +0x18. Skill identity is the signed SkillsTxt ID plus owner GUID. ArmageddonCtCFix additionally proves these list-head and used-skill fields through SrvDo124 and the 0x33DD40 resolver; see Mission/armageddon-ctc-fix.md.

entries.name: UNITS_GetStatListEx
entries.notes: Returns the extended stat-list pointer stored at unit+0x88; its first pointer is the current owning target unit.

entries.name: UNITS_GetUnitType
entries.notes: Returns the unit type used throughout the common 92777/93847 stat paths (0 player, 1 monster, 4 item). EnhancedDamageMinMaxFix limits inventory correction to players and monsters. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints its unique entry, guards each event dispatcher with the expected player/monster type and classifies units in the synthetic Fire-resolution context.

entries.name: MONSTERS_GetHirelingTypeId
entries.notes: Returns zero for an ordinary monster and a nonzero hireling type for a hireling. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints its unique 24-byte entry and excludes hirelings from the monster-attacker/defender flags passed to the native Fire resolver. BKVCombat uses the same helper to distinguish hirelings in Crushing Blow and Open Wounds policy.

entries.name: ITEMS_IsCharmUsable
entries.notes: Returns whether a charm can contribute its effects, with proven x64 ABI (item, player) -> int32. It rejects broken/disabled items, requires ITEMTYPE_CHARM 13, requires inventory page byte ItemData+0x55 to be zero and delegates attribute/level requirements to 0x36BC50. The item-grant path calls it after placement and refreshes the player inventory only when it returns nonzero. BaseMod 1.13d replaces the corresponding legacy D2Common ordinal 10415 at RVA 0x47090 for CharmZone; CharmZone 0.3.1 calls the native predicate first and then filters it by full configured-zone containment without mutating stat-list ownership. Runtime validation proved +20 fire resistance outside/inside/outside as 0/20/0.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetItemSeed
