entries.notes: Validates UNIT_ITEM and returns ItemData+0x04, the low/high item RNG seed pair. The vanilla Larzuk magic-quality branch calls it before the 0x6AC690C5 LCG roll. ForceLarzukSockets advances the same seed only when a configured inclusive range contains more than one legal result.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetItemQuality
entries.notes: Returns ItemData quality, defaulting to normal when no valid item data exists. The Larzuk reward path branches on values 4 through 9; ForceLarzukSockets configures only magic 4, set 5, rare 6, unique 7 and crafted 8, leaving all other qualities vanilla.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetInvPage
entries.notes: Validates UNIT_ITEM, calls UNITS_GetItemData 0x34A500 and returns ItemData+0x55, or 0xFF when no valid item data exists. CubeOutputQuantity 1.0.2 installs an inline hook at this entry. MassID 0.2.9 required the vanilla prologue and refused after that hook; MassID 1.0.0 removes the dependency and reads the proven field through UNITS_GetItemData. Local runtime validation on build 92777 confirmed that both plugins load together.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetMaxSockets
entries.notes: Returns the maximum socket count for the concrete item. The 92777 implementation reads ItemData item level at +0x38, ItemTypes socket thresholds and the compiled Items gemsockets cap. AdvancedItemTooltips and ForceLarzukSockets call this native routine instead of duplicating those rules; ForceLarzukSockets additionally preserves the inventory width-by-height cap applied by ITEMS_AddSockets.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetItemCode
entries.notes: Returns the packed four-byte base item code with proven x64 ABI (item) -> uint32. Its 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777 and the server caller at 0x4BB963 compares EAX with 0x20786F62 (`box `) to select the Horadric Cube path. The index records 94 direct callers. CharmZone 0.3.2 uses it only after native charm eligibility succeeds, allowing configured BK starter codes mfd, mfc and mff to bypass the spatial restriction.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetTotalMaxStack
entries.notes: Returns the concrete item's maximum stack quantity. The verified 92777 body resolves the ItemsTxt record, reads maxstack at +0xF0, adds stat 254 and caps the total at 511. It has 39 direct callers; QtyDisplayIssue uses it instead of duplicating the stack rules.

entries.name: ITEMS_HasDurability
entries.notes: Returns nonzero only for an item whose compiled ItemsTxt record has nodurability clear at +0x122 and durability nonzero at +0x121, whose effective maximum durability is nonzero, and whose total item_indestructible stat 0x98 is <= 0. The ethereal generator calls it at 0x4432F4 before the random roll and again at 0x443507 after applying the ethereal flag. Proven x64 ABI: (item) -> int32.

entries.name: ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId
entries.notes: Checks an item against an itemtypes row through D2R's compiled equivalence LUT. The plugin filters only the two ethereal-generation callers.

entries.name: ITEMS_DecodeItemFromBitstream
entries.notes: Full item decoder reached by 36 direct callers. Item-action handlers pass the destination item, bitstream pointer, byte length, version 105 and a failure output. The unique 14-byte entry signature begins 40 55 53 41 55 41 57 48 8B EC 48 83 EC 68. For historical provenance only, the RuffnecKk ExtendedItemStats prototype overrode the byte length during a thread-local validated EIT1 replay; this is not upstream eezstreet or an ISC12 product dependency.

entries.name: ITEMS_ReadItemBitstreamMetadata
entries.notes: Five-argument wrapper reached by 31 direct callers before item creation. It forwards data context, bitstream pointer, byte length, mode and metadata output to 0x375010 while supplying version 105. Its complete 27-byte wrapper signature is unique in build 92777. The output role is proven by 0x9C/0x9D receiver call sites; a more specific internal structure name remains intentionally unclaimed.

entries.name: ITEMS_AddSockets
entries.notes: Applies a requested socket count after capping inventory area to six, quality to magic 4, rare 2, crafted/tempered 3 and set/unique 1 unless already socketed, then base/type/ilvl through ITEMS_GetMaxSockets. It sets IFLAG_SOCKETED and stat 0xC2. ForceLarzukSockets owns a strict 16-byte inline hook here, forwards every non-Larzuk caller unchanged and bypasses only the generic quality cap for the guarded quest call.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemToBitstream
entries.notes: Initializes the 0x28-byte bit-buffer, invokes the item serializer at 0x37FFD0, returns zero when the overflow field at +0x20 is set, and otherwise returns the written byte count. Its 20 direct callers include save paths using a 0x4000-byte capacity and item-action packet paths using 0xF4. The 29-byte prologue/signature beginning 48 89 5C 24 08 57 48 83 EC 60 48 8B D9 41 8B F9 is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: STATLIST_CopyBaseStatsBounded
entries.notes: Observed ABI int32 (statList, destination, capacity). The exact unique 96-byte body witness at 0x2F6527 clamps statList+0x38 to capacity, copies that many records from statList+0x30 as two DWORDs per eight-byte record and returns the copied count. The complete-item serializer calls it at 0x37F0B3 with capacity 511 and destination RBP+0x860. The native body and callsite are byte-identical in the governed corpus covering 92777 and 93847.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete
entries.notes: Complete-item serializer body called once from the outer serializer at 0x3800F0. Its exact unique 37-byte prologue through SUB RSP,RAX sets RBP to final RSP+0x100 and probes then allocates a 0x1970-byte frame containing the low-ID compound suppression table and the per-list stat snapshot. D2MOO supplies semantic naming only; entry, call graph, x64 frame and ABI evidence are native and byte-identical for governed targets 92777 and 93847.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_OccupiedChildCount
entries.notes: Exact unique 114-byte native window enumerates every immediate item-inventory child, clamps the encoded count to seven and writes exactly three bits at 0x37D66F..0x37D678. This field remains distinct from the later STAT_ITEM_NUMSOCKETS capacity and supplies no global tree depth or node bound. The window is byte-identical in the governed 92777/93847 corpus.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_SuppressionTableInit
entries.notes: Exact unique 17-byte memset window zeros exactly 0x7FC bytes at RBP+0x60: 511 DWORD suppression slots for direct stat IDs 0..510. Under ISC12, valid ID 511 would read the uninitialized gap at RBP+0x85C and ID 512 would alias the snapshot beginning at RBP+0x860 unless the bounded writer relay bypasses the table.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_StatSnapshotCall
entries.notes: Exact unique 29-byte setup/call passes capacity 0x1FF and destination RBP+0x860 to STATLIST_CopyBaseStatsBounded 0x2F64E0. Together with the helper body it proves a maximum of 511 eight-byte records per serialized stat list and exact adjacency to the 511-DWORD suppression table.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_DirectStatIdExtraction
entries.notes: Exact unique 45-byte window loads one snapshot record at RBP+index*8+0x860, extracts its high uint16 through SAR 16 and MOVZX directly into EDI, resolves the context DataTables and performs the first statId<rowCount guard. No ordinal adjustment exists before the suppression-table index at 0x37F17C.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_BoundedStatIdWrite
entries.notes: Exact unique 50-byte governed site [0x37F174,0x37F1A6) covers the prerequisite nonzero rejection, unsafe 511-DWORD indexed comparison, 0x1FF clamp/default, 9-bit setup and writer CALL. ISC12 may mutate only [0x37F17C,0x37F1A1): retain native table comparison for IDs below 511, bypass it for 511..4094, then use 0xFFF and 12 bits. The CALL is never rewritten: runtime may use the native target directly or an exactly attested D2RCore WriteItemSaveStatId provider whose 1.1/1.2 body, PDATA, unwind and live slot all forward to D2R+0xA1B710. Publication requires every promoted owner, table, snapshot, direct-ID and low compound witness to match.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_CompoundPartner51Write
entries.notes: Exact unique window fetches stat 51 and stores it in suppression slot 51 after primary stat 50, preserving lightmindam/lightmaxdam single-token compound encoding. D2MOO supplies only semantic names.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_CompoundPartner49Write
entries.notes: Exact unique window fetches stat 49 and stores it in suppression slot 49 after primary stat 48, preserving firemindam/firemaxdam single-token compound encoding. D2MOO supplies only semantic names.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_CompoundPartner18Write
entries.notes: Exact unique window fetches stat 18 and stores it in suppression slot 18 after primary stat 17, preserving item maximum/minimum damage-percent single-token compound encoding. D2MOO supplies only semantic names.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_CompoundPartner53Write
entries.notes: Exact unique window fetches stat 53 and stores it in suppression slot 53 after primary stat 52, preserving magicmindam/magicmaxdam single-token compound encoding. D2MOO supplies only semantic names.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_CompoundPartner58Write
entries.notes: Exact unique window fetches stat 58 and stores it in suppression slot 58 after poison primary stat 57. It is the poison maximum-damage partner; D2MOO supplies only semantic names.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_CompoundPartner59Write
entries.notes: Exact unique window fetches stat 59 and stores it in suppression slot 59 after poison primary stat 57. It is the poison-length partner; D2MOO supplies only semantic names.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_CompoundPartner55Write
entries.notes: Exact unique window fetches stat 55 and stores it in suppression slot 55 after cold primary stat 54. It is the cold maximum-damage partner; D2MOO supplies only semantic names.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_CompoundPartner56Write
entries.notes: Exact unique window fetches stat 56 and stores it in suppression slot 56 after cold primary stat 54. It is the cold-length partner; D2MOO supplies only semantic names.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_Call
entries.notes: Sole direct CALL from outer item serializer 0x37FFD0 into complete-item body 0x37D140. The exact unique 20-byte call-through-return witness begins at 0x3800E8 and binds the shared save/packet call graph in the governed 92777/93847 corpus.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetRequiredLevel
entries.notes: Computes an item's effective required level with observed x64 ABI (item, unit) -> int32. The quality dispatch reads ItemData+0x00 and routes Magic 4, Set 5, Rare 6, Unique 7 and Crafted 8 separately. Its three indexed xrefs are the exported tail wrapper at 0x371AA0, the authoritative requirement predicate call at 0x36C06D and its recursive socketable-item call at 0x3771D3. The common tail preserves socketed-item and skill requirements, adds stat item_levelreq (92) at 0x3779E4, clamps at zero and applies the player-specific adjustment before returning.

entries.name: CraftedRequiredLevelBaseBonus
entries.notes: Unique eight-byte witness 44 8D 61 09 44 8D 79 4D at the Crafted quality branch. ECX is exactly 1 after the quality-8 dispatch, so LEA r12d,[rcx+9] initializes the vanilla crafted required-level bonus to 10. The BKVince companion patch replaces the four-byte instruction with XOR r12d,r12d plus one NOP.

entries.name: CraftedPrefixRequiredLevelBonus
entries.notes: Conditional ADD r12d,3 reached only when the current crafted prefix record resolves. It belongs to the unique 24-byte crafted-affix witness beginning at 0x377084. The BKVince companion patch replaces exactly these four bytes with NOPs while preserving affix required-level comparison.

entries.name: CraftedSuffixRequiredLevelBonus
entries.notes: Conditional ADD r12d,3 reached only when the current crafted suffix record resolves. It belongs to the unique 24-byte crafted-affix witness beginning at 0x377084. The BKVince companion patch replaces exactly these four bytes with NOPs while preserving affix required-level comparison.

entries.name: ITEMS_CapturePacketState
entries.notes: Captures an item's state into a 16-byte output structure with proven x64 ABI (stateOut, item) -> stateOut. Fields are mode dword +0, inventory page dword +4, x word +8, y word +10 and node page dword +12. The argument order is proven by the entry moves RCX to RSI (output) and RDX to RBX (item), followed by writes through RSI. Its extended 32-byte prologue is unique in build 92777. Transmogrify records this state before detaching a source; CharmZone uses the same helper without relying on private ItemData coordinate offsets.

entries.name: ITEMS_InitializePacketState
entries.notes: Initializes the 16-byte item packet state as unplaced (mode 4, inventory page 0xFF, zero position and node). Transmogrify initializes its output state here before setting the selected same-container position.

entries.name: INVENTORY_FindFreePosition
entries.notes: Finds a valid free x/y position for an item in a specified inventory, Inventory.txt grid and storage page. Transmogrify searches only the source container after temporarily freeing the source slot.

entries.name: INVENTORY_GetUnitGUIDFromCorpse
entries.notes: Returns the first dword of a corpse-list record, which is the auxiliary UNIT_PLAYER GUID. Native D2R caller 0x425010 combines it with INVENTORY_GetFirstCorpse/GetNextCorpse and SUNIT_GetServerUnit(game, UNIT_PLAYER, guid). MassID 0.2.6 uses the same ABI before applying the shared-stash marker and inventory-owner filters.

entries.name: STATES_CheckState
entries.notes: Checks whether a unit has a state id with observed x64 ABI (unit, stateId) -> int32. Both native shared-stash handlers pass state 0xBA before accepting an auxiliary player as a shared-stash proxy. Caller 0x33A231 independently iterates state ids and calls this same predicate. Burn Damage Fix borrows it without patching to witness state burning (115) for diagnostics and to gate immediate and periodic fire_hit replay. Armageddon CtC Fix 0.1.1 borrows it without patching to erase a retained random seed only when Armageddon's native state has actually expired. Its strict 32-byte entry is 48 89 5C 24 08 48 89 74 24 10 57 48 83 EC 20 8B DA 48 8B F1 E8 07 68 01 00 85 C0 74 0E 83 E8 01.

entries.name: STATES_ToggleState
entries.notes: Observed x64 ABI (unit, stateId, enable) -> void. SUNITDMG_ApplyBurnDamage calls it at 0x45143C with defender, native state burning 115 and enable=1 after rejecting non-positive duration or damage. Burn Damage Fix never calls or patches this function; 2.2 conditionally replaces only compiled state 115 overlay1 before the original Burn application reaches this toggle, and still reads the resulting state through STATES_CheckState. The strict 32-byte entry is 48 89 5C 24 08 48 89 6C 24 18 48 89 74 24 20 57 48 83 EC 20 41 8B E8 8B DA 48 8B F1 85 D2 78 38.

entries.name: STATES_ToggleState_DataTablesLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte read-only witness inside STATES_ToggleState. It calls GetItemDataContext, passes AL to GetDataTablesForContext, and loads the signed-safe state count from DataTables+0x298 before checking the requested id. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints this exact context/count contract before reading compiled state 115.

entries.name: StatesTxtRecord_EmptyOverlaySentinelWitness
entries.notes: Unique 47-byte initializer for records of stride 0x44. It zeroes the remaining record fields, writes dword 0xFFFF0000 at +0 and advances by 0x44; combined with the native StatesTxt field descriptor, this proves state id 0 at +0 and the empty first-overlay sentinel 0xFFFF at +2. Burn Damage Fix 2.2 uses only an atomic compare/exchange 224 -> 0xFFFF and therefore preserves custom overlay ids.

entries.name: SUNIT_IsDead
entries.notes: Unit-death predicate with observed Windows x64 ABI int32 (unit). It reports dead for a null or death-flagged unit, for player death/dead modes 0/17, for monster death/dead modes 0/12 and conservatively for unsupported unit types. Burn Damage Fix and Revive Overhaul borrow it without patching. Its strict unique 32-byte entry signature is 48 83 EC 28 48 85 C9 75 1D 88 4C 24 30 48 8D 4C 24 30 E8 59 94 FF FF 84 C0 74 4D CC B8 01 00 00.

entries.name: INVENTORY_GetOwnerId
entries.notes: Validates an inventory and returns its owner GUID from +0x48. Both native shared-stash transfer handlers compare this value to the requesting player's UnitId; MassID 0.2.6 repeats that ownership proof before traversing a shared proxy inventory.

entries.name: INVENTORY_GetFirstItem
entries.notes: Validates the 0x01020304 inventory header and returns the first item pointer at inventory+0x10.

entries.name: INVENTORY_GetFirstCorpse
entries.notes: Returns the first auxiliary-unit record at inventory+0x68. D2R reuses this native corpse registry for shared-stash proxy players; MassID 0.2.6 only reads the list and installs no hook here.

entries.name: INVENTORY_RemoveItemFromInventory
entries.notes: Detaches an item from its actual parent inventory and returns the removed unit on success. The ABI and return contract were proven from 92777 call sites and validated by Transmogrify for inventory and stash sources.

entries.name: INVENTORY_GetNextItem
entries.notes: Validates an item unit, resolves ItemData, and returns the linked-list successor at ItemData+0xB0.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetParentInventory
entries.notes: Returns the inventory that currently owns an item. Transmogrify uses it to validate direct player ownership or an item-container whose own parent is the requesting player's inventory.

entries.name: INVENTORY_GetNextCorpse
entries.notes: Returns the qword at structure+0x10. Native caller 0x425010 gives that generic accessor linked-list meaning in the inventory context, while the exact ISC12 witness at 0x9F95C6 independently gives it save-object byte-length meaning. Treat the body as a shared structural accessor, not as inventory-only semantics.

entries.name: DAMAGE_LogResolvedType
entries.notes: Per-damage-type observer called by SUNITDMG_ApplyResistancesAndAbsorb after resistance and flat reduction are resolved. The 3.2 caller at 0x452651 passes game, attacker, defender, base damage, resistance, reduction, final damage, type name, damage structure, and the table flag. FloatingDamage hooks its build-unique strict 26-byte prologue without modifying any argument or result.

entries.name: PLRMODE_FinalizePlayerMode
entries.notes: D2R 3.2 equivalent of legacy sub_6FC817D0. Its seven-argument ABI and mode-finalization role are proven by the resurrect handler call at 0x4B664B, which passes (game, player, null, TOWNNEUTRAL, 0, 0, 1). CharmInventoryAuras hooks the strict prologue and filters the shared routine by return address 0x4B6650.

entries.name: D2GAME_SKILLMANA_Consume
entries.notes: Native mana and charged-item consumption path used by the official plugin pack.

entries.name: WeaponQuantityDelta
entries.notes: Separate projectile-consumption path for weapon/arrow/bolt/throwable quantity; it is not the melee durability rollover handled by ApplyDurabilityLoss.

entries.name: ITEMS_CreateItemUnit
entries.notes: Creates an item unit from player, class id, game, spawn target, quality, no-sockets, no-ethereal, item level and optional seed arguments. The 11-argument ABI is proven by the 92777 wrapper at 0x517530 and the stack-to-drop-flags mapping in its strict prologue. Transmogrify hooks it only while creating its output and forces noSockets=1 before packet serialization.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetPlayerItemLevel
entries.notes: Returns the native item level selected for a player-created item. Transmogrify uses it when creating an unplaced normal-quality output before same-container placement.

entries.name: SUNIT_RemoveServerUnit
entries.notes: Releases a server unit after it has been detached from inventory ownership. Transmogrify calls it only after the native remove-from-container action and successful inventory detach.

entries.name: ApplyDurabilityLoss
entries.notes: Native durability-loss routine; 4 percent weapon and 10 percent armor thresholds. Throwing weapons used in melee enter this routine, and depleted internal durability can roll over into a one-point stack reduction.

entries.name: D2GAME_ITEMS_GenerateMagicAffixes
entries.notes: Build-92777 Magic affix generator with observed ABI (itemWrapper, generation) -> int32. The wrapper contains the item pointer at +0x00 and generation carries item level at +0x18 plus native prefix/suffix decision fields at +0xA8/+0xB4. The prologue saves RDX/RCX into RSI/RDI only after the 0x442C78 prefix load, so any helper injected there must preserve both volatile arguments. ProgressiveAffixesPlugin leaves the entry and native affix application intact.

entries.name: MagicPrefixDecisionLoad
entries.notes: Exact six-byte load 8B 82 A8 00 00 00 of the native Magic prefix decision, located before the prologue saves RDX/RCX into RSI/RDI. ProgressiveAffixesPlugin 0.2.1 redirects only this load through a near relay that call-preserves both arguments and returns one when the ordered TOML category and item-level step require two affixes.

entries.name: MagicSuffixDecisionLoad
entries.notes: Exact six-byte load 8B 86 B4 00 00 00 of the native Magic suffix decision. ProgressiveAffixesPlugin redirects only this load through a near relay; the following native CMOV and affix-selection call remain intact.

entries.name: ForceMagicSuffixSite
entries.notes: Validated 3.2 equivalent of the legacy force-magic-suffix edit.

entries.name: EtherealWeaponTypeGateCall
entries.notes: First ethereal eligibility type check: ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId(item, ITEMTYPE_WEAPON), returning to 0x4432DA.

entries.name: EtherealArmorTypeGateCall
entries.notes: Fallback ethereal eligibility type check: ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId(item, ITEMTYPE_ANY_ARMOR), returning to 0x4432E9.

entries.name: EtherealDurabilityEligibilityCall
entries.notes: Pre-roll ethereal eligibility call to ITEMS_HasDurability, returning to 0x4432F9. Ethereal Item Rules redirects only this call to the strict helper at 0x46D840 so durable indestructible items reach the configured roll while genuinely durability-free bases remain excluded; the post-application call at 0x443507 stays vanilla.

entries.name: D2GAME_PlayerStatRegenGameFrameLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Unique read-only witness 44 8B 89 70 01 00 00 48 8B DA 89 44 24 28 41 FF C1 inside player stat regeneration. It proves that the current server frame is the dword at Game+0x170 immediately before scheduling the next stat-regeneration event. Burn Damage Fix 2.1 fingerprints this layout before using the frame to cadence fire_hit replay.

entries.name: D2GAME_EVENTS_PlayerEventDispatcher
entries.notes: Authoritative player-event dispatcher with observed Windows x64 ABI void (game, unit, eventType, callbackArg0, callbackArg1, callbackArg2). It bounds eventType to 0..14 and forwards callback arguments 4, 5 and 6 to the selected handler; event type 3 selects player stat regeneration at 0x42E600. Its two direct callers are 0x48CB2F and 0x48CBC4. The strict unique 32-byte entry signature is 48 89 5C 24 08 48 89 6C 24 10 48 89 74 24 20 57 48 83 EC 30 49 63 D8 41 8B F9 48 8B F2 48 8B E9. Burn Damage Fix 2.1 owns this entry exclusively only while periodic overlay replay is enabled and forwards all six original arguments unchanged.

entries.name: MONSTERMODE_EventHandler
entries.notes: Authoritative monster-event dispatcher with observed Windows x64 ABI void (game, unit, eventType, callbackArg0, callbackArg1, callbackArg2). It validates unit type 1, bounds eventType to 0..14 and forwards callback arguments 4, 5 and 6 to the selected handler; event type 3 selects monster stat regeneration at 0x448C00. Its only direct caller is 0x48C83F. The strict unique 39-byte entry signature is 48 89 5C 24 10 48 89 6C 24 18 48 89 74 24 20 57 48 83 EC 50 80 3D 61 76 66 02 00 41 8B E9 49 63 F8 48 8B DA 48 8B F1. Burn Damage Fix 2.1 owns this entry exclusively only while periodic overlay replay is enabled and forwards all six original arguments unchanged.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_GenericBurnProductionAdd
entries.notes: Unique extended witness 81 C3 3C 01 00 00 41 0F 48 DE in the common 92777/93847 corpus. The native path has already multiplied the existing Burn numerator into EBX and advanced the unit seed into R8D, then incorrectly adds numeric stat id 316 as flat damage. Burn Damage Fix replaces only the six-byte ADD with a rel32 relay, consumes the current random value without advancing the seed again, adds the max-exclusive burningmin/burningmax roll after passive_fire_mastery, recreates the sign flag and resumes at 0x44CB38.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_GameDifficultyDataSetLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Unique 38-byte read-only witness 48 89 4C 24 30 0F B6 91 04 01 00 00 48 8B F9 48 89 4C 24 40 4D 8B F9 0F B6 89 06 01 00 00 49 8B F0 E8 CA 28 EB FF. Inside SUNITDMG_CalculateTotalDamage it proves difficulty at Game+0x104, data-set context at Game+0x106 and the call order GetDifficultyRecord(dataSet,difficulty). Burn Damage Fix 2.1 fingerprints this layout before using the same offsets in its synthetic Fire resolution context.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_ApplyBurnDamage
entries.notes: Unique 23-byte entry signature 45 85 C9 0F 8E E6 01 00 00 48 89 6C 24 20 56 41 56 41 57 48 83 EC 40 in the common 92777/93847 corpus. ABI (attacker, defender, burnDamage, burnLength) -> void. Burn Damage Fix resolves positive Burn through the live Fire Resistance path before calling the original trampoline; it does not change duration or tick scheduling.

entries.name: AbsorbPercentageCapImmediate
entries.notes: Low byte of the MOV ECX,40 immediate at 0x4506A0 in the native percentage-absorb path. The strict sequence B9 28 00 00 00 3B C1 0F 4C C8 85 C9 is unique in build 92777; plugin-items changes only this byte when items.absorbCap is enabled.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_ApplyResistancesAndAbsorb
entries.notes: Common 92777/93847 Fire-resistance resolver with observed call ABI (damageInfo, resistanceRecord, dontAbsorb); callers ignore its return value. The strict unique 32-byte vanilla entry signature is 48 89 6C 24 18 56 41 54 41 55 41 56 41 57 48 83 EC 50 4C 8B 3A 33 ED 45 8B E8 4C 8B F2 48 8B F1. Burn Damage Fix never hooks this function and calls its live address. It accepts either the exact unowned vanilla entry or exactly one DiagnosticsService-tracked inline owner whose plugin id is monsterdisplay; every internal resistance, pierce, reduction and absorb layout witness remains strict. An unknown, untracked or ambiguous modification refuses loading.

entries.name: ResistanceFloorUncappedClampImmediate
entries.notes: Five-byte MOV ECX,-100 in the uncapped negative-resistance path of SUNITDMG_ApplyResistancesAndAbsorb. The extended witness B9 9C FF FF FF 3B D9 0F 4F CB EB 51 is unique in the governed corpus reused for D2R 3.3.93847. Resistance Floor redirects only this MOV through a near relay, selects a floor from defender Unit* at context+0x10 and resistance stat id at record+0x08, then resumes at 0x4524C9 before the original CMP/CMOV/JMP.

entries.name: ResistanceFloorCappedClampImmediate
entries.notes: Five-byte MOV ECX,-100 in the capped resistance path of SUNITDMG_ApplyResistancesAndAbsorb. The extended witness B9 9C FF FF FF 3B D9 0F 4F CB 8B D8 is unique in the governed corpus reused for D2R 3.3.93847. Resistance Floor redirects only this MOV through a near relay and resumes at 0x4524EC, preserving the plugin-items upper-cap operands at 0x4524D6 and 0x4524DE.

entries.name: PhysicalResistanceCapImmediate
entries.notes: Low byte of the MOV EAX,50 immediate selected for physical damage inside SUNITDMG_ApplyResistancesAndAbsorb. The surrounding physical/elemental cap sequence at 0x4524D0 is unique in build 92777; plugin-items changes only this byte when items.physResistCap is enabled.

entries.name: ElementalResistanceCapImmediate
entries.notes: Low byte of the adjacent MOV EAX,95 immediate used as the elemental resistance ceiling inside SUNITDMG_ApplyResistancesAndAbsorb. It shares the unique 0x4524D0 signature with the physical cap; plugin-items changes only this byte when items.elementalResistCap is enabled.

entries.name: CharacterScreenResistanceFloorOperand
entries.notes: Four-byte -100 operand of MOV EAX,-100 at 0x14E7299 in the Character Screen loop shared by Fire, Lightning, Cold and Poison. The containing witness 8D 4F 4B 83 F9 5F 7C 05 B9 5F 00 00 00 B8 9C FF FF FF is unique in the governed corpus, and four branch sources select maximum-resistance stats 40, 42, 44 and 46 before reaching the same clamp. Resistance Floor writes only this operand with the configured player floor.

entries.name: D2GAME_ITEMS_Identify
entries.notes: Authoritative identify path with observed ABI (game, player, item, flag) -> void. The native Cain inventory loop calls it at 0x53C8F5 with flag 1 for each unidentified inventory/Cube item. It sets IFLAG_IDENTIFIED, updates item statlists when needed, sends the item update, refreshes the player inventory and calls SUNIT_AttachSound(player, 6, player). The 0x517530 item-grant path also reuses it after placement. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: SynchronizeItemAndBoundSkillQuantity
entries.notes: Central routine reached by the Book path; updates STAT_QUANTITY and the bound scroll/book skill.

entries.name: RefreshPlayerItemStatLists
entries.notes: Native full player-item refresh: snapshots vitals and active skills, walks the inventory, obtains each owned item's stat-list mode, calls 0x2F8290 then 0x2F81A0, and restores the snapshot. CharmInventoryAuras invokes it after confirmed corpse recovery and, since 1.6.0, immediately after the softcore player returns to town.

entries.name: ITEMS_RefreshPlayerInventory
entries.notes: Thin native inventory-refresh dispatch used when post-placement attachment reports that a player refresh is required. Transmogrify calls it under the same condition as the proven item-grant path.

entries.name: RejectedJavelinQuantityCandidate
entries.notes: Explicit Javelin item-type path (0x29), not the tome path.

entries.name: ITEMS_PlaceItemForPlayer
entries.notes: Places an item for a player from a 16-byte item state and cell value. Native Cube and generic move call sites prove that the state's inventory page controls the destination; Transmogrify also preserves the source node page for shared-stash routing.

entries.name: D2GAME_SendItemAction9C
entries.notes: Builds server item-action packet 0x9C with ABI (client RCX, item RDX, action R8B, temporary item-flags mask R9D, gamble uint32 stack arg5) -> void; all 11 direct callers ignore RAX. It serializes exactly one node through 0x375EE0 with recursion disabled and capacity 0xF4, adds the 8-byte header and stores the total in one byte. Payload 244 is the last native-safe size. The producer temporarily changes ItemData+0x18 before serialization, restores it before the queue CALL, then walks socketed children through 0x481B50. G9-A publishes a five-byte rel32 entry detour over the complete pushes 40 53 55 56 57, a process-lifetime registered-unwind trampoline that replays them and continues at 0x479CD5, and an entry wrapper that opens or joins the TLS transaction. Runtime qualification on 2026-09-01 covers live unwind, real 0x9C roots, delayed queue, overflow zero-callback, flush reentry containment and complete-stack coexistence.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9CQueueCall
entries.notes: Exact unique five-byte CALL E8 DB 79 00 00 from the 0x9C producer to D2GAME_QueueServerPacket 0x4817F0, with continuation 0x479E15 and ABI (client RCX, stack packet RDX, zero-extended byte length R8) -> void. G9-A publishes a rel32 capture relay that copies the span synchronously and suppresses the real queue during collection or rejection. Real 0x9C runtime transactions complete with staging-error=0 and flush-error=0; rejected overflow issues zero callbacks.

entries.name: D2GAME_SendItemAction9D
entries.notes: Builds server item-action packet 0x9D with ABI (client RCX, parent unit RDX, item R8, action R9B, temporary item-flags uint32 stack arg5, gamble uint32 stack arg6) -> void; all 12 direct callers ignore RAX. It serializes exactly one node through 0x375EE0 with recursion disabled and capacity 0xF4, adds the 13-byte parent-unit header and stores the total in one byte. Payload 239 is the last native-safe size; 240..242 produce totals 253..255, 243..244 wrap the byte length, and serializer overflow returns zero for a header-only send. The producer temporarily changes ItemData+0x18 and conditionally ItemData+0x54, restores them before the queue CALL, then invokes 0x481B50. G9-A publishes the same five-byte entry detour and a registered-unwind trampoline continuing at 0x479EA5. The governed walker proves each child call is (same client, active item as parent, child item, action 0x12, temporaryFlags = parentTemporaryFlags | 0x08, gamble zero). Real three-node socket trees complete 3/3 in mod-local and global scopes.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9DQueueCall
entries.notes: Exact unique five-byte CALL E8 EA 77 00 00 from the 0x9D producer to D2GAME_QueueServerPacket 0x4817F0, with continuation 0x47A006 and ABI (client RCX, stack packet RDX, zero-extended byte length R8) -> void. G9-A publishes a rel32 capture relay that copies the span synchronously and suppresses the real queue during collection or rejection. A real socketed parent plus two rune children completes with nodes=3, captured=3, queued=3, staging-error=0 and flush-error=0.

entries.name: D2GAME_QueueServerPacket
entries.notes: Queues a server packet with ABI (client RCX, packetBytes RDX, size_t packetLength R8) -> void. The item producers zero-extend their one-byte length into R8 before the calls at 0x479E10/0x47A001. Thirty-eight indexed references and the exact unique 22-byte entry signature 40 55 56 57 48 83 EC 40 49 8B E8 48 8B F2 48 8B F9 48 85 C9 75 1F prove this shared queue; the interior witness at 0x4818B6 proves synchronous consumption of [packet, packet+length]. G9-A leaves this entry untouched and calls it directly, in captured order, only after a root transaction succeeds. The void return cannot support rollback after a partial flush. For historical provenance only, the RuffnecKk ExtendedItemStats prototype is not upstream eezstreet or an ISC12 dependency.

entries.name: CharmAuraZoneTransitionCall
entries.notes: Unique 3.2 equivalent of the legacy 0x2A041F call. Its return address 0x486AE5 selects the intended zone-transition caller of ActTransitionDispatch.

entries.name: SUNIT_GetServerUnit
entries.notes: Resolves a server unit by game, unit type and GUID. Transmogrify uses the item GUID carried by the native use-item packet and requests unit type 4 before any recipe or ownership decision. Cast Triggers validates the input target at its 0x4F8DE0 hook, persists only the exact type/GUID and calls this resolver again when the matching successful handler consumes the descriptor; its strict 50-byte witness is unique in the governed corpus.

entries.name: SUNIT_AttachSound
entries.notes: Stores the 16-bit sound ID and source unit, then schedules the sound. CharmInventoryAuras filters this shared routine by the unique successful corpse-recovery return address 0x4B35A6 and sound ID 0x64.

entries.name: AITHINK_MinimalTickContextWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 117-byte window, SHA-256 85EE58C57F0381F78B286B2B05B9636883A408CB508EBFCF51BA07F4600F5FA9, initializes the stack D2AiTickParam subset used by Scripted AI: D2AiControl* at +0x00 and the context-specific MonStatsTxt*/MonStats2Txt* pointers at +0x28/+0x30. The category-2 and handoff witnesses separately bind distance/combat and target at +0x20/+0x24/+0x10. This range remains read-only.

entries.name: AiSpecialStateDispatchRead
entries.source: ROADMAP.html#i9-bkvince-revive-ai-32; Mission/ruffneckk-scripted-domains.md; direct 92777 dispatcher analysis; D2MOO@19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 semantic reference only
entries.notes: Direct 92777 ABI proof for the AI dispatch. The callback is invoked as void(Game*, Unit*, D2AiTickParam*) under the Windows x64 ABI. The minimal tick layout directly observed in the caller is D2AiControl* at +0x00, target Unit* at +0x10, target distance at +0x20, combat flag at +0x24, MonStatsTxt* at +0x28, and MonStats2Txt* at +0x30. D2AiControl begins with signed nAiSpecialState at +0x00. The unique sequence at 0x4A2BC8 loads the tick's first pointer, reads that state into EDX, calls AITHINK_GetAiTableRecord at 0x4A36C0, then dispatches on the returned record. AISPECIALSTATE_REVIVED remains value 7. No complete tick layout is claimed.

entries.name: AITHINK_TargetCategoryDispatch
entries.source: Mission/ruffneckk-scripted-domains.md; reverse-engineering/d2r-3.2.92777/findings.md; direct 92777 dispatcher analysis; D2MOO@19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 semantic reference only
entries.notes: Unique 28-byte switch witness 48 63 10 83 FA 06 77 53 4C 8D 05 1B D4 B5 FF 41 8B 8C 90 08 2F 4A 00 49 03 C8 FF E1. The seven jump-table destinations are category 0 -> 0x4A2CF1, 1 -> 0x4A2BF2, 2 -> 0x4A2C7A, 3 -> 0x4A2BF2, 4 -> 0x4A2C31, 5 -> 0x4A2CA0 and 6 -> 0x4A2CC9. Categories 1/3 use 0x4A69A0 and require a target; category 2 directly calls nullable selector 0x595750 and always reaches the main callback; category 4 skips the main callback; categories 5/6 use 0x4A6760, with 5 requiring a target and 6 continuing after the wrapper's own no-target fallback. Category 2 is the minimal Scripted AI bridge profile because it preserves native targeting without a pre-callback action.

entries.name: AITHINK_Category2TargetSelectionWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 38-byte category-2 block passes Game*, Unit*, D2AiControl*, int32* distance, int32* combat and the byte context to AIUTIL_SelectTargetForAiThink 0x595750, then joins the common handoff without rejecting a null target. Scripted AI fingerprints this block read-only; it does not patch the dispatcher.

entries.name: AITHINK_Category2CallbackHandoffWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 19-byte common handoff stores the nullable target at D2AiTickParam+0x10, passes the stack tick as R8 with Unit* in RDX and Game* in RCX, and calls the native AI-think continuation 0x4A37F0. Scripted AI fingerprints it read-only to bind target storage and callback ABI.

entries.name: AITHINK_GetAiTableRecord
entries.notes: Resolves a unit's active 0x20-byte AI table record. Nonzero accepted states index the special-state table at RVA 0x23981F0; state 7 therefore selects the Revive/NecroPet record at RVA 0x23982D0. The normal path reads signed WORD MonStatsTxt+0x52, requires 0 <= AI < 155, and indexes the normal table at RVA 0x2396E90. The two tables are exactly adjacent because 0x2396E90 + 155*0x20 = 0x23981F0, so widening the bound alone cannot append an in-place record. Direct xrefs are 0x4A276A, 0x4A27B7 and 0x4A2BD1. Its strict 17-byte prologue is unique in 92777.

entries.name: AITHINK_UnitMonStatsRecordWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 17-byte resolver witness, SHA-256 544B34BB7798AA3B84B20F566A3FAE565621EEB5C1061F6393C950C0447A8980. It reads Unit+0x10 as MonsterData and then MonsterData+0x00 as the active MonStatsTxt record, with a resolver fallback path only when MonsterData is null. Scripted AI uses this pointer solely to match the authoritative Classic, LoD or RotW MonStats TableView before any scripted routing.

entries.name: SKILLS_MonsterSkillModeLookupWitness
entries.source: Mission/ruffneckk-scripted-domains.md; direct governed D2R analysis; D2MOO@19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 semantic reference only
entries.notes: Exact unique 82-byte monster skill-mode lookup, SHA-256 2E7C902457E62260B9CB88486C045B10F363181A1F459E9737C129043C7257B1. After resolving the active MonStatsTxt record, the native path searches eight uint16 skill IDs at +0x1C4 and returns the corresponding signed mode from the eight int16 entries at +0x1DC. Scripted AI mirrors this bounded lookup so castOnTarget accepts only a skill declared by that monster and passes its native per-monster mode to AITACTICS_UseSkill; modes outside 0..15 fail closed.

entries.name: AITHINK_SpecialAiLookupWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 32-byte special-state branch, SHA-256 0916D113567A61197A92DA63BFADA77EE02FC58F26613245788F4619F6B38193. It scales an accepted nonzero special state by 0x20 and resolves the table based at RVA 0x23981F0. Scripted AI delegates every nonzero special state to the original resolver and fingerprints this range read-only.

entries.name: AITHINK_NormalAiLookupWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 63-byte normal/fallback branch, SHA-256 77EB51353B60204B4926B3D1CE4A00184816E0998040BAA4BCC5A80AB8C44BFD. It reads signed WORD MonStatsTxt+0x52, requires 0 <= AI < 155, applies stride 0x20, uses normal-table base RVA 0x2396E90 and returns row zero on rejection. Scripted AI fingerprints this range read-only.

entries.name: AITHINK_NormalAiBoundWitness
entries.notes: Unique ten-byte normal-AI bound sequence B9 9B 00 00 00 66 3B C1 73 19. The resolver has loaded the signed WORD MonStatsTxt+0x52 into AX, rejects values greater than or equal to 155, shifts accepted values by 5 and indexes the normal AI table at RVA 0x2396E90. This is a read-only layout witness, not a safe one-byte append patch.

entries.name: D2GAME_MONSTERS_AiFunction03
entries.notes: D2R 3.2 generic monster AI preamble containing the inlined equivalent of legacy D2GAME_AICORE_MinionLeash_6FCF0D10. The caller at 0x4A2BBB supplies the game, monster and AI tick state after resolving MonStats and MonStats2; the inlined leash spans 0x4A3B50-0x4A3C6B and matches the legacy owner, walk-mode, owner-life, distance, scatter and catch-up control flow.

entries.name: MinionLeashOwnerScatterGate
entries.notes: Unique 92777 sequence for the legacy close-owner scatter branch: compares full-unit distance with 1, then at 0x4A3C0F requires ownerType UNIT_PLAYER before calling the escape helper at 0x4A7DF0 with distance 19. This path is shared by all applicable minions and must be filtered to AISPECIALSTATE_REVIVED by the plugin instead of patched globally.

entries.name: MinionLeashCatchUpGate
entries.notes: Unique 92777 catch-up sequence matching legacy MinionLeash: compares distance with 20, calls AITACTICS_SetVelocity at 0x4A7270 with mode 7, velocity 0 and bonus 40, then calls the owner-follow helper at 0x4A8090 with distance 19. The exact signature begins 83 F8 14 0F 8E 5A FF FF FF 45 33 C0 41 B1 28.

entries.name: AITACTICS_IdleInNeutralMode
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI void (game, monster, frames). The D2R routine normalizes zero frames to one, changes the unit to neutral mode when required, calls 0x48B890 with event type 2 and custom id 0, then schedules event type 2 through EVENT_SetEvent 0x48B720 at Game+0x170+frames. The internal 16-byte sequence at 0x4A6D71 is unique: 45 8D 41 02 E8 16 4B FE FF 44 8B 8F 70 01 00 00. It is the first proven fail-safe rescheduling leaf for Scripted AI.

entries.name: AITACTICS_SetVelocity
entries.notes: Exact 3.2 equivalent of the legacy helper: normalizes mode 1 to 7, validates a monster unit, obtains MonsterData AI velocity parameters and tail-calls the low-level setter with (mode, velocity, byte bonus). MinionLeash calls it at 0x4A3C4A with (monster, 7, 0, 40), returning at 0x4A3C4F; ReviveOverhaul 1.1 uses that exact return address plus the signed call sequence 41 B1 28 48 8B CB 41 8D 50 07 E8 21 36 00 00 to confine velocity configuration to the Revive catch-up path.

entries.name: AITACTICS_ChangeModeAndTargetUnit
entries.source: Mission/ruffneckk-scripted-domains.md; reverse-engineering/d2r-3.2.92777/findings.md; direct 92777 analysis; D2MOO@19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 semantic reference only
entries.notes: Windows x64 ABI int32(Game*, Unit*, int32 mode, Unit* target). It builds the mode-change descriptor through 0x4471E0, writes the target at descriptor+0x10, calls the native mode pipeline 0x4475C0 and returns that result without adding an idle fallback. Its instruction-aligned 32-byte entry witness ending in 49 8B D9 and its 40-byte pipeline/return witness at 0x4A7900 are each unique. Scripted AI may use an allowlisted attack mode and must call AITACTICS_IdleInNeutralMode only when this helper rejects the action.

entries.name: AITACTICS_UseSkill
entries.source: Mission/ruffneckk-scripted-domains.md; Mission/d2r33-hardcoded-skill-references.md; reverse-engineering/d2r-3.2.92777/findings.md; direct 92777 analysis; D2MOO@19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 semantic reference only
entries.notes: Windows x64 ABI int32(Game*, Unit*, uint8 mode, int32 skillId, Unit* target, int32 x, int32 y, uint8 flag). It prepares the skill and native mode descriptor, returns 1 when 0x4475C0 accepts the action, and otherwise calls AITACTICS_IdleInNeutralMode at 0x4A7CCE for 10 frames before returning 0. The instruction-aligned 28-byte entry witness through cmp r8b,0x10 and the 70-byte success/fallback witness at 0x4A7C9F are each unique. Scripted AI must not schedule a second fallback after this helper returns false because the helper already owns it.

entries.name: D2GAME_AICORE_Escape
entries.source: ROADMAP.html#i9-bkvince-revive-ai-32; Mission/ruffneckk-scripted-domains.md; reverse-engineering/d2r-3.2.92777/findings.md; direct 92777 analysis; D2MOO@19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 semantic reference only
entries.notes: Windows x64 ABI int32(Game*, Unit*, Unit* target, uint8 distance, int32 deleteAiEvent). The call at 0x4A3C29 passes game, minion, owner, distance 19 and flag 1, matching the legacy escape invocation. The helper derives coordinates away from the target and returns the result of native movement helper 0x4A7540; it does not install an idle fallback on rejection. Its strict 27-byte entry witness and 35-byte terminal-call witness at 0x4A7F1D are each unique. Scripted AI must therefore idle natively when retreat is rejected.

entries.name: AITACTICS_WalkCloseToUnit
entries.source: Mission/ruffneckk-scripted-domains.md; reverse-engineering/d2r-3.2.92777/findings.md; direct 92777 analysis; D2MOO@19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 semantic reference only
entries.notes: Windows x64 ABI int32(Game*, Unit*, uint8 radius). It selects randomized coordinates near the unit and calls AITACTICS_MoveToTarget 0x4A8A10 in walk mode with no target, step 1 and flags 0, returning the native acceptance result without an idle fallback. Its instruction-aligned 34-byte entry witness and 64-byte terminal witness at 0x4A84A0 are each unique. This is the bounded Scripted AI wander primitive; a false result requires the native idle guard.

entries.name: AITACTICS_WalkToTargetUnitWithFlags
entries.source: Mission/ruffneckk-scripted-domains.md; reverse-engineering/d2r-3.2.92777/findings.md; direct 92777 analysis; D2MOO@19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 semantic reference only
entries.notes: Windows x64 ABI int32(Game*, Unit*, Unit* target, uint16 flags). It calls AITACTICS_MoveToTarget 0x4A8A10 in walk mode with zero coordinates and step 1. With the Scripted AI V1 flags fixed to zero, a rejected move returns 0 without hidden wander or idle behavior, so the wrapper must install the native idle guard. Its complete instruction-aligned 39-byte body is unique; the former 28-byte prefix ended mid-instruction and had two matches.

entries.name: AITACTICS_MoveToTarget
entries.source: Mission/ruffneckk-scripted-domains.md; reverse-engineering/d2r-3.2.92777/findings.md; direct 92777 analysis; D2MOO@19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 semantic reference only
entries.notes: Windows x64 ABI int32(Game*, Unit*, Unit* target, int32 mode, int32 x, int32 y, uint8 step, uint16 flags). It constructs the native movement mode and returns the acceptance result. Failure flags can request stock cleanup, wander or idle behavior; with flags 0, failure returns 0 without a fallback. The instruction-aligned 62-byte entry/null-guard witness is unique; the former 22-byte prefix ended mid-instruction and had five matches. Scripted AI uses this core only through the narrower walk wrappers.

entries.name: D2GAME_AICORE_WalkToOwner
entries.notes: Owner-follow helper called by both MinionLeash branches at 0x4A3C61 with game, minion, owner and distance 19. Its role and arguments match legacy D2GAME_AICORE_WalkToOwner_6FCD0B60.

entries.name: CorpseRecoverySuccessSoundCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte sequence that loads sound 0x64, passes the recovering player as both unit and source, and calls SUNIT_AttachSound after item transfer, corpse-list removal, world deletion and server-unit removal have succeeded. Return address is 0x4B35A6.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_Resurrect
entries.notes: Server handler for the one-byte resurrect packet. The 92777 control flow matches legacy Rcv0x41_Resurrect: validates packet size, requires player mode 0x11 (dead), disconnects hardcore clients, restores life/mana/stamina, changes act, finalizes town-neutral mode, then reassigns both active skills.

entries.name: TownRespawnPlayerModeFinalizeCall
entries.notes: Unique resurrect-handler call to 0x42D2C0 after PlayerChangeAct has returned the softcore player to town. The 43-byte signed setup passes (game, player, null, 1, 0, 0, 1) and returns at 0x4B6650; the hardcore disconnect branch does not reach this site.

entries.name: D2GAME_HandleUseItemPacket
entries.notes: Authoritative server handler for the D2R use-item request. The source item GUID is stored at packet+0x0A in the 92777 packet layout. Transmogrify hooks the strict prologue, validates the resolved item and loaded recipe server-side, and delegates all noneligible items to the original handler.

entries.name: RejectedBookQuantityCandidate
entries.notes: Rejected candidate retained vanilla for regression checks.

entries.name: LarzukAddSocketsCall
entries.notes: Authoritative server reward call to ITEMS_AddSockets after Larzuk sets IFLAG_SOCKETED, obtains ITEMS_GetMaxSockets, rolls magic in 1..min(2,max) and forces qualities 5 through 9 to min(1,max). The return RVA 0x4FD580 and caller stack slot +0x58 for D2GameStrc are exact on build 92777; D2GameStrc+0x104 is read by the same function for difficulty.

entries.name: ActTransitionDispatch
entries.notes: D2R 3.2 equivalent of legacy 0x2EC080. CharmInventoryAuras hooks its build-specific prologue and refreshes charms only when the caller returns to 0x486AE5.

entries.name: ITEMS_GiveQuestItem
entries.notes: Resolves an item code, creates a quality-controlled item through ITEMS_CreateItemUnit, finds player-inventory space, places it and emits the native creation/update packets. Its decompiled 92777 ABI is (game, player, code, itemLevel, quality, groundFallback). It provides the canonical creation/finalization sequence used as the proof model for Transmogrify's explicit same-container placement path.

entries.name: ITEMS_SendItemUpdate
entries.notes: Serializes generalized item actions to the owning client. Native 92777 call sites prove the nine-argument ABI: creation passes action, secondary code, mode, inventory page, node page, then packed position. Transmogrify 1.1.1 follows that order; 1.1.0 had inverted the last two values and produced a visible but frozen client item. Source removal uses action 0x20 with the captured packed position in the final argument. For an actor UNIT_PLAYER carrying state 0xBA, the branch at 0x53623C resolves the owning client and sends through 0x536410; native shared withdrawal consequently addresses its removal update to the proxy at 0x4C690C and its personal-inventory addition to the main player at 0x4C694B.

entries.name: GambleScreenGenerationLimitImmediate
entries.notes: Immediate byte in the unique 92777 loop bound `83 FD 0E 0F 8C DB FE FF FF` inside D2GAME_STORES_FillGamble. EBP is incremented after item generation and the loop continues while EBP is below this value. Vanilla is exactly 14; GambleScreenLimit validates the full signature and configures the immediate from 14 through 127.

entries.name: GAME_GetPlayerCountBonus
entries.notes: Computes per-monster player-count bonuses. BKVince hooks it with strict expected bytes to cap monster HP scaling independently at players 8 while the requested difficulty can remain 65535.

entries.name: BKVincePositiveRoomLevelGuard
entries.notes: The unique native sequence `80 FA 01 74 1E 45 85 FF 74 19` contains the classic-game and Normal-difficulty skips. In the private BKVince Expansion profile it is replaced by `83 BC 24 B8 00 00 00 00 7E 19`, which compares the actual null-safe DRLGROOM_GetLevelId result spilled at [rsp+0xB8] against zero and falls back at 0x543D50 when no positive room LevelId exists. This intentionally BKVince-only write remains excluded from the public RuffnecKk D2RLoader Suite.

entries.name: MonsterStatsAreaLevelGuard
entries.notes: Native `test r15d,r15d; je 0x543D50` prevents area-level scaling when the effective difficulty index is Normal. The former RuffnecKk rewrite `45 85 F6 7E 19` was invalidated because the surrounding control flow overwrites r14d with a boolean before this gate, so r14d is not the positive room LevelId claimed by the former description. The corrected BKVince-only owner starts at 0x543D2D and tests [rsp+0xB8] instead.

entries.name: YinyinNormalAreaLevelDifficultySkip
entries.notes: yinyin333333's external patch changes only the native `je 0x543D50` bytes `74 19` to two NOPs. It directly enables Normal and preserves the classic-game and later eligibility checks, but the 2026-08-27 BKVince full-stack load then reached the D2Common LvlTbls.cpp:284 assertion with eLevelId zero. It is therefore rejected for BKVince, overlaps the private ten-byte owner at 0x543D2D, and must never coexist with it.

entries.name: SKILLS_SrvDoFunc20_StaticField
entries.notes: Build-92777 Static Field server handler with x64 ABI (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel) -> int32. It resolves SkillsTxt, evaluates calc2/calc1 and aura range, then enumerates targets through 0x4327D0 with callback 0x5556A0. The 53-byte entry witness used by StaticFieldRework is exact, while its wildcarded form is unique in .text. D2MOO was used only to confirm the semantic role; no legacy address, structure or ABI was transposed.

entries.name: SKILLS_SrvDoFunc30_Curse
entries.notes: Build-92777 native area-state applicator with x64 ABI (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel) -> int32. It validates aurastat1 and auratargetstate, evaluates aurarangecalc and auralencalc, evaluates up to six aura stat formulas, and enumerates targets using aurafilter. The 64-byte entry witness used by StaticFieldRework is exact and its wildcarded form is unique in .text.

entries.name: BookQuantityDeltaBeforeSynchronization
entries.notes: Loads -1 into r9d after the Book type check and before the central quantity synchronization call.

entries.name: AIUTIL_SelectTargetForAiThink
entries.source: Mission/ruffneckk-scripted-domains.md; reverse-engineering/d2r-3.2.92777/findings.md; direct 92777 analysis; D2MOO@19019806df7f3e877fa105b05395d1e3597e2316 semantic reference only
entries.notes: Windows x64 ABI Unit* (Game*, Unit*, D2AiControl*, int32* targetDistance, int32* combatFlag, uint8 context). The category-2 branch calls it directly at 0x4A2C99 and reaches the main AI callback even when it returns null. The routine enumerates and filters native candidates, populates distance/combat outputs and ends at 0x595F7F. Its direct-call set contains neither EVENT_SetEvent 0x48B720 nor event deletion 0x48B890. The strict 32-byte entry witness including the stack-cookie load is unique.

entries.name: AIUTIL_GetDistanceToCoordinates_FullUnitSize
entries.notes: Full-unit-size distance helper used by the inlined MinionLeash at 0x4A3C05. Its result feeds the exact <=1 close-owner and >20 catch-up comparisons, matching the legacy AIUTIL_GetDistanceToCoordinates_FullUnitSize call.

entries.name: LANG_GetStringById
entries.notes: Resolves a 16-bit localized string ID to the active-language UTF-8 text. Independent 92777 callers read the ItemsTxt name-string ID at record offset +0xFC before calling it. Transmogrify 1.0.3 validates its strict 14-byte entry signature and resolves UI string 5387 (convertsto) plus the TMogType output name. CLIENT_BuildNpcInteractionMenu also calls it for each registered action label and immediately copies the result into a 0x200-byte local buffer; its extended 32-byte prologue is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_FindChildWidgetByName
entries.notes: Finds a direct child widget by name with ABI (panel, const char* name) -> widget*. The 92777 implementation walks the pointer range at panel+0x58/panel+0x60, compares each child name through 0x12277A0 and returns the first matching widget or null. Runtime memory at the native VendorPanel callsites confirms raw names such as button_repair, button_repair_all and button_refresh. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 pins its strict 32-byte entry and resolves button_refresh plus the runtime anchors StashWidget, gold_icon and gold_amount without shipping a vendor layout. Skill-tree rebuild and interaction do not resolve dynamic skill children by their generated names; they enumerate children and use payload Skill IDs.

entries.name: UI_GetWidgetLocalRect
entries.notes: Reads a widget rectangle with ABI (widget, rectOut) -> rectOut. For ordinary widgets it copies the 16-byte signed integer rectangle {x,y,width,height} from widget+0x70. When the fill-parent flag at +0x52 is set it recursively derives the parent area. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 pins the strict 32-byte entry, reads the live refresh and gold-anchor geometry through this helper, and writes only button_refresh x/y at +0x70 after validating usable dimensions.

entries.name: INPUT_IsVirtualKeyDownAsync
entries.notes: Thin native wrapper around the imported asynchronous key-state function: it forwards the virtual-key code in ECX and returns bit 15 as a boolean. The skill-tree allocation path calls it with VK_SHIFT at 0x14C69F3. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.0.7 validates the same strict 21-byte function and queries generic, left and right Ctrl; Shift is resolved from the native packet extra marker emitted immediately after this call.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_CanAllocateSkill
entries.notes: Client skill-tree gate taking a skill id and returning a boolean. It obtains the local player, checks unspent skill points stat 5, resolves SkillsTxt and current base level, applies the custom cost/requirement calculation, reads runtime MaxLvl through 0x214220 and rejects blocking state 0x36. The native click path invokes it before BulkSkillPointAllocation observes the 0x3B request; 1.2.1 adds no client-side rank loop.

entries.name: SkillTreeAllocateClickBranch
entries.notes: Skill-tree click branch that extracts the selected skill id and invokes SKILLTREE_CanAllocateSkill before the native 0x3B packet builder.

entries.name: SkillTreeAllocatePacketCall
entries.notes: Validated skill-tree call to CLIENT_SendFiveByteCommandPacket after the eligibility gate. It uses opcode 0x3B, the selected skill id, extra=0 for one total rank, or extra=0xFFFF when Shift requests every permitted rank.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_ClassPageInteractionGate
entries.notes: Unique RIP-relative comparison of SKILLTREE_CurrentPageState against General Skills state 3 in the skill-widget interaction path. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 changes only the final immediate to 4 after fingerprinting the complete containing surface.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_FindTextTabWidget
entries.notes: Observed ABI (skillTreePanel, tabIndex) -> text widget. It formats the indexed TextTab widget name, resolves the child and validates the expected widget type. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in the governed common corpus and is a layout/ABI witness for FourthSkillTree 0.2.0.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_FindTabWidget
entries.notes: Observed ABI (skillTreePanel, tabIndex) -> tab widget. It formats the indexed Tab widget name, resolves the child and validates the expected widget type. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in the governed common corpus and is a layout/ABI witness for FourthSkillTree 0.2.0.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_AdvancePageWithWrap
entries.notes: Reads SKILLTREE_CurrentPageState, increments below the terminal state and otherwise wraps to zero before calling SKILLTREE_SetPageState. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 fingerprints the strict 32-byte path and changes the CMP immediate at 0x14C6BC2 from 3 to 4.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_RewindPageWithWrap
entries.notes: Reads SKILLTREE_CurrentPageState, decrements above zero and otherwise loads the terminal state before calling SKILLTREE_SetPageState. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 fingerprints the strict 32-byte path and changes the MOV immediate at 0x14C6BFA from 3 to 4.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_ClassPageAllocationGate
entries.notes: Unique RIP-relative comparison of SKILLTREE_CurrentPageState against General Skills state 3 in the allocation path. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 changes only the final immediate to 4 so page 3 remains an ordinary class page.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_TabTextRefreshLoop
entries.notes: Refresh loop that resolves TabN and TextTabN, applies active state and text color, then compares EBX against 4 at 0x14C789B. The strict 32-byte loop witness is unique. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 changes that terminal count to 5; missing layout widgets are already null-checked by the native loop.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_GeneralSkillsPrimaryGate
entries.notes: First General Skills branch in SKILLTREE_RebuildPageWidgets. It compares the same current-page global against 3; FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 changes only that terminal immediate to 4.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_GeneralSkillsFallbackGate
entries.notes: Fallback General Skills branch in SKILLTREE_RebuildPageWidgets. It targets SKILLTREE_CurrentPageState and is one of seven exhaustive page-3 comparisons changed to 4 by FourthSkillTree 0.2.0.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_GeneralSkillsContainerGate
entries.notes: Selects the CommonSkillsContainer and ItemSkillsContainer branch for General Skills. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 moves its current-page comparison from state 3 to state 4.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_GeneralSkillsEnabledStateGate
entries.notes: Late General Skills enabled-state comparison against SKILLTREE_CurrentPageState. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 moves the terminal immediate from 3 to 4.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_GeneralSkillsVisibilityGate
entries.notes: Final General Skills visibility comparison against SKILLTREE_CurrentPageState. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 moves the terminal immediate from 3 to 4.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_SetPageState
entries.notes: Observed ABI void (skillTreePanel, requestedPage). The independently bounded body at 0x14C3B10..0x14C3B86 clamps negative values to 0 and values above 3 to 3, writes SKILLTREE_CurrentPageState at 0x3BBDCBC, then calls SKILLTREE_RebuildPageWidgets. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in the governed common corpus for D2R 3.2.92777 and 3.3.93847. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 changes the MOV immediate at 0x14C3B27 from 3 to 4 after a complete fail-closed preflight. Four direct callers cover the decoded ActivateTab payload and both wraparound navigation directions.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_RebuildPageWidgets
entries.notes: Observed ABI void (skillTreePanel), independently bounded at 0x14C7720..0x14C826E. The routine refreshes the current skill-tree page, loops over exactly four tab/text pairs at 0x14C7850..0x14C789E and handles state 3 as General Skills through seven exhaustive gates at 0x14C4084, 0x14C7428, 0x14C7907, 0x14C7986, 0x14C7BC0, 0x14C820B and 0x14C822B. Only the non-General branch enumerates ordinary class-skill widgets. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in the governed common corpus. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 extends the loop to five and moves every General gate to state 4.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_PopulateClassSkillWidgets
entries.notes: Logical population body for a SkillTreePanel, independently bounded at 0x14C4520..0x14C5E96 despite the larger compiler unwind range. It enumerates the runtime class skill count, selects SkillPage rows, constructs each 0xB88 ButtonWidget, installs its skill payload, clones the rank counter and attaches the finished child. The native page loop remains limited to pages 1..3 until Skill Trees Revamp re-enters its proven loop body at 0x14C48B0 once for SkillPage 4; the exact 22-byte destination witness is unique in the governed common corpus.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_ClassPagePopulateLoopSeed
entries.notes: Exact unique 28-byte loop-initialization witness. It seeds R14D, R13D and [rsp+0x3C] to three native class pages, clears the first tab byte and seeds EAX/[rsp+0x38] to zero. Skill Trees Revamp fingerprints this ABI because its page-IV leaf relay deliberately adds one iteration and later restores these terminal values.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_ClassPagePopulateLoopBody
entries.notes: Entry destination of each native class-page population iteration. The exact unique 22-byte witness begins by resolving TabEAX through SKILLTREE_FindTabWidget and branches to the loop tail when the tab is absent. Skill Trees Revamp fingerprints this destination before its page-IV leaf relay may jump here with EAX=3 and R13D=4.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_AttachPageContainerCall
entries.notes: Unique rel32 call to UI_Widget_AddChild that attaches the freshly created class-page container to TabN before the skill loop appends SkillWidgets to that container at 0x14C5284. The surrounding context keeps the page container in R15, TabN in RBX and the real SkillPage in R13D; the class byte remains at caller stack +0x30. Skill Trees Revamp 0.8.0 owns only this callsite to populate an explicitly softcoded ChromeContainer that already contains typed, noninteractive ImageWidget templates, then delegates to UI_Widget_AddChild. This avoids the unresolved direct ImageWidget factory entirely and keeps generated chrome before the native page container in Tab child/render order.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_NativeWidgetIdentityClamps
entries.notes: Exact unique 59-byte block clamping SkillColumn to 1..3 and SkillRow to 1..6 before native name formatting and local table indexing. The unique context at 0x14C4B0A passes SkillPage, clamped column-minus-one and clamped row-minus-one to the formatter, so expanded cells can duplicate an internal widget name. Rebuild and interaction instead consume the payload Skill ID; the clamped name and local slot are not the operational skill identity. Skill Trees Revamp fingerprints the clamp block without patching it.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_SkillWidgetPayloadAddressWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 21-byte producer-side witness containing the LEA at 0x14C5027 that selects SkillWidget+0x668 as the payload destination during construction. The bare seven-byte LEA has three corpus matches and is therefore not used alone.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_PublishSkillWidgetPayload
entries.notes: Exact unique 20-byte producer-side witness moving the temporary skill payload pointer into the selected SkillWidget+0x668 slot before the position call at 0x14C50F1. Independent consumers at 0x14C7536 and 0x14C7D28 prove that payload+0 is the signed runtime Skill ID ordinal.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_SetSkillWidgetPositionCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte rel32 call to UI_SetWidgetLocalPosition inside class-skill widget construction. The strict 30-byte witness at 0x14C50D8 pins the surrounding SkillColumn and SkillRow coordinate loads. Skill Trees Revamp owns only this narrow callsite so its validated Skill-ID mapping can substitute x/y while every unrelated UI caller remains native.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_SetSkillWidgetPositionSuccessorContext
entries.notes: Exact unique 21-byte context immediately after the position CALL. The return address is naturally callsite+5 rather than a hardcoded plugin jump target; Skill Trees Revamp fingerprints this successor context as an additional fail-closed control-flow witness.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_CloneCounterTemplateCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte rel32 call to UI_CloneWidgetTree for CounterTemplate. RCX is the SkillWidget whose +0x668 payload is already published, RDX is the template cached at rsp+0x60 and R8 is the override name. UI_CloneWidgetTree returns the attached clone in RAX although this caller ignores it. A narrow wrapper could reposition only managed rank counters after cloning, but it cannot create dark squares or prerequisite arrows and is unnecessary when the governed full node footprint already fits the usable area.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_LegacyCellWidgetTableWrite
entries.notes: Writes the completed SkillWidget into a zero-initialized 18-pointer stack table using 6*clampedColumnIndex+clampedRow (1..18). The strict 33-byte witness beginning at 0x14C5289 is unique: 48 8B 95 00 03 00 00 4B 8D 04 7F 48 8D 0C 45 00 00 00 00 49 03 CD 48 89 BC CD 28 04 00 00 48 85 D2. A complete 1,435-instruction audit of SKILLTREE_PopulateClassSkillWidgets 0x14C4520..0x14C5E96 finds only the table zero-initialization at 0x14C4992..0x14C49D1 and this write: no read, address escape, consumer or cleanup. Clamped-cell aliases therefore overwrite an unused local slot and do not establish a functional eighteen-widget ceiling.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_ClassPagePopulateLoopTail
entries.notes: Unique nine-byte terminal test and backward branch of the native class-page population loop. The strict 34-byte witness beginning at 0x14C5313 proves the loop state updates and branch target 0x14C48B0. A leaf relay can add exactly one (Tab3, SkillPage 4) iteration and restore the vanilla terminal state before continuing at 0x14C532E; changing the original page seed would instead shift the vanilla pages and is rejected.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_GeneralSkillsTabFactoryTarget
entries.notes: Unique 15-byte block in SKILLTREE_PopulateClassSkillWidgets that resolves the factory parent from the literal Tab3 name through UI_FindChildWidgetByName. Skill Trees Revamp 0.8.0 replaces the complete block with a stack-neutral sequence that loads index 4 into R14D, preserves RCX=SkillTreePanel and calls the already-governed SKILLTREE_FindTabWidget 0x14C5F60. R14D=4 then drives the existing TextTab resolver, so Tab4 and TextTab4 are selected without a new hook.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_GeneralSkillsTextTabResolverCall
entries.notes: Unique 19-byte witness 41 8B D6 49 8B CC E8 DC 0A 00 00 48 8B D8 48 85 C0 74 2B proving that R14D is copied to EDX and passed with RCX=SkillTreePanel to SKILLTREE_FindTextTabWidget. Fingerprinting this consumer closes the fail-closed chain from the 0x14C536C Tab4 retarget to TextTab4.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_GeneralItemContainerLookups
entries.notes: Unique 38-byte block that resolves CommonSkillsContainer and ItemSkillsContainer beneath the General Skills tab saved by the factory. The native population path retains both containers and categorizes non-investable common and item-granted skills, including oskills; Skill Trees Revamp fingerprints this block without replacing either lookup.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_GeneralSkillsFactoryRequirements
entries.notes: Unique 41-byte guard requiring panel+0x8F8 ButtonTemplate, CommonSkillsContainer and ItemSkillsContainer before General/Item skill population continues. A keyboard/mouse softcode layout that omits any of these three dependencies produces an empty fifth tab even when native Tab4 routing succeeds.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_DynamicGeneralSkillsRebuildTabLookup
entries.notes: Unique 33-byte witness showing SKILLTREE_RebuildPageWidgets reads SKILLTREE_CurrentPageState, passes that dynamic index to SKILLTREE_FindTabWidget and then enters the General Skills branch when the state matches the terminal gate. Moving the gate from 3 to 4 therefore makes the rebuild consume Tab4 without an additional lookup patch.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_InitializePanelWidgets
entries.notes: Observed ABI void (SkillTreePanel*). Its unique 35-byte body calls SKILLTREE_PopulateClassSkillWidgets, then SKILLTREE_RebuildPageWidgets, and finally tail-jumps to the common UI continuation. This ordering proves that the page-IV loop seam creates widgets before the refresh path enumerates them.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_SkillWidgetPayloadRead
entries.notes: Unique layout witness loading the skill payload pointer from SkillWidget+0x668, null-checking it and reading the signed 32-bit Skill ID at payload+0. Skill Trees Revamp fingerprints this witness before its position wrapper uses the same established payload contract.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_RebuildSkillWidgetPayloadRead
entries.notes: Unique rebuild-path witness loading the same payload pointer from SkillWidget+0x668 and sign-extending its 32-bit Skill ID. The parent child count is read at 0x14C7CDF and every child is fetched by index through UI_GetChildWidgetByIndex at 0x14C7CF5 before this payload lookup. It confirms that dynamically populated and expanded-page children retain the Skill-ID identity consumed by refresh, allocation-state and rank rendering.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_CurrentPageState
entries.notes: Signed 32-bit current skill-tree page state. SKILLTREE_SetPageState compares and writes it; the forward/backward input paths read it; SKILLTREE_RebuildPageWidgets consumes it for tab activation, class-page enumeration and the General Skills branches. Vanilla owns domain 0..3. FourthSkillTree 0.2.0 validates that live pre-patch range and then establishes class pages 0..3 plus General Skills state 4.

entries.name: StatsAllocateClickHandler
entries.notes: Reference UI handler for stat allocation. Its modifier payload resolves normal click to a total of 1 and Ctrl to 5, then the packet call at 0x14E9F4D passes total-1 in the extra word; Shift takes precedence and follows the confirmation path. This behavior proves the native quantity encoding pattern, but protocol 0x3A itself is not reused for skills.

entries.name: LANG_GetStringByKey
entries.notes: Resolves a UTF-8 string key view {pointer,length} to active-language text. CharacterStatLevelUpButtonWidget_ShowAssignAllConfirmation calls it for the prompt and native Yes/No labels. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 hooks its strict 29-byte prologue and substitutes only AssignAllStatPointsConfirmation while opening its own modal.

entries.name: UI_DispatchMessage
entries.notes: Common UI message dispatcher receiving a message object whose optional payload pointer is stored at +0x110. ConfirmationModal dispatches its selected callback through this entry. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 consumes only the callback carrying its private stat-index sentinel and forwards every other message unchanged.

entries.name: UI_InterfaceToggle_DispatchCall
entries.notes: Five-byte rel32 call to UI_DispatchMessage inside the native interface-toggle path; execution resumes at 0xCE3B6 after the synchronous dispatch that lazily creates panels such as HirelingInventoryPanel. The 23-byte witness beginning at 0xCE3A9 is unique in the 92777 .text. ExtendedMerc reserves this narrow post-dispatch candidate instead of taking a second hook on the common dispatcher entry; the production owner remains gated on the first runtime-created missing slot.

entries.name: UI_InventoryItemWidget_Constructor
entries.notes: InventoryItemWidget base constructor with effective x64 ABI (widget, const char* name, Widget* parent) -> widget. InventorySlotWidget_Factory calls it directly before installing the derived vtable. It initializes the inherited strings and item-render state, including a zero cellSize pair at +0x5B8/+0x5BC; the render paths at 0x2A7574/0x2A75A3 and 0x2A7969/0x2A7971 consume those components. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_InventorySlotWidget_Factory
entries.notes: InventorySlotWidget factory with effective x64 ABI (ignoredTypeDescriptor, const char* name, Widget* parent) -> Widget*. It allocates exactly 0x640 bytes through the UI allocator, calls the InventoryItemWidget base constructor, installs vtable 0x1CF3F20, initializes the direct fields and sets isHireable at +0x638 to false. Its 37-byte signature through the 0x640 allocation is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_InventorySlotWidget_Finalize
entries.notes: Runtime InventorySlotWidget vtable slot +0x08. If backgroundFilename at +0x5F8 is non-empty, it loads that asset into +0x628 through 0x858990, then tail-calls the InventoryItemWidget finalizer at 0x2A8E60. Native widget constructors call this virtual finalizer before UI_Widget_AddChild; identity is pinned by the live vtable plus the exact body because the short prologue alone has two .text matches.

entries.name: UI_Widget_AddChild
entries.notes: Adds one child widget with x64 ABI (Widget* parent, Widget* child) -> void. It appends to the parent vector at +0x58/+0x60/+0x68, grows and transfers the allocation through the native UI allocator when required, and preserves ownership semantics. Twenty-eight direct callsites use the same parent/child order after the child's vtable +0x08 finalizer. Its strict 18-byte entry is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_CloneWidgetTree
entries.notes: Generic recursive widget-tree clone with observed ABI (parent, source, overrideNameOrNull) -> cloned root. The skill-tree population path uses it for CounterTemplate on every SkillWidget and for the optional controller HotkeyText child. Skill Trees Revamp reuses the native population loop rather than calling this helper directly; its unique 44-byte entry remains a governed lifecycle witness.

entries.name: UI_GetChildWidgetByIndex
entries.notes: Returns one direct child widget by index from the parent child-vector contract at +0x58/+0x60. SKILLTREE_RebuildPageWidgets reads the live child count at 0x14C7CDF and calls this function at 0x14C7CF5 for every child before consuming its payload Skill ID. The loop is not bounded to the legacy 18-cell scratch table and includes page-IV and expanded-page children appended by the native constructor.

entries.name: UI_SetWidgetLocalPosition
entries.notes: Observed ABI void (widget, const PointI*). Its unique 55-byte body copies signed x/y to widget+0x70/+0x74 while preserving width and height. It has 99 native xrefs and therefore remains unhooked globally; Skill Trees Revamp redirects only the class-skill construction callsite at 0x14C50F1 and always delegates to this original function.

entries.name: UI_SetWidgetLocalRect
entries.notes: Observed ABI void (Widget*, const RectI*) with signed RectI {x,y,width,height}. Its unique body copies the four dwords to Widget+0x70/+0x74/+0x78/+0x7C and has 29 native callsites. Skill Trees Revamp does not hook this generic setter; it is a governed witness for any future page-overlay or CounterTemplate geometry.

entries.name: UI_ImageWidget_SetFilename
entries.notes: Observed ABI (ImageWidget*, StringView{pointer,length}*) for replacing an ImageWidget logical resource filename. It copies the path to +0x108, loads through 0x858990 into +0x130 and refreshes the image and intrinsic geometry through 0x859710/0x8574D0. SKILLTREE_PopulateClassSkillWidgets calls it at 0x14C4979 on the layout-backed TabN/Background ImageWidget, independently anchoring its identity.

entries.name: UI_ImageWidget_FactoryCandidate
entries.notes: Factory-shaped routine with observed callback ABI (typeContext, const char* name, Widget* parent) -> 0x158-byte derived Widget*. It allocates through the UI allocator, calls UI_Widget_Constructor 0x854710, initializes image state and installs a derived vtable. Zero direct xrefs are consistent with indirect type registration, but no registration or live-vtable witness yet proves that this exact factory is ImageWidget; native mutation remains forbidden until that identity and child render/hit-test order are promoted to high confidence.
