entries.name: UI_ButtonWidget_Constructor
entries.notes: Constructor used by the native skill-tree population path after allocating 0xB88 bytes for each skill button. Skill Trees Revamp does not replace the factory: the additional SkillPage 4 loop iteration executes this same constructor and native payload/counter/finalization sequence.

entries.name: UI_ButtonWidget_Factory
entries.notes: Factory callback with observed ABI (ignored type descriptor, const char* name, Widget* parent) -> ButtonWidget*. Its unique 27-byte entry signature allocates exactly 0xB88 bytes through the UI allocator and tail-calls UI_ButtonWidget_Constructor 0x86E920 with the name and parent preserved. The Skill Trees Revamp scale probe does not call or replace this factory; it uses the identification only to govern the live SkillWidget type.

entries.name: UI_GetCumulativeWidgetScale
entries.notes: Observed ABI float (Widget*). The unique 31-byte entry recursively follows Widget+0x30 to the parent, multiplies every Widget+0x80 scale and uses the native root scale when no parent exists. ButtonWidget rendering, generic scaled-rectangle hit testing and the skill-tree tooltip placement path all call it. This proves scale propagation through a widget subtree, but the concrete ButtonWidget hit-test vtable slot remains runtime-gated because vtable 0x1CE4148 is zero in both governed static PE images.

entries.name: ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation
entries.notes: Validates an item and requested BodyLoc with x64 ABI (item, bodyLoc) -> int32. It resolves the compiled ItemTypes row, compares both BodyLoc bytes at +0x0A/+0x0B, and preserves the paired weapon-location exception for BodyLocs 11 and 12. The ExtendedMerc client path calls it narrowly at 0x2CB0D9.

entries.name: UNITS_GetAllowedEquipmentItemTypes
entries.notes: Provisional name for the target equipment-type resolver with observed x64 ABI (targetUnit, typeAOut, typeBOut) -> void. Static flow requires unit type 1, resolves the compiled target class record through 0x0976E0 and writes the signed 16-bit values at record offsets +0x80/+0x82. ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 observed the QtyTester Rogue target return type A 47 and type B 56, which vanilla itemtypes.txt identifies as Missile Weapon and Missile.

entries.name: CLIENT_CheckMercenaryItemCompatibility
entries.notes: Client-side mercenary/item compatibility predicate with observed x64 ABI (mercenary, item) -> bool. The equipped-slot handler calls it at 0x2CB0E8 after BodyLoc validation. Static flow preserves class-specific restrictions, recognizes Armor and Helm through ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId, and otherwise compares the item against the mercenary-specific type pair resolved by 0x3AEB70. Runtime tracing returned zero natively for Leather Armor class 314 and for the exact Strong Leather Gloves of Self-Repair class 334; ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 proved that the Rogue pair is {47, 56} while Gloves is type 16. The 0.0.20 prototype admitted only the final type-B call at 0x159FC8 for a requested BodyLoc 10 already accepted by ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation, producing compatibility result one without replacing this whole function.

entries.name: CLIENT_MercenaryTargetTypeBValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 C3 98 21 00 85 C0 74 24 48 8B 6C 24 30 B0 01 48 8B inside CLIENT_CheckMercenaryItemCompatibility. It is the final ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId call for the target's type-B value after the type-A test failed. ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 observed native result zero for the class-334 glove against Rogue type B 56. Prototype 0.0.20 changed only this callsite result to one while the requested BodyLoc was 10 and ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation(item, 10) returned nonzero; the enclosing compatibility predicate then returned one.

entries.name: ITEMS_CheckItemRequirementsForUnit
entries.notes: Shared client/server item requirement predicate with observed x64 ABI (item, targetUnit, option, strengthOut, dexterityOut, levelOut, finalOption) -> int32. It resolves ItemsTxt, evaluates identified state and effective strength, dexterity, level and class restrictions, and returns zero when any required gate fails. With the exact class-334 compatibility result temporarily admitted at its dedicated client callsite, ExtendedMerc observed this predicate return one at both mercenary callsites 0x2CB10D and 0x4C1031. The plugin does not own this broadly shared function.

entries.name: UI_MercenaryBodyLocValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 32 0A 0A 00 85 C0 74 77 48 8B D5 48 8B CF E8 73 ED inside UI_HandleEquippedItemClick. It calls ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation for the cursor item and widget BodyLoc, then joins the UI refusal branch on zero. Runtime tracing of the exact class-334 glove against the created BodyLoc 10 returned one.

entries.name: UI_MercenaryCompatibilityValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 73 ED E8 FF 84 C0 74 68 33 C9 45 33 C9 89 4C 24 30 inside UI_HandleEquippedItemClick. It calls CLIENT_CheckMercenaryItemCompatibility and joins the UI refusal branch when the boolean result is false. Runtime tracing returned zero natively for the exact class-334 glove; the temporary ExtendedMerc 0.0.8 override returned one only at this callsite so the later authoritative path could be observed.

entries.name: UI_MercenaryRequirementsValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 3E 0B 0A 00 85 C0 74 36 8B 83 D8 05 00 00 89 84 24 inside UI_HandleEquippedItemClick. It calls ITEMS_CheckItemRequirementsForUnit for the cursor item and mercenary immediately before the successful path builds the equip command through 0x15C220. Runtime tracing returned one for the exact class-334 glove once only the preceding compatibility callsite was admitted experimentally.

entries.name: SERVER_MercenaryRequirementsValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 1A AC EA FF 85 C0 75 37 4C 8B 45 9F 8D 50 5D 48 8B in SERVER_HandleMercEquipmentPacket51. It calls the same ITEMS_CheckItemRequirementsForUnit predicate after resolving the packet item and mercenary; a zero result enters the authoritative refusal branch. Runtime tracing returned one for the exact class-334 glove after the narrow client compatibility experiment, proving the later server placement path is responsible for the remaining refusal.

entries.name: SERVER_MercenaryFirstPlacementCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 77 04 FB FF 84 C0 75 36 4C 8B 45 9F BA 5C 00 00 00 in SERVER_HandleMercEquipmentPacket51. It calls the common server item-placement routine at 0x471500 after mercenary requirements pass. Native ExtendedMerc tracing of the exact class-334 glove returned zero here; prototype 0.0.20 admitted only the target type-B decision deeper at 0x472CED, after which the same placement envelope returned one.

entries.name: SERVER_ItemPlacementStateBuilderCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 64 1B 00 00 80 BD F8 96 00 00 00 0F 84 64 02 00 00 inside the common item-placement routine. It calls the provisional placement-state builder at 0x473210. Runtime tracing showed a valid builder result for the rejected class-334 mercenary-glove transaction.

entries.name: SERVER_ItemPlacementValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 74 27 00 00 84 C0 0F 84 B9 01 00 00 48 83 C7 04 49 inside the common item-placement routine. It calls 0x473ED0 for the built item-placement state. Correlated ExtendedMerc 0.0.16 runtime tracing returned zero for the native class-334 server glove transaction; with only the late target type-B decision admitted, 0.0.20 observed the same authoritative placement envelope return one.

entries.name: SERVER_PlacementFinalValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 C4 C8 FF FF 84 C0 0F 84 89 01 00 00 4C 8B 74 24 48 inside ITEMS_PlaceItemForPlayer 0x471500. It calls the provisional final validator at 0x46E050 after every 0x473ED0 item-state validation succeeds. The native class-334 server glove transaction did not reach this call because 0x473ED0 returned zero first; a later {4, 255, 0, 0} state observed by ExtendedMerc 0.0.17 reached it and returned one. Prototype 0.0.20 also reached the call for the authoritative {1, 255, 10, 10} glove transaction after the narrow 0x472CED admission and observed final-validator result one.

entries.name: SERVER_ValidateItemPlacementState
entries.notes: Provisional name for the server predicate reached from callsite 0x471757 with observed ABI (state, item, placement, flag) -> bool. For the exact class-334 mercenary-glove server transaction, runtime tracing observed 0x36E240, 0x36E2D0, 0x34FC20 and 0x34FC60 all return zero; 0x385550 and D2GAME_ValidateItemPacketState 0x474700 return one; and 0x46E2B0 returns a record whose first pointer is null. Correlated ExtendedMerc 0.0.16 tracing then observed 0x472D20 return zero and this enclosing function return zero. A later {4, 255, 0, 0} state succeeds here but lies outside the rejected placement-server-first envelope. Prototype 0.0.20 admitted only the final target type-B test at 0x472CED for BodyLoc 10; 0x472D20, the following validators and this enclosing predicate then all returned one for the authoritative {1, 255, 10, 10} state. These results establish control flow only; helper semantics remain provisional.

entries.name: SERVER_PlacementDestinationValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 F7 EC FF FF 84 C0 74 C6 48 8B D5 48 8B CB E8 B8 F4 inside 0x473ED0. It calls the provisional destination validator at 0x472D20 and returns to the enclosing rejection branch on zero. Correlated ExtendedMerc 0.0.16 runtime tracing observed zero for the native class-334 server glove transaction and did not reach 0x4734F0. Prototype 0.0.20 admitted only the late type-B check at 0x472CED; this call and the following 0x4734F0 validation then returned one.

entries.name: SERVER_ValidatePlacementDestination
entries.notes: Provisional name for the predicate called at 0x474024 with observed ABI (state, item, placement) -> bool. Correlating the archived ExtendedMerc logs with the placement-server-first entry and exit proves that the exact rejected server placement has four int32 fields {1, 255, 10, 10} at offsets +0x00/+0x04/+0x08/+0x0C; the previous {1, -1, 10, 10} transcription treated 255 as signed, while {4, 255, 0, 0} belongs to a later state outside that server envelope. ExtendedMerc 0.0.16 observed 0x472B10 return zero, after which this function returned zero without reaching 0x46E450, 0x4730E0 or 0x4734F0. With only the final target type-B callsite 0x472CED admitted for BodyLoc 10, prototype 0.0.20 observed 0x472B10=1, 0x46E450=1, 0x4730E0=1, this function=1 and the following 0x4734F0=1.

entries.name: SERVER_PlacementEquippableItemValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 97 FB FF FF 44 0F B6 F0 84 C0 74 29 8B 53 0C 48 8B inside 0x472D20. It calls the provisional equippable-item predicate at 0x472B10 for placement states whose field +0x0C is below 11. ExtendedMerc 0.0.16 observed this exact call return zero for the native class-334 server glove state {1, 255, 10, 10}; the following 0x46E450 and 0x4730E0 calls were not reached. Prototype 0.0.20 changed only the final type-B subcall at 0x472CED under a BodyLoc-10 guard, after which this call returned one and both following validators were reached successfully.

entries.name: SERVER_ValidateEquippableItemForTarget
entries.notes: Provisional name for the predicate called from 0x472F74 with observed ABI (placementState, item) -> bool. ExtendedMerc 0.0.18 observed the exact {1, 255, 10, 10} glove transaction pass its identified flag, class-validity, broken flag, special-restriction and target-class-policy guards before both generic Armor type 3 and Helm type 37 tests returned zero. ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 then observed 0x3AEB70 return the Rogue target pair {47, 56}; the class-334 glove matched neither type, proving the first negative cause. Prototype 0.0.20 preserved every preceding guard and changed only the final type-B callsite 0x472CED to one while BodyLoc 10 was requested and ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation(item, 10) succeeded; this predicate then returned one and the complete authoritative placement succeeded. D2MOO's legacy body-item placement routine is semantic evidence only; no legacy address or ABI is transferred.

entries.name: SERVER_TargetAllowedEquipmentTypesCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 B1 BE F3 FF 40 84 ED 74 36 84 DB 74 32 8B 54 24 68 inside SERVER_ValidateEquippableItemForTarget. It calls 0x3AEB70 to build the target-specific item-type pair after the generic Armor and Helm tests fail. ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 observed the QtyTester Rogue target produce type A 47 and type B 56.

entries.name: SERVER_EquippableTargetTypeBValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 9E 0B F0 FF 85 C0 0F 85 A9 FE FF FF 48 8B 5C 24 58 inside SERVER_ValidateEquippableItemForTarget. It is the final ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId call for the target's type-B value after the type-A test at 0x472CD4 failed. ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 observed native result zero for the class-334 glove against Rogue type B 56. Prototype 0.0.20 changed only this result to one while the authoritative placement requested BodyLoc 10 and ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation(item, 10) returned nonzero; 0x472B10, 0x472D20, 0x473ED0, the final validator and ITEMS_PlaceItemForPlayer then all returned one.

entries.name: UI_ShowConfirmationModal
entries.notes: Build-92777 ConfirmationModal constructor with ABI (prompt, confirmLabel, dismissLabel, confirmMessage, dismissMessage, displayFlag). It copies the two callback messages into the modal and updates the three text widgets when an existing modal is reused.

entries.name: StatsAllocatePacketCountEncoding
entries.notes: The instruction LEA R8D,[RDI-1] encodes a resolved total allocation count as additional ranks immediately before CLIENT_SendFiveByteCommandPacket. Normal total 1 becomes extra 0 and Ctrl total 5 becomes extra 4. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 applies this proven total-minus-one encoding to opcode 0x3B; extra 4 yielding exactly five instant skill ranks was validated in game on build 92777.

entries.name: CharacterStatLevelUpButtonWidget_ShowAssignAllConfirmation
entries.notes: Reads the stat index at widget+0xB88, constructs confirm and dismiss UI messages, resolves AssignAllStatPointsConfirmation plus native Yes/No labels, and calls UI_ShowConfirmationModal at 0x847C40. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 calls this proven builder with a private sentinel instead of reimplementing Diablo's modal layout.

entries.name: D2GAME_MONSTER_ApplyStatRegen
entries.notes: Monster stat-regeneration event callback with proven x64 ABI (game, unit, a3, a4) -> void. The negative-life path reads HPREGEN and current hitpoints, checks current life below 256 before the town guard, then applies the tick; a tick crossing directly from positive life to zero therefore bypasses the vanilla town safeguard.

entries.name: UNITS_GetRoom
entries.notes: Returns the active room for a unit through its path representation. D2GAME_MONSTER_ApplyStatRegen passes this result directly to DUNGEON_IsRoomInTown before suppressing a low-life negative tick. MapSense fingerprints the strict unique 32-byte entry plus the unique 36-byte type-branch/layout witness at 0x34B461 in both its monster-marker and POI current-level chains before calling the function.

entries.name: DUNGEON_IsRoomInTown
entries.notes: Null-safe room predicate that follows room+0x18 to the DRLG room and returns the level-record Town field through 0x360FC0. Its use in the stat-regeneration callback matches the D2MOO semantic implementation. RemoteStash 0.2.26 leaves this prologue untouched for Prevent Merc Death in Town and redirects only its four proven client call sites through a near relay. MapSense 0.9.3 validates its strict 16-byte prologue before using it to publish an explicitly empty navigation batch in town.

entries.name: EVENT_SetEvent
entries.notes: Schedules a unit event with observed native Windows x64 ABI void (game, unit, eventType, expireFrame, customId, customParam, arg7). The semantics of arg7 remain unproven. After sub rsp,0x48, the prologue reads incoming stack arguments 5, 6 and 7 at rsp+0x70, rsp+0x78 and rsp+0x80, inserts the internal callback argument and calls the timer initializer at 0x48BE80. Its strict unique 32-byte entry signature is 48 83 EC 48 8B 84 24 80 00 00 00 89 44 24 38 8B 44 24 78 89 44 24 30 8B 44 24 70 89 44 24 28 48. The player and monster stat-regeneration callsites at 0x42E634 and 0x448CA0 schedule event type 3 at game frame plus one. D2MOO's six-argument prototype is semantic evidence only and does not describe the native D2R ABI.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x77_Ui
entries.notes: Builds the two-byte server UI packet 0x77 with ABI (client, uiAction) and queues it for the client. The bank operation caller at 0x52829C passes action 0x10 (UPDATEUI_OPENSTASH); a second caller at 0x5809E1 passes 0x14. Its exact 16-byte entry signature 40 57 48 83 EC 40 C6 44 24 50 77 48 8B F9 88 54 is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_InteractWithEntity
entries.notes: Network receive callback with ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32. It requires a 9-byte interaction packet whose payload contains unit type at +1 and GUID at +5, then validates the target and interaction path. Its exact 23-byte prologue is unique. A runtime hook did not fire during a normal integrated local stash opening, proving this receive callback is not itself the local UI trigger.

entries.name: OBJECTS_OperateFunction32_Bank
entries.notes: Bank object operation handler with probable ABI (operation, operateMode) -> int32. It rejects a non-neutral stash object, resolves the player client through SUNIT_GetClientFromPlayer 0x48FDE0, and sends UI action 0x10 through D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x77_Ui 0x480650 before returning success. Its exact 18-byte entry signature 40 53 48 83 EC 20 48 8B D9 48 8B 49 08 E8 DE 28 E2 FF is unique. Static identity is high-confidence; a planned runtime entry hit was blocked before game entry by the official offline-login validation.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetTransactionCost
entries.notes: Public transaction-cost entry that tail-jumps to the implementation at 0x36F0C0. The client individual-repair quote at 0x10CD5F and authoritative server individual-repair path at 0x540277 pass repair transaction type 3 through this entry.

entries.name: ITEMS_CalculateTransactionCost
entries.notes: Shared transaction-cost implementation with proven x64 ABI (player, item, difficulty, questFlags, vendorId, transactionType) -> int32. Repair All calls it directly at 0x3754CB; RepairCostsCap 1.4.0 hooks its unique 29-byte prologue for transaction type 3 and applies the single non-increasing maximumGold cap, where zero makes the repair free.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetAllRepairCosts
entries.notes: Iterates body locations 0 through 12, tests repairability and durability or charged-skill state, calls 0x36F0C0 with transaction type 3, totals each returned cost and invokes an optional per-item callback. Its x64 ABI is (game, player, vendorId, difficulty, questFlags, callback) -> int32 and its strict 33-byte prologue is unique. RepairCostsCap 1.4.0 hooks it so the same maximumGold setting caps the final Repair All total for the two UI callers and two authoritative server passes.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_RepairItem
entries.notes: Common server-side repair routine with proven x64 ABI (game, item, player) -> void. The individual handler calls it at 0x5402C7; Repair All supplies its 0x5413F0 jump stub as the callback at 0x53FFC1. It repairs quantity, charges, broken state and physical durability, then synchronizes the affected stat with the player client. RepairCostsCap 1.4.0 hooks its unique 32-byte prologue for post-success permanent durability wear independently of whether the repair price is free.

entries.name: D2GAME_SetItemStatAndNotifyClient
entries.notes: Sets an item stat through STATLIST_SetUnitStat and, when the supplied client is non-null, sends the matching stat update packet. Proven x64 ABI: (item, client, sendUpdate, statId, value, layer) -> void. The vanilla repair routine uses it for quantity stat 70 and durability stat 72; RepairCostsCap reuses it for maximum durability stat 73 and current durability stat 72.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetMaxDurabilityFromUnit
entries.notes: Returns an item's effective maximum durability. The common repair routine calls it at 0x53BC08 before restoring durability, matching the pinned D2MOO semantic reference without transposing its legacy address or ABI.

entries.name: UNITS_GetSeed
entries.notes: Confirmed-static accessor returning the native seed pair at unit+0x28. RepairCostsCap uses the repaired item's seed. Mechanics 2.0 proves Critical/Deadly, monster critical, Event15/16/20 and the leech-overlay choice all call this accessor, then inline their own LCG/modulo sequence; this RVA is not a shared callable random-roll primitive.

entries.name: SEED_RollLimitedRandomNumber
entries.notes: Advances the supplied native seed and returns a value in [0, upperBound). Its strict 32-byte prefix is governed. RepairCostsCap rolls over 10000 basis points; ProgressiveAffixesPlugin calls it once per configured Rare or Crafted count selection using the exact integer-weight total.

entries.name: SUNIT_GetClientFromPlayer
entries.notes: Returns the client pointer for a player unit and safely returns null for a null or non-player unit. The vanilla repair routine calls it before stat synchronization; RepairCostsCap reuses it after successful wear.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_RepairHandler
entries.notes: Authoritative Repair All handler. It first calls 0x375330 without a callback, compares the total with the client request, validates carried and bank gold, debits nonzero cost, then calls 0x375330 again with the vanilla repair callback before returning success.

entries.name: RepairAllZeroCostCallbackBranch
entries.notes: Vanilla JE skips both debit and the second Repair All callback pass when total cost is zero. When its repair policy is enabled, RepairCostsCap 1.4.0 validates the unique 16-byte context at 0x53FF65 and changes only the displacement byte at 0x53FF70 from 0x6F to 0x21 so maximumGold=0 skips debit but still reaches the callback setup at 0x53FF92.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_GetVendorChainEntry
entries.notes: Resolves an NPC class id, then tail-calls the vendor-chain lookup at 0x502BB0. Proven x64 ABI: (game, npc, indexOut) -> VendorChainEntry*. FillStoreInventory and the store-opening dispatcher call it directly; the lookup walks D2GameStrc+0x3838 in 0x78-byte entries and compares the 16-bit NPC id at +0x00.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_ClearVendorInventory
entries.notes: Authoritative normal-vendor cleanup with proven x64 ABI (game, vendorEntry, npc) -> void. Its sole caller at 0x540952 executes only when VendorChainEntry+0x35 requests a refresh. It removes and synchronizes the current store inventory, clears the filled flag at +0x34 and timestamp at +0x38, then updates the NPC through 0x540AA0 before FillStoreInventory runs at 0x540960.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_UpdateVendorRefreshState
entries.notes: Walks the 0x78-byte vendor chain, filters entries by the compiled NPC vendor group, and maintains normal-store refresh state. In its timed path, GetTickCount64 greater than VendorChainEntry+0x38 plus 0x3A980 (240000 ms) sets the refresh-pending byte at +0x35 and stores the new timestamp. Two direct callers at 0x502DEB and 0x502EE2 prove the server maintenance path.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_FillStoreInventory
entries.notes: Authoritative normal-store fill with proven x64 ABI (game, player, npc) -> void and one direct caller at 0x540960. It resolves the NPC's VendorChainEntry, writes GetTickCount64 to +0x38, generates random normal/magic stock from the 12-byte cache entries at +0x40/+0x48 and regenerates permanent item codes from +0x58/+0x60 through D2GAME_NPC_GenerateStoreItem. The pinned plugin-items hook owns this canonical entry.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_GenerateStoreItem
entries.notes: Creates one server-side vendor item for the supplied NPC, item code, game, quality, item level and player level. Three direct callers belong to the normal-store fill path. The pinned plugin-items implementation calls this exact entry for random and permanent stock and validates its build-specific address before installing the FillStoreInventory hook.

entries.name: D2GAME_STORES_FillGamble
entries.notes: Authoritative gamble fill reached from the store-opening dispatcher at 0x540913 only for interface type 3. This is distinct from normal-store cleanup at 0x502F00 and fill at 0x53C9F0. Its generation loop contains the separately governed GambleScreenGenerationLimitImmediate at 0x541A7E.

entries.name: CLIENT_SendNineByteCommandPacket
entries.notes: Builds the current 92777 client command layout {opcode:u8, action:u32, targetGuid:u32} and submits exactly nine bytes through CLIENT_QueueOutgoingPacket 0xEE2A0. Proven x64 ABI: (opcode byte, action dword, targetGuid dword) -> void. Twenty-six direct references include the vendor entity-action callers; its 48-byte entry signature is pinned by VendorStockRefresh 0.1.1.

entries.name: CLIENT_GetVendorPanelGambleMode
entries.notes: Returns the client gamble-state global used by VendorPanel configuration at 0x241240. A nonzero result stores panel mode 2 at panel+0x168. VendorStockRefresh uses this native predicate so RefreshAll keeps vanilla action 2 in gamble and selects its private VSRF marker only for a normal vendor panel.

entries.name: CLIENT_SendVendorRefreshAction
entries.notes: Loads the current NPC GUID, sets entity action 2 and tail-calls CLIENT_SendNineByteCommandPacket with opcode 0x38. Its exact 19-byte body is unique and it has exactly two references, both in the vendor panel: the direct input path at 0x240E82 and the VendorPanelMessage:RefreshAll branch at 0x241D79.

entries.name: VendorRefreshInputModeGuard
entries.notes: Unique 23-byte vendor-panel input guard requiring panel+0x168 mode 2 before the direct refresh path reaches CLIENT_SendVendorRefreshAction. The vendor configuration uses both modes 0 and 1 for normal NPC classes: Charsi hcIdx 154 selects jump-table entry 1 and reaches the explicit mode-1 store at 0x2412DE. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 leaves this vanilla direct-input guard intact; the reused native button still emits VendorPanelMessage:RefreshAll, while CLIENT_GetVendorPanelGambleMode distinguishes vanilla gamble action 2 from the private normal-vendor VSRF marker.

entries.name: VendorRefreshButtonEnableModeGate
entries.notes: First of two unique, adjacent mode gates applied to the only widget enabled exclusively in vendor panel mode 2. The governed layout proves this widget is the original button_refresh. Charsi hcIdx 154 resolves through the native jump table to panel mode 1 at 0x2412DE, disproving the earlier assumption that mode 1 was a separate repair screen. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 preserves this vanilla predicate and overrides the same widget only after UI_VendorPanel_Configure returns in a normal vendor panel.

entries.name: VendorRefreshButtonVisibilityModeGate
entries.notes: Second unique mode gate for the native button_refresh widget, paired with the enable gate at 0x24137D through the widget vtable +0x50 method. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 preserves this vanilla mode-2 visibility gate, then applies the same enabled/visible methods to button_refresh only when CLIENT_GetVendorPanelGambleMode is zero.

entries.name: UI_VendorPanel_HandleMessage
entries.notes: Vendor-panel message handler with ABI (panel, message) -> void. The branch comparing hash 0xB7AA1748D66EFCAF performs panel cleanup through 0x241EF0 and tail-calls CLIENT_SendVendorRefreshAction, proving the VendorPanelMessage:RefreshAll route declared by button_refresh.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_EntityAction
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback with ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32. It requires the current nine-byte opcode-0x38 payload, resolves and validates the NPC, checks act and proximity, then routes action 1 normal store and action 2 gamble through the common store dispatcher 0x540850. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.1 hooks its unique 21-byte prologue to translate only the private VSRF marker into action 1 before forwarding to all vanilla validation. The legacy D2MOO 13-byte packet layout does not apply to build 92777.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_ConfigureVendorInteraction
entries.notes: Configures the player's vendor session immediately before the common store dispatcher. Proven x64 ABI: (game, npc, player, mode byte) -> void. It reads and replaces PlayerData+0x100, where callers pass mode 2 normal store, 3 gamble and 4 hire, and stores the NPC class at +0xFC. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.0's old-session discriminator failed its first gameplay witness; 0.1.1 arms refresh state only inside the thread-local scope established by its validated VSRF entity-action callback.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetDisplayName
entries.notes: Resolves the localized display name for a unit, including the ItemsTxt name-string path for UNIT_ITEM. UI_BuildGroundItemTooltip calls it directly in the proven 92777 ground-label chain.

entries.name: UI_BuildGroundItemTooltip
entries.notes: Builds the bounded ground-label text and color using the ABI (unit, textBuffer, bufferSize, colorCode). Its sole direct caller at 0x1FAA18 belongs to the remastered ground-label record builder.

entries.name: GroundItemLabelRecordLimit
entries.notes: First site in the coupled 92777 limit set. The renderer clamps or pads its dynamic vector to 32 records of size 0x144; the associated byte offset at 0x1516ECE and fill count at 0x1516F41 must be patched together.

entries.name: GroundItemLabelLayoutListLimit
entries.notes: Normalizes the synchronized ground-label layout list to 32 nodes. GroundItemLabelLimit validates and patches this comparison plus the coupled sites at 0x1519A4F, 0x1519AAA and 0x1519AF9.

entries.name: CLIENT_HandleUiPacket77
entries.notes: Registered at runtime as the handler for opcode 0x77 with an exact packet length of two bytes. The registration table is proven by the adjacent 0x9C and 0x9D handlers and its 24-byte-per-opcode stride. This entry tail-jumps to CLIENT_ApplyUiPacket77 at 0x1F0AB0. RemoteStash 0.1.0 calls it on the UI thread with the native packet {0x77,0x10}; this proves only the local client panel action, not an authoritative server bank session.

entries.name: CLIENT_ApplyUiPacket77
entries.notes: Consumes the action byte at packet+1. Action 0x10 follows the native open-stash UI branch and action 0x14 follows its separate UI branch. The exact 32-byte entry signature is pinned by RemoteStash 0.1.0 before the wrapper at 0x12DBC0 can be called.

entries.name: UI_ApplyInterfaceModeTransition
entries.notes: Observed x64 ABI (int32 mode, bool transitionFlag) -> void at a unique 20-byte entry signature. The state dispatcher at 0xC1E80 calls it as (2, true) from the unique callsite 0xC1F01 on the native stash-state 0x18 branch. RemoteStash 1.1.6 redirects only that callsite and, only inside a bounded hotkey-open scope, forwards (2, false). The exact behavioral meaning of transitionFlag remains gameplay-gated, so the semantic name and confidence remain provisional.

entries.name: CLIENT_ResetMouseButtonState
entries.notes: Zeroes six client input globals and returns. Their consumers at 0x8B989, 0x8BA1F, 0x8BB30 and 0x8B007 route held mouse-button actions into the local-player input dispatcher. UI_ApplyInterfaceLayoutMode at 0xB9C20 tail-jumps here for both the native stash-open layout transition and the state-1 inventory-close transition. RemoteStash 1.1.9 hooks the unique strict 32-byte entry and suppresses it only inside the thread-local hotkey-open scope, extended through the immediate companion-inventory close. The exact individual meaning of all six globals remains provisional.

entries.name: CLIENT_ResetMouseButtonStateWithFinalize
entries.notes: Reads the current local input-context index, zeroes the same six client mouse-input globals as CLIENT_ResetMouseButtonState 0x8D510, sets two additional state globals to 0x10, then tail-jumps to 0xF15C0 to finalize the indexed input context. Its strict first 32 bytes are unique in build 92777 and it has 16 direct xrefs. RemoteStash 1.1.11 preserves the native function and its finalizer, but snapshots and restores only the six shared mouse-input globals when this entry is reached inside the exact thread-local hotkey-open transition. The individual semantic names of the six globals and the complete role of 0xF15C0 remain provisional.

entries.name: UI_CloseActiveInterfaceStates
entries.notes: Builds a temporary list of active UI-state identifiers and closes each entry through UI_CloseInterfaceState at 0xC84C6. Runtime capture during a click-to-move action proves the call chain 0x102590 -> 0xC8240 -> 0xC84C6. The observed x64 arguments are two integer or boolean mode values, but their complete semantic meaning remains provisional.

entries.name: WorldActionCloseActiveInterfacesCall
entries.notes: Exact E8 AB 5C FC FF call to UI_CloseActiveInterfaceStates. A RemoteStash 1.1.7 runtime stack capture proved this callsite as the close cascade reached when clicking the world to move while both remote stash state 0x18 and inventory state 1 are open. RemoteStash redirects only this callsite and uses a thread-local scope so only the movement-driven inventory close is suppressed; explicit inventory hotkey and close-button paths remain native.

entries.name: UI_OpenInterfaceState
entries.notes: Opens or refreshes a native UI state with observed x64 ABI (int32 state, bool secondary) -> bool. The entry indexes the UI-state byte array with the signed state argument, validates the transition, and dispatches the state-specific UI message. Its strict 68-byte prologue is unique in build 92777. Direct callers pass state 1 for inventory, while CLIENT_ApplyUiPacket77 opens the stash with state 0x18. RemoteStash 1.1.3 proved that suppressing state 1 before native composition leaves a broken desktop shell. RemoteStash 1.1.5 instead delegates every open first; after a successful remote state 0x18 open, a bounded one-shot hotkey ticket may close the companion state 1 through UI_CloseInterfaceState. No native open is suppressed.

entries.name: UI_InterfaceStateTable
entries.notes: Governed array of 32 native UI-state bytes. UI_OpenInterfaceState reads state[RBX] at 0xCD7FB, UI_ToggleInterfaceState reads the same indexed byte at 0xCDE3C, and UI_CloseInterfaceState first proves RBX < 0x20 then writes zero at 0xC7DF1. These three independent instruction-aligned witnesses all encode RVA 0x2A2ADA0. MapSense 0.13.2 reads only a copied 32-byte snapshot and suppresses every MapSense-owned pixel and input bound when a modal/panel state is active; it neither hooks nor writes this table.

entries.name: UI_OpenInterfaceStateTableReadWitness
entries.notes: Exact nine-byte MOVZX at UI_OpenInterfaceState+0x3B reading byte ptr [moduleBase + state + 0x2A2ADA0]. MapSense fingerprints this internal witness instead of the function prologue, which RemoteStash may legitimately own through an inline hook in the complete plugin stack.

entries.name: UI_CloseInterfaceStateTableWriteWitness
entries.notes: Exact 19-byte sequence comparing the signed state index to 0x20, rejecting out-of-range values, then writing zero to UI_InterfaceStateTable[state]. It proves the 32-entry bound and byte semantics consumed read-only by MapSense.

entries.name: UI_ToggleInterfaceStateTableReadWitness
entries.notes: Exact nine-byte MOVZX at UI_ToggleInterfaceState+0x3C independently reading byte ptr [moduleBase + state + 0x2A2ADA0]. It cross-checks the table address without consuming or conflicting with RemoteStash's hookable UI-state entrypoints.

entries.name: UI_ToggleInterfaceState
entries.notes: Toggles an existing native UI state with observed x64 ABI (int32 state, bool secondary) -> bool. The strict 68-byte entry is unique in build 92777, preserves the state identifier in EBX and the secondary byte in R15B, then calls the shared transition guard at 0xD00B0 with operation 2 before applying the state-specific UI transition. Static disassembly distinguishes this existing-panel route from UI_OpenInterfaceState 0xCD7C0. Gameplay 1.2.7 proves this hook is reached for Inventory state 1 and can scope held-click preservation while Inventory opens beside RemoteStash; Quest, Character and Waypoint use other callers of the shared guard.

entries.name: UI_PanelCompatibilityCloseStateCall
entries.notes: Unique E8 33 77 FF FF call to UI_CloseInterfaceState 0xC7D30 inside the shared transition guard entered by Close, Open and Toggle interface-state operations. After the native compatibility matrix accepts a transition, the guard scans the 32 UI states; for each active state whose matrix relation is close-before-open and when the transition flag permits it, this exact call closes that state. Gameplay 1.2.8 proves that Character, Skills, Quest and Waypoint do not reach this close while RemoteStash remains active, so this callsite is not their pre-transition convergence.

entries.name: UI_SelectManagedPanelState
entries.notes: Selects an interface state from a panel-owned list with observed x64 ABI (panelGroup, int32 requestedState) -> void. The entry scans count at panelGroup+0x188 and state identifiers at panelGroup+0x168, then enters the shared selector at 0x27F2F0 with the resolved index. That selector closes the previously selected state through UI_CloseInterfaceState at 0x27F35C and opens the requested state through UI_OpenInterfaceState at 0x27F416. Direct build-92777 callers pass Character 2, Skills 4 and Quest 0x0E. Its strict 17-byte entry signature is unique. Gameplay with RemoteStash 1.2.9 proves this function is not the live convergence for Character, Skills, Quest or Waypoint replacement, so the experimental hook was removed.

entries.name: UI_GeneralPanelTeardownCloseStashCall
entries.notes: Unique E8 32 D3 E9 FF call to UI_CloseInterfaceState 0xC7D30 in function 0x22A7E0. The caller sets ECX to stash state 0x18 and EDX to false, then immediately closes states 0x19 and 0x0B as part of a general panel teardown. Runtime instrumentation in RemoteStash 1.2.9 observed return RVA 0x22A9FE for the stash close requested when native panels attempted to replace the remote stash. RemoteStash 1.2.10 permits this exact close only outside the thread-local movement-close scope.

entries.name: UI_PlayerInventory_RefreshGoldControls
entries.notes: PlayerInventoryPanel refresh method with ABI (panel) -> void. It resolves gold_amount and gold_button through UI_FindChildWidgetByName, refreshes the displayed bank-gold value and applies the native gold-button state. RemoteStash 0.1.0 hooks its strict 32-byte prologue, calls the original first, then measures the active panel, grid, footer and private button for fail-closed dynamic placement.

entries.name: UI_ButtonWidget_OnClick
entries.notes: Generic ButtonWidget click handler with probable ABI (button, inputMessage) -> void. Runtime type metadata proves onClickMessage at button+0x558; the handler dispatches that embedded message at 0x8F1069. RemoteStash 0.1.0 hooks the strict 32-byte prologue and consumes only hash 0x055A7CEA95897DC9 for PlayerInventoryPanelMessage:RemoteStash, forwarding every other button unchanged.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetDimensions
entries.notes: Returns an item's one-byte width and height through the proven x64 ABI (item, widthOut, heightOut, sourceFile, sourceLine) -> void. INVENTORY_FindFreePosition calls it before choosing a scan direction; CubeQuickMove pins its 32-byte prologue and uses it only after the vanilla Cube search succeeds.

entries.name: D2GAME_ServerPacketCallbackTable
entries.notes: Base of the authoritative 256-entry server packet callback table, with one eight-byte function pointer per opcode. Runtime captures prove slots 0x01-0x12 point respectively to 0x4AC050, 0x4ACE20, 0x4ACE40, 0x4ACE60, 0x4ACE80, 0x4ACF80, 0x4AD030, 0x4AD0E0, 0x4AD100, 0x4AD120, 0x4AD140, 0x4AD230, 0x4AD330, 0x4AD3E0, 0x4AD490, 0x4AD4B0, 0x4AD4D0 and 0x4AD4F0 on build 92777. PotionAutoPickup 1.1.1 validates every pointer before redirecting those player-action slots; slot 0x16 remains the vanilla pickup callback at 0x4B9DF0.

entries.name: INVENTORY_GetFreeBeltSlot
entries.notes: Chooses a free belt cell with proven x64 ABI (inventory, item, freeSlotOut, allowAnyBeltable) -> int32. The automatic ground-pickup helper calls it at 0x471C31. Its strict 32-byte prologue is unique in build 92777. PotionAutoPickup 1.1.1 hooks it only inside a thread-local scope bound to the exact inventory and ground item selected by the plugin.

entries.name: InventoryPlayerHeightPlacementGate
entries.notes: The exact bytes 40 80 FE 01 compare the item height with one inside INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Equality calls the bottom-right weighted search at 0x38D8F0; other heights continue into the player top-left path. CubeQuickMove does not patch this shared branch.

entries.name: INVENTORY_ResolveOccupancyGrid
entries.notes: Resolves the temporary occupancy grid used by free-position searches with ABI (inventory, gridIndex, gridInfo) -> occupancyGrid. The Cube caller supplies native page 3, so INVENTORY_FindFreePosition passes grid index 5. INVENTORY_GetFreeBeltSlot passes grid index 1 with the static belt grid info at 0x237B638; the resulting grid exposes width at +0x10, height at +0x11 and the cell item-pointer array at +0x18.

entries.name: INVENTORY_SearchBottomRightWeighted
entries.notes: Native bottom-right-to-top-left weighted placement search with ABI (inventory, occupancyGrid, freeXOut, freeYOut, widthByte, heightByte) -> int32. Its only vanilla xref is the height-equals-one branch at 0x386754. CubeQuickMove 0.1.0 reused it for taller Cube items, but that design was retired after the first gameplay witness failed; 0.1.1 scans the resolved occupancy grid directly.

entries.name: INVENTORY_BuildGridContext
entries.notes: Builds the 24-byte temporary Inventory.txt grid descriptor consumed by INVENTORY_ResolveOccupancyGrid with ABI (itemDataContextByte, inventoryRecordId, reservedZero, gridContextOut) -> void. The exact call sequence is proven inside INVENTORY_FindFreePosition and INVENTORY_AutoSortPlanner. Descriptor width and height are the bytes at +0 and +1; +0x10 and +0x11 belong to the separately resolved occupancy-grid layout and must not be read from this descriptor.

entries.name: CubeAutomaticFindFreePositionCall_0FA33D
entries.notes: Automatic placement call E8 6E C2 28 00 to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Its caller writes the sixth page argument as native Cube page 3 with C6 44 24 28 03. CubeQuickMove 0.1.2 owned this five-byte call; 0.1.3 retains it in the 27-site page-3-capable set.

entries.name: CubeAutomaticFindFreePositionCall_2C7306
entries.notes: Automatic placement call E8 A5 F2 0B 00 to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Its caller writes the sixth page argument as native Cube page 3 with C6 44 24 28 03. CubeQuickMove 0.1.2 owned this five-byte call; 0.1.3 retains it in the 27-site page-3-capable set.

entries.name: CubeAutomaticFindFreePositionCall_471D62
entries.notes: Automatic placement call E8 49 48 F1 FF to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Its caller writes the sixth page argument as native Cube page 3 with C6 44 24 28 03. CubeQuickMove 0.1.2 owned this five-byte call; 0.1.3 retains it in the 27-site page-3-capable set.

entries.name: CubeIndirectMoveFindFreePositionCall
entries.notes: Unique E8 38 AB EC FF signature in one indirect Cube-transfer path after base-code box validation, native page 3 selection and inventory-grid resolution. The proven substituted ABI is (inventory, item, inventoryRecordId, freeXOut, freeYOut, pageByte) -> int32 and returns at 0x4BBA78. CubeQuickMove 0.1.2 owned it among eight explicit page-3 calls; 0.1.3 retains it in the 27-site page-3-capable set.

entries.name: CubePacket15FindFreePositionCall
entries.notes: Automatic Cube placement call E8 D5 43 EC FF to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition inside the 0x15-byte packet parser beginning at 0x4C2050. The caller resolves inventory grid page 3 and writes page argument 3 explicitly. Runtime counters disproved it as the reported 0.1.2 equipped-sword path. CubeQuickMove 0.1.3 retains it in the 27-site page-3-capable set.

entries.name: CubeAutomaticFindFreePositionCall_4F2C8B
entries.notes: Automatic placement call E8 20 39 E9 FF to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Its caller writes the sixth page argument as native Cube page 3 with C6 44 24 28 03. CubeQuickMove 0.1.2 owned this five-byte call; 0.1.3 retains it in the 27-site page-3-capable set.

entries.name: CubeAutomaticFindFreePositionCall_527DC2
entries.notes: Automatic placement call E8 E9 E7 E5 FF to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Its caller writes the sixth page argument as native Cube page 3 with C6 44 24 28 03. CubeQuickMove 0.1.2 owned this five-byte call; 0.1.3 retains it in the 27-site page-3-capable set.

entries.name: CubeAutomaticFindFreePositionCall_528053
entries.notes: Automatic placement call E8 58 E5 E5 FF to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Its caller writes the sixth page argument as native Cube page 3 with C6 44 24 28 03. CubeQuickMove 0.1.2 owned this five-byte call; 0.1.3 retains it in the 27-site page-3-capable set.

entries.name: UI_DynamicPageFindFreePositionCall
entries.notes: Client availability call E8 4F C3 22 00 to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. The helper preserves its page argument in r14b and writes it as the sixth argument; UI_CanQuickMoveItemToCube calls the helper with native Cube page 3 at 0x15A2BB-0x15A2BD. CubeQuickMove 0.1.3 observed this site at runtime for a 1x3 item.

entries.name: UI_QuickMovePlacementFindFreePositionCall
entries.notes: Gameplay-proven client placement call to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition inside the routine beginning at 0x15F8B0. The routine copies the returned x/y pair into its placement output before emitting packet 0x54. The 0.1.3 equipped-sword witness observed native Cube page 3, outgoing coordinates 4,3, accepted transfer result 1 and Vincent's visible 1x3 placement at the bottom-right.

entries.name: ServerDynamicPageFindFreePositionCall
entries.notes: Server placement call E8 9D A9 E8 FF to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. The enclosing branch selects native page 0 or 3 dynamically, consumes both output coordinates, then calls ITEMS_PlaceItemForPlayer at 0x4FBD90. The gameplay probe identified 0x15F94F plus packet handler 0x4C2050 for the reported equipped-sword action, so 0x4FBC0E is not that action's current runtime witness.

entries.name: UI_BankCube_UpdateControls
entries.notes: Integrated stash/Cube control update with proven x64 ABI (controller) -> void. The panel root is controller+0x2A0; the function resolves horadriccube_grid, convert and horadriccube_cover through UI_FindChildWidgetByName, then applies native enabled and visible state through widget vtable slots +0x48/+0x50. TransmuteHotkey pins the strict 32-byte prologue, calls the original first and considers only the same panel's visible enabled convert button.

entries.name: UI_HoradricCube_UpdatePanel
entries.notes: Standalone Horadric Cube panel update with proven x64 ABI (panel) -> void. It resolves grid, flourish and convert, updates native widget state and tail-calls the base update path. TransmuteHotkey pins the strict 32-byte entry beginning at 0x2CDA90 despite the wider unwind range beginning at 0x2CDA80, calls the original first and dispatches only the embedded message of the same panel's visible enabled convert button.

entries.name: UI_FindTopLevelPanelByName
entries.notes: Finds a top-level panel by UTF-8 name with proven x64 ABI (const char* name) -> panel*. The 22-byte wrapper forwards the name and the global UI manager to 0x89F760 or returns null. TransmuteHotkey validates the wrapper and uses it only on the UI thread to refuse ChatPanel and known text-entry or confirmation modals.

entries.name: UI_IsHoradricCubePage
entries.notes: Recognizes native inventory page 3 as the Horadric Cube in the quick-move eligibility path. The corresponding D2R 2.4 helper is at 0x130DC0. EquippedItemToCube leaves this helper unchanged.

entries.name: UI_CanQuickMoveItemToCube
entries.notes: Central Cube quick-move eligibility helper. It validates the relevant panels, calls UI_IsHoradricCubePage, excludes the Cube item itself and keeps the native destination-space and transaction path. EquippedItemToCube does not patch this function.

entries.name: UI_HandleEquippedItemQuickMove
entries.notes: Hovered/equipped-item quick-move handler. It resolves the hovered unit, evaluates a new 3.2 client guard at 0x228B91, tests Ctrl at 0x228B9E and then reuses the native Cube eligibility and item-move path. The corresponding 2.4 handler lacks the new conditional exit.

entries.name: EquippedItemCubeEligibilityGuardBranch
entries.notes: Exact six-byte 0F 84 55 01 00 00 conditional exit introduced before the native Ctrl test in build 92777. EquippedItemToCube owns only 0x228B98..0x228B9D and replaces this branch with six NOPs after validating the 47-byte context at 0x228B81.

entries.name: OBJECTS_OperateFunction06_TowerTome
entries.notes: Build-92777 Tower Tome server handler with ABI (operation, operateMode) -> int32; the second argument is unused. The operation structure is observed at +0x00 game, +0x08 object, +0x10 player and +0x20 object class id. It rejects animation modes above 2, resolves quest 5, requires the quest intro gate, starts the operating animation and ENDANIM event, sends scroll string id 127 through QUESTS_SendScrollMessage, then advances the A1Q5 quest state. Its extended entry signature through both the animation-mode and quest-data calls is unique. D2MOO 1.10f is semantic evidence only; the 92777 control flow and data accesses independently prove the identity.

entries.name: QUESTS_SendScrollMessage
entries.notes: Authoritative server helper with ABI (game, player, unit, uint16 stringId) -> void. It resolves the player's client, builds the 0x28-byte server packet 0x27 as {header 0x27, unitType 2, unitGuid, one-message list, stringId}, and queues it through 0x47E340. Direct callers are 0x547DA6, 0x59EF50 and Tower Tome at 0x5DC61E. Its strict 30-byte prologue is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: QUESTS_GetQuestData
entries.notes: Resolves a server quest record with ABI (game, questId) -> questData*. It walks the quest chain rooted at game+0x21D8 and compares the requested id. Tower Tome calls it with quest id 5. Its strict 41-byte signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetObjectsTxtRecordCount
entries.notes: Returns dataTables+0x1530 with ABI (uint8 dataContext) -> int32. MapSense calls it before DATATBLS_GetObjectsTxtRecord so every waypoint object class id is bounds-checked. Its strict 20-byte signature 48 83 EC 28 E8 17 0E F7 FF 8B 80 30 15 00 00 48 83 C4 28 C3 is unique in the governed corpus.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetObjectsTxtRecord
entries.notes: Returns the compiled ObjectsTxt record with ABI (dataContext, objectClassId) -> ObjectsTxt*. It resolves the context data tables through 0x300A90, bounds the id against dataTables+0x1530, uses the record base at +0x1528 and a record size of 0x168. Tower Tome reads frame count at record+0x9C. Its strict 36-byte signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: CLIENT_HandleScrollMessagePacket27
entries.notes: Client handler for the server 0x27 message-list packet with ABI (packet) -> void. For unit type 2 and ordinary menu 0 it stores the object GUID from +0x02, reads the 16-bit string id from +0x0A and calls CLIENT_ShowScrollMessageById at 0x197BF0. The alternate menu-3 branch performs the direct LANG_GetStringById lookup. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: CLIENT_ShowScrollMessageById
entries.notes: Creates the native scrolling-lore UI with ABI (uint16 stringId) -> void. It resolves the active-language UTF-8 text through LANG_GetStringById 0x5F4A50, builds the scroll widgets and marks the known lore ids including Tower Tome id 127. Its sole direct caller is CLIENT_HandleScrollMessagePacket27 at 0x19A801. A strict 64-byte signature including cookie setup, local context and initialization calls is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: ScrollMessageLocalizationCall
entries.notes: The sole LANG_GetStringById call inside CLIENT_ShowScrollMessageById. Exact bytes E8 EC CD 45 00 target 0x5F4A50 in build 92777. BookOfLore 0.2.0 validates the enclosing scroll function, the language resolver entry and this call before redirecting only this site through a near relay; it deliberately leaves the global localization prologue unhooked for PluginPack coexistence.

entries.name: CLIENT_TransferItemToInventoryPage
entries.notes: Computes a native free position and emits the 21-byte client inventory-transfer packet 0x54 with proven x64 ABI (item, owner, destinationPage, option, source, placementOut) -> bool. The strict 32-byte entry is pinned by EquippedItemToCube 0.2.0. RemoteStash 0.2.26 leaves this prologue untouched and redirects its eight direct D2R.exe callers through a near relay. For destination page 3, CubeQuickMove may redirect its INVENTORY_FindFreePosition call at 0x15F94F, and the returned x/y pair is copied both to placementOut and packet offsets +17/+19.

entries.name: UI_ButtonWidgetDispatchMessageCall
entries.notes: Exact E8 22 2D F5 FF call to UI_DispatchMessage immediately after lea rcx,[rdi+0x558] in UI_ButtonWidget_OnClick. RemoteStash 0.2.26 redirects only this call so plugin-skills remains free to own the dispatcher entry.

entries.name: UI_QueueStyledTextLayout
entries.notes: Queues one 0x2E8-byte styled-text layout record in the component vector at +0x168 with ABI (component, text, requestedRect, style, secondaryText) -> void. UI_DrawStyledText calls it at 0x843D87 after resolving the text component. Extended Item Stats hooks its strict 32-byte prologue, scopes itself to the active paged item-tooltip text, and expands only that record to the native width measured from the complete item's widest affix.

entries.name: UI_MeasureStyledText
entries.notes: Measures styled UTF-8 text with ABI (text, style, widthHeightOut, uiScale, limits) -> void. UI_RecalculateTextLayout calls it at 0x8DAD3F and 0x8DAE87 and stores the returned width and height in the layout record. Extended Item Stats measures each complete-tooltip line separately to avoid the native oversized-allocation failure while determining a stable maximum width.

entries.name: UI_GetScale
entries.notes: Returns the current UI scale as float. The styled-text layout path calls it immediately before both measurement and rendering. Extended Item Stats passes the same native scale to UI_MeasureStyledText.

entries.name: UI_GetNativeWidth
entries.notes: Returns the native UI width used by UI_QueueStyledTextLayout to construct its clamping rectangle. The paired height getter is 0x7F4A0.

entries.name: UI_GetNativeHeight
entries.notes: Returns the native UI height used by UI_QueueStyledTextLayout to construct its clamping rectangle. The paired width getter is 0x7F510.

entries.name: UI_ClampTextLayoutToRect
entries.notes: Clamps a styled-text layout record's primary and secondary origins to an x/y/width/height rectangle. UI_QueueStyledTextLayout calls it at 0x8802A2 after constructing native screen bounds. Extended Item Stats reuses it after widening the active item-tooltip record so the fixed frame remains on screen.

entries.name: CLIENT_SendTwentyOneByteCommandPacket
entries.notes: Builds a packed 21-byte client command from (opcode byte, five uint32 fields) and submits it through CLIENT_QueueOutgoingPacket. The native client path at 0x1141AB calls it with opcode 0x34 after computing the Cain identify-all transaction. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_ShiftRightClickPlaceAction
entries.notes: Native item action with observed ABI (item, owner, page, flag, state) -> void and three direct callers. UI_InventorySlotWidget_HandleClick calls it at 0x2C7D54 only after the mouse-state right branch and native VK_SHIFT test. The MassID 0.1.4 witness proved that this modern-panel action is not reached by the player's active legacy inventory panel, so 0.1.5 leaves it intact. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_ShiftRightClickQuickMoveAction
entries.notes: Native item action with observed ABI (widget, item) -> void. Its only direct caller is UI_InventorySlotWidget_HandleClick at 0x2C7D1A after the mouse-state right branch and native VK_SHIFT test. The MassID 0.1.4 witness proved that this modern-panel action is not reached by the player's active legacy inventory panel, so 0.1.5 leaves it intact. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_LegacyInventoryTooltipAppenderMoveCallA
entries.notes: Exact E8 AF D2 3C 00 call to LOCALIZATION_GetStringByKey for InventoryItemTooltipAppenderMove inside the legacy inventory tooltip appender. The hovered item is stable in R13. MassID 0.2.5 redirects only this five-byte call through the same R13 near relay as the legacy Drop appender.

entries.name: UI_LegacyInventoryTooltipAppenderMoveCallB
entries.notes: Exact E8 55 D2 3C 00 second call to LOCALIZATION_GetStringByKey for InventoryItemTooltipAppenderMove inside the legacy inventory tooltip appender. The hovered item remains stable in R13. MassID 0.2.5 redirects only this five-byte call through its R13 near relay.

entries.name: UI_LegacyInventoryTooltipAppenderDropCall
entries.notes: Exact E8 CE D1 3C 00 call to LOCALIZATION_GetStringByKey for InventoryItemTooltipAppenderDrop inside the legacy inventory tooltip appender. Its outer function receives the hovered item in R8 and preserves it in R13. MassID 0.1.5 redirects only this five-byte call through a near relay that passes R13 as the wrapper's second argument.

entries.name: UI_LegacyInventorySlotWidget_HandleClick
entries.notes: Keyboard/mouse inventory handler with ABI (widget, eventStateValue) -> void. It stores the second argument by value and passes the address of that stack copy to widget vtable +0xC8 at 0x228B2D, rejects mouse state 5 at 0x228AF0, tests Ctrl at 0x228BA3 and Shift at 0x228CA4, then dispatches the vanilla right-click through vtable +0xD0 at 0x228CED. The MassID 0.1.5 gameplay witness invalidated treating eventStateValue itself as a pointer; 0.1.6 reproduces the local-copy ABI. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_InventorySlotWidget_HandleClick
entries.notes: Modern inventory-slot click handler with ABI (widget, eventStateValue) -> void. It stores the second argument by value and passes the address of that stack copy to widget vtable +0xC8 at 0x2C7801, validates the slot at 0x2C756B, separates mouse state 5 from the right branch at 0x2C7614, tests Ctrl at 0x2C78CD and Shift at 0x2C7CEC, then calls 0x2AA9F0 or 0x15F660. MassID 0.1.6 hooks this entry together with 0x228AB0 so panel selection is no longer inferred from an indirect witness. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_ModernInventoryTooltipAppenderMoveCallA
entries.notes: Exact E8 4A F9 32 00 call to LOCALIZATION_GetStringByKey for InventoryItemTooltipAppenderMove inside the modern inventory tooltip appender. The hovered item is stable in R12. MassID 0.2.5 redirects only this five-byte call through a near relay that passes R12 as the wrapper's second argument.

entries.name: UI_ModernInventoryTooltipAppenderMoveCallB
entries.notes: Exact E8 FE F8 32 00 second call to LOCALIZATION_GetStringByKey for InventoryItemTooltipAppenderMove inside the modern inventory tooltip appender. The hovered item remains stable in R12. MassID 0.2.5 redirects only this five-byte call through its R12 near relay.

entries.name: UI_ModernInventoryTooltipAppenderMoveCallC
entries.notes: Exact E8 E0 F7 32 00 third call to LOCALIZATION_GetStringByKey for InventoryItemTooltipAppenderMove inside the modern inventory tooltip appender. The hovered item remains stable in R12. MassID 0.2.5 redirects only this five-byte call through its R12 near relay.

entries.name: UI_ModernInventoryTooltipAppenderDropCall
entries.notes: Exact E8 5E F6 32 00 call to LOCALIZATION_GetStringByKey for InventoryItemTooltipAppenderDrop inside the modern inventory tooltip appender. The hovered item is stable at [RBP-0x78]. MassID 0.1.5 redirects only this five-byte call through a near relay, complementing the legacy call at 0x2279BD without owning the global localization function or ITEMS_BuildItemTooltip.

entries.name: UI_AlternateInventoryTooltipAppenderMoveCall
entries.notes: Exact E8 AB A8 32 00 call to LOCALIZATION_GetStringByKey for InventoryItemTooltipAppenderMove inside the alternate inventory tooltip appender. The hovered item is stable in R13. MassID 0.2.5 redirects only this five-byte call through its R13 near relay.

entries.name: D2GAME_ITEMS_IdentifyStoredItem
entries.notes: Observed ABI (game, item, player) -> void. The function sets IFLAG_IDENTIFIED and performs the stored-item stat-list path when applicable, but does not itself send the complete item update or attach the vanilla identify sound. Its only direct caller at 0x4FD79D uses it during item creation before later placement and notification steps. MassID 0.1.0/0.1.1 used this partial helper and replaced it with the complete D2GAME_ITEMS_Identify path at 0x46E8C0 in 0.1.2.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_Rcv0x2E
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback in dispatch-table slot 0x2E with ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32 and an exact 0x15-byte size gate. It was incorrectly attributed to opcode 0x34 during MassID 0.1.0-0.2.3. The dispatch-table base is proven as 0x1D2A790 by RemoteStash's functional opcode 0x18 mapping to 0x4BFF30; 0x4AE280 is stored at 0x1D2A900, therefore index 0x2E.

entries.name: D2GAME_SHAREDSTASH_DepositHandler
entries.notes: Native shared-stash deposit handler. It resolves an auxiliary UNIT_PLAYER from the packet GUID, requires state 0xBA through STATES_CheckState, validates that auxiliary inventory's owner GUID against the requesting player, and confirms the proxy in the player's corpse registry. RemoteStash owns the inline hook; MassID does not hook this function.

entries.name: D2GAME_SHAREDSTASH_WithdrawalHandler
entries.notes: Native shared-stash withdrawal handler with the same auxiliary UNIT_PLAYER, state 0xBA, inventory-owner and corpse-registry validation chain as the deposit path. Its ITEMS_PlaceItemForPlayer call uses the auxiliary unit as the shared inventory holder. RemoteStash owns the inline hook; MassID only reuses the proven accessors.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_Rcv0x34_IdentifyItemsWithNpc
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback in dispatch-table slot 0x34 with ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32. It requires exactly 0x15 bytes and is stored at 0x1D2A930, which maps to opcode 0x34 from the table base 0x1D2A790. MassID 0.2.4 recognizes two private payload markers before this vanilla path and delegates every normal Cain request unchanged.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_TryDeductGold
entries.notes: Authoritative server helper with observed ABI (game, player, amount) -> int32. It returns zero without mutation when carried gold plus personal bank gold is insufficient; otherwise it debits carried gold first, then only the required remainder from the personal bank, and returns one. It reads stat ids 14 and 15, never the shared stash. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777 and D2GAME_NPC_RepairHandler calls it at 0x53FF7B.

entries.name: QUESTS_ConsumeCharsiImbueReward
entries.notes: Consumes Charsi's native imbue reward for the current difficulty with observed ABI (game, player) -> void. It resolves quest id 3 and uses the governed quest-flag set, clear and check helpers; BKVince's current infinite-reward patch suppresses two calls inside this routine. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: QUESTS_ConsumeAnyaPersonalizationReward
entries.notes: Consumes Anya's native personalization reward for the current difficulty with observed ABI (game, player) -> void. It resolves quest id 0x26 and uses the governed quest-flag set, clear and check helpers; BKVince's current infinite-reward patch suppresses two calls inside this routine. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: QUESTS_ConsumeLarzukSocketReward
entries.notes: Consumes Larzuk's native socket reward for the current difficulty with observed ABI (game, player) -> void. It resolves quest id 0x23 and uses the governed quest-flag set, clear and check helpers; BKVince's current infinite-reward patch suppresses its two authoritative callers. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: CLIENT_BuildNpcInteractionMenu
entries.notes: Builds the active NPC interaction menu from the native 72-byte-per-NPC action registry. For the Reset Stat/Skill Points entry identified by localized string id 11168, the branch at 0x114C14 reads current-difficulty quest 0x29 RewardGranted and RewardPending flags: a consumed reward is omitted, while a pending reward is added with the registered callback. This is a client visibility gate only; opcode 0x39 remains server-authoritative.

entries.name: CLIENT_NpcMenuAction_ResetStatsAndSkills
entries.notes: Affirmative callback for the native Reset Stat/Skill Points confirmation. It closes the modal, reads the current NPC GUID, and calls CLIENT_SendFiveByteNpcCommandPacket at 0x11311A with opcode 0x39 and that GUID. The action is registered for Akara by the 0x109200 initializer under localized string id 11168.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_Rcv0x39_ResetStatsAndSkillsWithNpc
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback with observed ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32. A controlled 92777 runtime read proved slot 0x39 of the server callback table at D2R+0x1D2A790 points here. It requires exactly five bytes, decodes the NPC GUID at +1, validates the interaction and NPC service record, and for Akara requires current-difficulty quest 0x29 RewardPending before calling D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetStatsAndSkills at 0x4B2A23. Native first-use bookkeeping follows through QUESTS_ConsumeAkaraRespecReward.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_Rcv0x3B_AllocateSkillPoints
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback with observed ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32. A controlled D2R 3.3.93847 runtime read proved slot 0x3B of the server callback table at D2R+0x1D2A790 points here. It requires exactly five bytes, decodes the skill id at +1 and additional-rank marker at +3, validates the id against the compiled SkillsTxt count, resolves the skill and its MaxLvl, reads the current base rank, then applies ranks through the native server mutation helper at 0x438670 until the request is exhausted or a validation/cap/mutation fails. The callback never reads SkillPage, SkillRow or SkillColumn, so authoritative allocation is independent of the UI page number.

entries.name: D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetStatsAndSkills
entries.notes: Native combined respec transaction with observed ABI (game, player) -> int32. Its only direct caller is the authoritative opcode 0x39 callback at 0x4B2A23. It resets and refunds invested skills through D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetSkills, resets base Strength/Energy/Dexterity/Vitality through D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetBaseStats, refreshes inventory and derived state, attaches the native sound, and returns one.

entries.name: D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetSkills
entries.notes: Iterates the player's class skill list, reads each invested base level, removes the skill ranks through the native reset/update path, sums the refunded ranks, and adds that total to stat id 5 (unspent skill points). D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetStatsAndSkills calls it first at 0x580F30.

entries.name: D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetBaseStats
entries.notes: Resets player base stat ids 0 through 3 to the class starting Strength, Energy, Dexterity and Vitality values, refunds the removed points into stat id 4, and routes the dependent life, mana and stamina recalculations through native helpers. D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetStatsAndSkills calls it at 0x580F3B.

entries.name: QUESTS_ConsumeAkaraRespecReward
entries.notes: Performs native post-respec bookkeeping for current-difficulty quest 0x29 with observed ABI (game, player) -> void. It sets RewardGranted, clears RewardPending and then evaluates an additional quest flag before the remaining quest-event path. The opcode 0x39 callback is its only direct caller and invokes it only when the NPC service record carries a nonzero quest field. Paid repeats must bypass this routine to preserve quest flags bit-exactly.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_HandleItemServiceTransaction
entries.notes: Shared authoritative server transaction for NPC item services with observed ABI (game, player, packetState, phaseFlag, context) -> int32. The native opcode 0x34 callback calls it at 0x4AE317 with phase 0; a native quest-bearing service consumes its reward and returns 4, causing a 0x30-byte job snapshot whose worker calls it again at 0x4B6087 with phase 1. It resolves a service record whose byte +0x0B selects Charsi Imbue (1), Larzuk Sockets (2), or Anya Personalization (4); byte +0x10 controls quest availability, worker scheduling and later reward-consumption calls. Clearing +0x10 makes the repeat remain synchronous in phase 0. Its strict 23-byte prologue is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_Rcv0x38_NpcItemServiceDialog
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback with observed ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32 for the nine-byte NPC item-service dialog request. It resolves the interacting NPC service record at 0x4A9A5A. A repeat-only call-local record whose quest byte +0x10 is cleared follows the ordinary service-menu action path and skips the native quest-event branch; first rewards retain the original record. Its strict 24-byte prologue is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: NpcItemServiceDialogRecordResolveCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte call to the NPC service-record resolver inside opcode 0x38. RepeatableServices wraps only this invocation, validates a consumed current-difficulty reward and selector 1, 2 or 4, then returns a 17-byte thread-local copy with quest byte +0x10 cleared. Native, pending and unrelated services delegate the original pointer unchanged.

entries.name: AkaraRespecServiceRecordResolveCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte call to the NPC service-record resolver inside opcode 0x39. Returning a repeat-only 17-byte local copy with quest byte +0x10 cleared bypasses RewardPending and native reward-consumption bookkeeping only after Akara quest 0x29 is already consumed; the first reward keeps the original record.

entries.name: NpcItemServiceTransactionRecordResolveCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte record-resolver call in the shared Charsi, Larzuk and Anya server transaction. Its result is stored immediately before NpcItemServiceQuestAvailabilityGate at 0x4FC5EC. A repeat-only local record copy with byte +0x10 cleared keeps the transaction synchronous in phase zero and suppresses all three native reward-consumption paths without mutating global records.

entries.name: NpcItemServiceFinalValidatorCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte call to the final common packet and inventory-state validator at 0x472590. It immediately precedes one shared service dispatch path, but repeated Larzuk may bypass this call through 0x4FD3E3 -> 0x4FD446. RepeatableServices may debit here after a successful early affordability preflight; a second guarded debit at the universal dispatch remains necessary for the direct Larzuk path. Runtime 0.1.7 proved that returning false here and entering the late cleanup at 0x4FD419 can erase the submitted item and strand the Add Sockets UI, so that branch is forbidden for repeat-service payment refusal.

entries.name: AkaraResetStatsAndSkillsCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte call from the authoritative opcode 0x39 callback to D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetStatsAndSkills after every native NPC, packet and quest-state validation. RepeatableServices performs an authoritative affordability preflight before virtualizing the consumed Akara record, then debits immediately before this mutation. A late debit anomaly is fail-open for the service and logged critically rather than risking a partially accepted transaction.

entries.name: NpcActionQuestSetCheckCall
entries.notes: First of two five-byte client QuestFlagCheck calls in the 24-byte NPC action-registration loop. For entries whose table predicate expects a set quest flag, a nonzero result invokes the entry callback. Runtime proved Larzuk's Add Sockets callback is present while quest 0x23 RewardPending is set and disappears after the native reward is consumed. RepeatableServices may report RewardPending set only when the same quest is already RewardGranted, the service is enabled, and the real RewardPending flag is clear. The pinned PluginPack commit dc75b49 does not own this site.

entries.name: NpcActionQuestClearCheckCall
entries.notes: Second five-byte client QuestFlagCheck call in the shared NPC action-registration loop, used by table predicates that expect a clear flag. It shares the same ABI (flags, quest, flag) -> int32 and wrapper as 0x114346; the wrapper changes only consumed RewardPending checks for configured Charsi quest 3, Larzuk quest 0x23, and Anya personalization quest 0x26, leaving all other NPC actions and incomplete or pending rewards native. The pinned PluginPack commit dc75b49 does not own this site.

entries.name: NpcMenuAkaraRewardGrantedCheckCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte client QuestFlagCheck call for RewardGranted inside Akara's menu visibility gate. For an enabled repeat and an already consumed quest 0x29 only, a wrapper reports RewardGranted clear so the action may continue; pending and incomplete native states delegate unchanged.

entries.name: NpcMenuAkaraRewardPendingCheckCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte client QuestFlagCheck call for RewardPending inside Akara's menu visibility gate. For an enabled repeat and an already consumed quest 0x29 only, a wrapper reports RewardPending set so the native Reset Stat/Skill Points action is added; the server opcode 0x39 callback remains authoritative.

entries.name: NpcMenuLocalizedActionLabelCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte call to LANG_GetStringById for the registered NPC action. The function returns UTF-8 char* and the text is copied immediately into a 0x200-byte local buffer. Runtime 0.1.1 proved that Larzuk's repeat action could be restored while a wrapper installed at this site still produced the vanilla label, so this callsite is not retained as the final decoration seam. The narrower effective seam is the final generic UI_AddNpcMenuEntry call at 0x114D4D; the server remains authoritative for price calculation.

entries.name: UI_AddNpcMenuEntry
entries.notes: Adds one UTF-8 text action to an NPC interaction menu with observed x64 ABI (menu, const char* label, style, enabled, callback, closeOnSelect) -> entry result. The generic CLIENT_BuildNpcInteractionMenu path calls it at 0x114D4D after every intermediate string resolution and formatting branch. Its extended 32-byte prologue is unique in build 92777. RepeatableServices wraps only the generic callsite, not this shared function entry. Runtime 0.1.2 rejected the incorrect wchar_t prototype because no service label comparison could match.

entries.name: NpcMenuGenericActionAddEntryCall
entries.notes: Unique five-byte call E8 DE 42 0D 00 to UI_AddNpcMenuEntry after the current registered NPC action label has been copied into the builder's 0x200-byte local buffer. RepeatableServices decorates only labels matching Imbue, Respec, Add Sockets or Personalize and only when the quest-gate decision identifies a consumed repeat. Runtime disproved the attempted 0.1.8 disabled-entry presentation: UI_AddNpcMenuEntry still exposed a selectable action and rendered the control prefix literally. Version 0.1.9 therefore leaves the native enabled state untouched, displays only the configured price and uses this seam to remember which item service panel is being offered. The pinned PluginPack commit dc75b49 owns neither this site nor 0x114CDC.

entries.name: ClientItemServiceSlotToggle
entries.notes: Shared client handler for placing or removing an item in the Charsi, Larzuk and Anya service panel, with observed x64 ABI (item) -> uint8. It reads the panel state at D2R.exe+0x2A96964: state 1 validates the item then writes state 2 and the item GUID, while state 2 writes state 1 and clears the GUID. Every native validation rejection returns zero before the 1-to-2 capture transition, so a hook can refuse a deposit without removing the item from the cursor or entering the server transaction. Version 0.1.9 returns zero only for a paid repeat whose synchronized carried plus personal-stash gold is below the displayed price; removal, native rewards, free services and unrelated panels delegate unchanged. Its strict 24-byte prologue is unique in build 92777, and the pinned PluginPack commit dc75b49 does not own this entry.

entries.name: NpcItemServiceQuestAvailabilityGate
entries.notes: Stores the resolved NPC item-service record, then reads its byte +0x10. Zero bypasses the native quest-availability test, worker scheduling and later Charsi/Larzuk/Anya reward-consumption calls; nonzero is range-checked and converted to a quest-state index with LEA EDX,[RDI-1] at 0x4FC7E5 before QUESTRECORD_GetQuestState. The record byte is therefore a one-based internal field, not a stable service identity. Every later reload reads only selector +0x0B or quest byte +0x10, so a 17-byte call-local copy is sufficient and never crosses into the worker. Its strict 19-byte signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: NpcItemServicePostValidationDispatch
entries.notes: Universal authoritative selector-dispatch seam reached after service-specific eligibility and packet/inventory-state validation but before any Anya, Larzuk or Charsi mutation. Runtime 0.1.4 proved that repeated Larzuk follows the direct 0x4FD3E3 -> 0x4FD446 branch and bypasses the validator call at 0x4FD410. Runtime 0.1.6 then disproved 0x4FD442 as universal: patching there left the direct Larzuk target inside displaced bytes and caused an access violation exactly at 0x4FD446. Both incoming paths have a valid service-record pointer in RAX at 0x4FD446, after loads at 0x4FD3D6 or 0x4FD442. Its strict 18-byte signature is unique in build 92777. RepeatableServices replaces the seven-byte selector-load/first-subtraction sequence with a register-preserving near relay. Runtime 0.1.7 proved the nominal Larzuk debit but also proved that branching from this late seam to 0x4FD419 on insufficient funds erases the submitted item and freezes the UI. Version 0.1.8 therefore rejects affordability before record virtualization and makes this relay continuation-only: it charges once when still needed, reproduces the displaced instructions and always resumes at 0x4FD44D; a post-preflight debit anomaly completes without charge and logs a critical error.

entries.name: NpcMenuAkaraQuestVisibilityGate
entries.notes: Unique current-difficulty quest-flag gate for Akara's localized action id 11168 inside CLIENT_BuildNpcInteractionMenu. It rejects RewardGranted and normally requires RewardPending before the generic label/add-entry path. Paid or free repeats must bypass this gate only after the native reward is consumed; the first pending reward remains vanilla. Its strict 21-byte signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: NpcMenuLocalizedActionLabelResolve
entries.notes: Loads the uint16 string id for the current registered NPC action and calls LANG_GetStringById at 0x114CDC.
