entries.notes: Exact unique first reader sequence in function 0x530930..0x530BD3: reads a 9-bit ItemStatCost ID, then compares it with signed terminator 0x1FF. ISC12 prepares byte offsets +1 and +19 for 12-bit/0xFFF without publishing them.

entries.name: PLAYERSTATS_AuxSectionMarker
entries.notes: Exact unique G2 marker/bounds window requires 0x6667 before the first auxiliary ItemStatCost ID and anchors the prepared strict preflight.

entries.name: PLAYERSTATS_AuxNextStatIdCodec
entries.notes: Exact unique auxiliary loop reader sequence paired with 0x530A99; the back-edge re-enters stat value decoding only while the signed ID remains below the terminator.

entries.name: PLAYERSTATS_AuxStatIdWriter
entries.notes: Exact unique auxiliary writer sequence passes ItemStatCost ID in EDX and width 9 in R8D to the native bit writer; paired atomically with terminator site 0x534139 and both auxiliary readers.

entries.name: PLAYERSTATS_AuxStatIdTerminatorWriter
entries.notes: Exact unique combined sequence writes terminator 0x1FF with width 9. ISC12 prepares offsets +2 and +12 for 0xFFF/12 as part of G2 only.

entries.name: PLAYERSTATS_ModernFirstStatIdCodec
entries.notes: Exact unique first ItemStatCost ID reader in the modern regular player-stat section, including width read and signed terminator comparison.

entries.name: PLAYERSTATS_ModernSectionMarker
entries.notes: Exact unique G3 marker/bounds window requires 0x6667 before the first regular player-stat ItemStatCost ID and anchors the prepared strict preflight.

entries.name: PLAYERSTATS_ModernNextStatIdCodec
entries.notes: Exact unique modern player-stat loop reader paired with 0x53395E and regular writer group G3.

entries.name: PLAYERSTATS_ModernStatIdWriter
entries.notes: Exact unique regular player-stat writer passes ItemStatCost ID in EDX and width 9 in R8D; prepared offset +2 changes only the width immediate. The CALL is never rewritten: runtime may use the native target directly or an exactly attested D2RCore WritePlayerSaveStatId provider whose 1.1/1.2 body, PDATA, unwind and live slot all forward to D2R+0xA1B710.

entries.name: PLAYERSTATS_ModernStatIdTerminatorWriter

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9CPreparationWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 31-byte sequence saves the current ItemData+0x18 flags and applies the 0x9C caller mask before the real serializer. Together with the restore calls after serialization, it proves that a scratch serialization at function entry is not byte-equivalent by construction.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9DPreparationWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 64-byte sequence saves and applies ItemData+0x18 flags, inspects ItemData+0x54 and conditionally prepares that byte before the real 0x9D serializer. It proves that the staging design must preserve the native producer's preparation path rather than double-serialize at entry.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9CBeforeQueueWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 139-byte prefix proves recursion R9D=0, serializer capacity 0xF4, header increment 8, diagnostic comparison 0xFC, item-state restoration and queue arguments for one 0x9C root node. It ends immediately before the mutable range [0x479E10,0x479E15); the safe native payload ceiling is 244 bytes.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9CAfterQueueWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 14-byte continuation reloads temporary flags, item and client from nonvolatile state and calls the socketed-item walker 0x481B50. It is disjoint from the mutable 0x9C queue CALL.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9CEpilogueCodeWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 30-byte code witness [0x479E23,0x479E41) loads/xors/checks the stack cookie, deallocates 0x160 bytes, restores nonvolatile registers and includes RET. It proves code bytes only: static .pdata is non-authoritative for the future entry wrapper, whose unwind contract still requires live RtlLookupFunctionEntry validation.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9DBeforeQueueWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 139-byte prefix proves recursion R9D=0, serializer capacity 0xF4, header increment 13, diagnostic comparison 0xFC, item-state restoration and queue arguments for one 0x9D node. It ends immediately before the mutable range [0x47A001,0x47A006); the safe native payload ceiling is 239 bytes.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9DAfterQueueWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 19-byte continuation reloads the parent temporary flags, item and client and calls the socketed-item walker 0x481B50. The walker derives each child value as parentTemporaryFlags | 0x08 before invoking 0x9D. This continuation is disjoint from the mutable 0x9D queue CALL.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9DEpilogueCodeWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 30-byte code witness [0x47A019,0x47A037) loads/xors/checks the stack cookie, deallocates 0x170 bytes, restores nonvolatile registers and includes RET. It proves code bytes only: static .pdata is non-authoritative for the future entry wrapper, whose unwind contract still requires live RtlLookupFunctionEntry validation.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemOverflowZeroWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique interior epilogue returns zero when the bit-writer overflow flag is set. Item-action producers still queue their 8/13-byte header after this return, so G9-A must reject the complete item tree before the first queue rather than relying on this late signal.

entries.name: CLIENT_ItemAction9CPayloadBoundWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique interior window reads the one-byte 0x9C packet length, subtracts the 8-byte header and rejects payload above 0xF4. It is an interior native witness and requires no claim on the dispatcher entry.

entries.name: CLIENT_ItemAction9DBufferHeaderWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique interior window proves a 0x101-byte local buffer and minimum packet length 13, but does not prove a client-side 0xFC maximum or require a claim on the dispatcher entry.

entries.name: D2GAME_QueueServerPacketSpanDispatchWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 39-byte interior sequence builds packet+length and synchronously dispatches the [packet, packet+length] span through the client sink. This proves each G9-A relay must copy producer stack packets before returning. Runtime qualification proves ordered three-packet flush, overflow zero-callback and flush reentry containment. Because the queue ABI returns void, failure after the first real call cannot be rolled back and is terminal rather than transactionally recoverable.

entries.name: D2GAME_SocketedItemSeparate9DWalkerWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 102-byte inventory-walk window calls INVENTORY_GetFirstItem, checks the result, derives child temporary flags as parentTemporaryFlags | 0x08, sends the child through D2GAME_SendItemAction9D at 0x481BFE with action 0x12 and gamble zero, calls INVENTORY_GetNextItem and branches back to the same send path while one remains. Because each 0x9D producer captures its node then recursively invokes this walker before returning to the parent's GetNextItem, the native sequence is depth-first preorder. The G9-A transaction models and now runtime-qualifies this order and nesting on a real three-node socket tree; pre-flush rejection is all-or-none.

entries.name: DATATBLS_BBEConditionCalcCompilerWiring

The captured 16-byte window 73746174000000000000000073657466 has SHA-256 83626D991B1A0AD789DDB50D993623989AB1C1257879530005CEE0CA411F0E4F.

The table contains nine 16-byte records {callback VA qword, arity dword, zero padding dword}; callback RVAs are 0x3B3200, 0x3B3210, 0x3B3220, 0x3B32F0, 0x3B33A0, 0x3B33F0, 0x3B3500, 0x3B3590 and 0x3B3640. entries.name: DATATBLS_BBEItemStatCostOrdinalResolverWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique branch loads the authoritative ItemStatCost linker at DataTables+0x1270, resolves the named operand through 0xA121F0 and stores EAX as a full DWORD. No 0x1FF mask or narrow store occurs.

entries.notes: Exact unique generic-compiler branch limits callback-constant token 4 to signed values -128..127 and routes wider values to the 16-bit test.

entries.name: DATATBLS_BBEWideStatAccessorCallback
entries.notes: Exact unique function body copies EDX to full-width EDI, checks DataTables+0x1260 and forwards the same DWORD ordinal to the base, item-value or total-stat accessor. A governed read-only D2R 3.3.93847 capture proves callback-table record 5 at 0x1D09CA0 points here with arity 2, closing native stat-slot membership.

entries.name: SKILLS_BBEEvaluatorCallbackTableWiringWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique callsite passes callback table 0x1D09C50 with count 9 to generic evaluator 0xA234B0. Seven D2R table-wired evaluator xrefs use the same table/count; an eighth generic call passes no callback table. A governed read-only D2R 3.3.93847 capture proves the table is nine 16-byte records and that record 5 contains callback RVA 0x3B33F0 with arity 2.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_BuildRoomAndActiveRoom
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (uint8 dataContext, DrlgRoom*) -> void. The strict pipeline witness at +0x0F conditionally calls 0x3608A0, calls static grid initializer 0x3F38D0 and static map-tile builder 0x3F3930, then separately calls ActiveRoom allocator 0x326480. MapSense 0.13.21 fingerprints this control flow but deliberately calls only the static phases for distant POI descriptors.

entries.name: ACTIVEROOM_AllocateForDrlgRoom
entries.notes: ActiveRoom allocator called only after DRLGROOM_BuildRoomAndActiveRoom has completed the static room phases. MapSense 0.13.21 uses this RVA only as a negative control-flow witness and never resolves or calls it from passive distant-name capture.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_BuildNearRoomLinks
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (uint8 dataContext, DrlgRoom*) -> void. DRLGROOM_BuildRoomAndActiveRoom calls it only when the room's near-room vector state at +0x18 is zero; the function first delegates to the governed near-room-vector builder at 0x3614C0 and completes static room-link preparation.

entries.name: DRLGPRESET_AddPresetUnitDescriptors
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (uint8 dataContext, DrlgRoom*) -> void. DRLGROOM_CreateActiveRoom calls it for room type 2 when DrlgRoom flag bit 25 is clear. It materializes static PresetUnit descriptors used by exact waypoint discovery; MapSense never traverses or creates gameplay Unit or monster instances in this path.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_InitializeStaticRoomGrids
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (uint8 dataContext, DrlgRoom*) -> void. This is the first unconditional static phase in DRLGROOM_BuildRoomAndActiveRoom and precedes both static map-tile generation and the separate ActiveRoom allocation.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_AddStaticMapTiles
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (uint8 dataContext, DrlgRoom*) -> void. Dispatches by room type, creates static map-tile/RoomTile state and sets DrlgRoom HAS_ROOM bit 20. It returns before ActiveRoom allocation, allowing MapSense 0.13.21 to copy exact exit and waypoint descriptors without loading live room units.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_LoadTileLibraries
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (uint8 dataContext, DrlgRoom*) -> void. DRLGROOM_CreateActiveRoom calls it only when DrlgRoom flag bit 24 is clear; completion sets that tile-library-loaded bit before preset and static-room phases.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_ReleaseRoomData
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (DrlgRoom*, int32 keepRoom) -> void. With keepRoom=0 it clears DrlgRoom+0x58, tests and clears HAS_ROOM bit 20, and releases transient static room grids while retaining the lightweight descriptor chains required by normal DRLG lifecycle. MapSense calls it only for a static lease it created and only while +0x58 remains null.

entries.name: DRLG_SeedInitializationWitness
entries.notes: Strict 129-byte interior witness in the governed DRLG allocation path. It initializes the native seed pair as {mapSeed, 0x29A}, advances the 64-bit LCG with multiplier 0x6AC690C5, stores the original mapSeed at Drlg+0x840 and the low 32-bit result at Drlg+0x860. MapSense 0.13.22 reads both fields and accepts an external label-atlas request only when the pair satisfies this exact native relation; build names remain diagnostic only.

entries.name: NET_SendFixedStatPacket1D1F
entries.notes: Builds packet 0x1D, 0x1E or 0x1F according to the value width. Every stat-identifier field is stored as a WORD, including the R9W field in all three layouts; no ISC12 byte-to-word packet expansion is required.

entries.name: NET_SendPrivateStatPacket9EA0
entries.notes: Builds the 0x9E/0x9F/0xA0 private-stat packet family and stores the stat identifier from R8W in both compact layouts. The governed consumer switch at 0x12B070 reads the paired field with MOVZX WORD.

entries.name: NET_SendPrivateStatPacketA1A2
entries.notes: Builds the 0xA1/0xA2 private-stat packet family and stores the stat identifier from R8W in both compact layouts. The governed consumer switch at 0x12B070 preserves the complete WORD field.

entries.name: NET_SendStatPacket20
entries.notes: Builds the fixed 13-byte packet 0x20 layout: opcode byte +0, stat ID WORD +1 from R9W, layer WORD +3, unit GUID DWORD +5 and value DWORD +9. Consumer 0x12B5A0 reads the same WORD stat and layer fields.

entries.name: MercenaryPrivateUpdateWordStatWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique dispatcher window zero-extends the queued stat identifier from WORD [RBX+0x14] before calling the 0x9E producer; the sibling 0xA2 branch repeats the WORD load at 0x53AA19. This closes the upstream uint8-stat suspicion without a mutation.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetAutoStack
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (item) -> int32. Resolves the concrete item's ItemTypesTxt record and returns its AutoStack byte at +0x13. Potion Auto Pickup 2.0.0 overrides only configured potion calls after its compiled ItemsTxt mutations are ready.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetMinStack
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (item) -> int32. Resolves the compiled ItemsTxt row and returns the minstack DWORD at +0xEC.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetSpawnStack
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (item) -> int32. Resolves the compiled ItemsTxt row and returns the spawnstack DWORD at +0xF4. Together with minstack=1, Potion Auto Pickup uses this field to keep each generated ground potion equal to one bottle.

entries.name: ITEMS_CheckIfAutoBeltable
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (inventory, item) -> int32. Reads compiled ItemsTxt autobelt at +0x141 and falls back to the native inventory/item eligibility helper. The authoritative pickup path calls it at 0x471C06 before asking for a free belt slot.

entries.name: INVENTORY_FindBackPackItemForStack
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (inventory, item, excludedItem) -> item pointer. Searches the backpack grid for an exact native stack-compatible item whose STAT_QUANTITY is below ITEMS_GetTotalMaxStack. Potion Auto Pickup redirects only its scoped pickup to a chosen belt stack or suppresses backpack merging until an empty belt row is tried.

entries.name: D2GAME_StackItemIntoInventory
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (game, player, item) -> bool. Finds native-compatible partial stacks, transfers STAT_QUANTITY up to ITEMS_GetTotalMaxStack, synchronizes source and destination packets, and repeats until the source is empty or no destination remains.

entries.name: D2GAME_TryAutoStackPickedItem
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (game, player, item) -> bool. Handles book and ammunition families first, then gates the generic path through ITEMS_CheckIfStackable and ITEMS_GetAutoStack before calling D2GAME_StackItemIntoInventory. The pickup caller removes the ground unit only when this routine reports complete handling.

entries.name: D2GAME_ExecuteItemUseEffect
entries.notes: Observed Windows x64 ABI (game, player, item, target) -> void, continuous body 0x581680..0x5817E4. Dispatches the ItemsTxt use callback at 0x58178D, tests its true boolean AL at 0x581795 and decrements quantity itself only for Book type 0x12. The sole direct caller returns at 0x4F5923 and conditionally deletes according to packet byte +1, but that byte also governed the earlier state batch: changing it after the effect is not a valid retention strategy. September 5 development source wraps this dispatcher in a nested TLS observation scope, observes the actual callback and uses a shared pre-batch removal predicate. Confirmed successful multi-bottle use debits through 0x46F090 only when quantity is unchanged; last-bottle removal stays native. Static and local ABI tests only; not deployed or gameplay-qualified.

entries.name: ITEMS_ShouldRemoveOnUse
entries.notes: Observed ABI bool(item), return AL, continuous body 0x308E80..0x308F77. Book type 0x12 returns false; other items resolve their use descriptor and return true when its byte +8 is zero. Eleven direct callers include inventory/belt request construction at 0x1C7BD7/0x1C7C8E and authoritative opcode 0x26 validation at 0x4F4196. The latter compares AL with parsed packet byte +1 before preparing the state batch. The Potion development hook calls the original and changes true to false only for a managed ordinary known quantity above one; zero, unavailable, advanced-stash payload and last bottle delegate unchanged. Unique strict 32-byte entry signature, five-byte SDK-owned inline hook; unqualified in game.

entries.name: CLIENT_SendUseItemPacket26
entries.notes: Continuous body 0xED1E0..0xED2E1 constructs the 36-byte opcode 0x26 packet. The first argument CL is the removal flag stored at packet +1. Three belt-followup entries default to FF/0/0. At 0xED26E a 23-byte unique witness gates their copying on that flag and R8d mode == 2; false removal therefore does not request a belt-row collapse. Client calls at 0x1C7C11 and 0x1C7CDB receive the shared removal predicate result. No hook or packet mutation is installed here. The remaining packet ABI is not exposed as a callable plugin contract.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemUseEffectCallbackCall
entries.notes: CALL R9 (41 FF D1), followed by MOV R14,[RSP+0x58] (4C 8B 74 24 58) then TEST AL at 0x581795. Actual callback ABI bool(game RCX, player RDX, effectTarget R8); R8 is the item when spellicon == FF and otherwise the target. The 31-byte unique witness at 0x581778 covers argument selection, callback load, call, restore and AL test. Development observer owns exactly eight bytes: CALL rel32 plus three explicit NOPs, transactionally written by SDK PatchBytes. A 19-byte leaf relay restores R14 from [RSP+0x60] accounting for the new return address, then tail-jumps to a C++ four-argument observer with the original callback still in R9. No hook at the 0x4F40C0 Transmogrify-owned entry and no modification of the Infinite Quantities Book debit at 0x5817BD. Local x64 synthetic-call ABI test passes; native gameplay remains unqualified.

entries.name: MONSTERMODE_DeathModeCallback
entries.notes: Unique 48-byte entry signature with observed Windows x64 ABI int32(game, modeChange); modeChange+0x08 is the dying Unit. The routine performs the complete native death transition and conditionally enters the MonStats deathDmg corpse-explosion route. Its PDATA fragment does not describe reliable logical bounds and is not used as an ABI gate. Doll Explosion owns this entry exclusively, calls the original exactly once and runs custom work only after a successful return.

entries.name: MONSTERMODE_DeathDamageGuardWitness
entries.notes: Unique 58-byte interior witness in the death callback. It reads Game+0x106 as the data context, resolves the MonStats row by class and tests byte +0x3E for the deathDmg bit before entering the native corpse-explosion branch. A clear bit jumps past that entire route, proving that classic BKVince Dolls with blank deathDmg never reach the later missile-117 callsite.

entries.name: MONSTERMODE_CorpseExplosionMissileCallWitness
entries.notes: Unique 79-byte call context for CreateSkillMissile at 0x44535F. It passes game, missile ID 117, dying monster owner, skill 0, level 1, next game counter, zero origin offsets, captured X/Y and check 1. A null result skips the native area-damage branch. Doll Explosion fingerprints this semantic witness but does not hook it because deathDmg-blank targets are gated out earlier.

entries.name: MISSILES_CreateSkillMissile
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature with observed 11-position Windows x64 ABI (game, missileId, owner, skillId, skillLevel, nextGameCounter, originX, originY, targetX, targetY, check) -> missile Unit*. The index contains 24 direct calls, including the governed monster corpse-explosion call at 0x44535F. Doll Explosion borrows this helper only after validating its exact entry and caller-layout witnesses.

entries.name: MISSILES_GenericServerCallback
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature with observed Windows x64 ABI int32(game, missile). It has exactly two native xrefs: the pSrvDo=1 basic-handler tail jump at 0x45584C and call 0x457B44. Doll Explosion owns the entry exclusively, delegates foreign missiles exactly, calls the original before inspecting its result and consumes a matched delay sidecar only when the original returns 2.

entries.name: MISSILES_ServerDoBasic
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature for the native pSrvDo selector 1 handler. It resolves the context-aware Missiles row, performs basic missile work and tail-jumps to MISSILES_GenericServerCallback at 0x45584C. Doll Explosion does not hook this helper; it requires the live pSrvDo table entry 1 to keep resolving this exact address.

entries.name: MISSILES_ServerDoDispatcher
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature for the server missile-do dispatcher. It resolves the context-aware Missiles row, reads signed WORD pSrvDo at +0x2C, calls the indexed function table and removes the missile through the native lifecycle path when that callback returns 2. Doll Explosion fingerprints this dispatcher without modifying it.

entries.name: MISSILES_ServerDoTableCallWitness
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte dispatcher witness. It sign-extends MissilesTxt+0x2C, indexes the native function table at 0x2380E80, invokes ABI int32(game, missile), compares EAX with 2 and enters the governed native removal branch on equality. This closes the delayed-carrier expiration handoff.

entries.name: MISSILES_ServerDoFunctionTable
entries.notes: Native pSrvDo function-pointer table base referenced by the unique dispatcher callsite at 0x466E46. Selector 1 is expected to resolve D2R+0x455750 at runtime. Doll Explosion treats the live pointer relation as an additional fail-closed layout witness rather than authorizing by build name or channel.

entries.name: MONSTERMODE_CorpseExplosionDamageInitWitness
entries.notes: Unique 64-byte interior witness for the native corpse-explosion D2Damage initialization. It writes physical damage to record +0x18 and initializes the inline container pointer, size and capacity marker at +0x40/+0x48/+0x50. Doll Explosion reproduces the governed 0x180-byte record layout and calls the native destructor.

entries.name: MONSTERMODE_CorpseExplosionAreaDamageCallWitness
entries.notes: Unique 80-byte call context closing the native area-damage contract: (game, missile, x, y, radius, D2Damage*, 0, 0, null, 0x581). It also witnesses the D2Damage owned-subobject sentinel at +0x158 and surrounding zero-initialization before the direct 0x44A120 call.

entries.name: MISSILES_CurrentFrameLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Unique 64-byte missile-timing witness. It dereferences Unit+0x10 as MissileData, reads signed WORD total frames at MissileData+0x10 and reads the floating current-frame countdown at +0x14. The governed getter divides that float by 40 before truncation. Doll Explosion changes total and current frames together through exact native setters and verifies both through exact native getters.

entries.name: MISSILES_TotalFramesLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Unique 48-byte independent witness that validates unit type 3, dereferences Unit+0x10 as MissileData and reads the signed WORD total-frame field at +0x10. This independently closes the configurable delay width at 0..32767 frames.

entries.name: MISSILES_ApplyAreaDamage
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature with five direct callers. The governed corpse-explosion caller establishes ABI int32(game, sourceMissile, x, y, radius, D2Damage*, int32, int32, callback, flags). The routine resolves missile ownership, enumerates targets and deep-copies the supplied D2Damage before native missile-damage application.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetMissilesTxtRecordForContext
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature with observed Windows x64 ABI (uint8 dataContext, int32 missileId) -> compiled MissilesTxt record pointer. The server dispatcher and generic missile callback call it after reading Game+0x106. Doll Explosion uses it to require pSrvDo WORD +0x2C equal 1 and pSrvHit WORD +0x2E equal 0 for missile IDs 117 and 587.

entries.name: GAME_NextGameCounter
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature with observed Windows x64 ABI (game) -> int32. It advances or derives the per-game counter passed as the sixth argument to CreateSkillMissile. The native monster corpse-explosion route calls it immediately before constructing missile 117; Doll Explosion reuses the same helper for visual and delay-carrier creation.

entries.name: MISSILES_GetCurrentFrame
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature with observed Windows x64 ABI (missile Unit*) -> int32. It validates unit type 3, dereferences MissileData through Unit+0x10, divides the float at MissileData+0x14 by 40 and truncates the result. The generic callback reads this countdown, subtracts one, writes it back and enters terminal handling at zero.

entries.name: MISSILES_GetTotalFrames
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature with observed Windows x64 ABI (missile Unit*) -> int32. It validates unit type 3, dereferences MissileData through Unit+0x10 and sign-extends the total-frame WORD at MissileData+0x10. Doll Explosion uses it to verify the native carrier range and the configured replacement.

entries.name: MISSILES_SetCurrentFrame
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature with observed Windows x64 ABI (missile Unit*, int32 frames) -> void. It validates unit type 3 and MissileData, multiplies the accepted frame count by 40, converts it to float and stores it at MissileData+0x14. The generic callback invokes it after decrementing the current-frame countdown.

entries.name: MISSILES_SetTotalFrames
entries.notes: Unique 32-byte entry signature with observed Windows x64 ABI (missile Unit*, int32 frames) -> void. It validates unit type 3 and MissileData, bounds the input to the signed 16-bit domain and stores the total-frame WORD at MissileData+0x10. Native missile construction calls it immediately before MISSILES_SetCurrentFrame with the same computed range.
